findings.claim: None of the 72 cells (our 36 strategies at 15m and at 30m) shows a positive every-signal result that survives multiple testing. Averaged over all 36 strategies, the every-signal result is negative at both timeframes, and the 95% interval stays below zero.
findings.evidence: Every SUBMITTED signal run alone through the house exits: v3a = entered trades + nightly skipped shadows converted to R; v3b and v4 = replay. Pooled 15m: n 2,523, mean -0.235R, 4h-cluster bootstrap CI -0.370..-0.081, win 53.0%. Pooled 30m: n 1,115, mean -0.205R, CI -0.291..-0.111, win 58.6%. Positive cells after BH: 0 of 52 testable. Negative cells after BH (q<0.05): 13. Cells with n>=20: 35 of 41 have a negative mean, 15 have a CI entirely below 0, 0 have a CI entirely above 0. Sources: pooled_15_30.csv, cards_15_30.csv, summary_stats.txt (scripts cards.py, summary_stats.py).
findings.implication: With the house exits, the 15m/30m rule signals lose money. An AI trader on any of them starts from a negative base and has to create the edge itself, through which trades it takes and how it exits. Choosing the strategy does not hand it an edge.

verification.recomputed: Rebuilt every-signal rows on my own. For v3a I took entered trades from the raw trades.csv (R = pnl/(qty*|entry-stop_initial|)) and converted the d3 'skipped' shadow ROE to R with my own tier-walk sizing. That sizing matched the recorded fresh-account leverage on 1,510 of 1,510 base rows. For v3b/v4 I used the TRADED rows of replay_signals (R recomputed, max diff 4e-13). Results: 15m n 2,523, mean -0.2355, win 53.0%, 4h-cluster bootstrap CI [-0.370,-0.084]. 30m n 1,115, mean -0.2047, win 58.6%, CI [-0.289,-0.115]. BH over 52 testable cells: 0 positive, 13 negative. n>=20: 41 cells, 35 negative, 15 with hi<0, 0 with lo>0. Current-rule runs only (v3b+v4): 15m -0.130 [-0.346,+0.154], 30m -0.154 [-0.283,+0.001]. KST-day clusters with a t on 7 df, all runs: 15m [-0.50,+0.03], 30m [-0.33,-0.08]. Scripts: verify/v3a_build.py, es_rows.py, pooled.py, ct2.py, cells.py.
verification.note: Every number reproduces. The claim that the 95% interval stays below zero holds only for all runs pooled with 4h clusters. The 15m negativity is driven by v3a (-0.32R at mostly 50x tier walk) against v4 (-0.03R). Under the leverage rule now in use (v3b+v4) the 15m interval includes zero and the 30m upper bound is at zero. With day clusters the all-runs 15m interval also crosses zero. The count of 13 BH-negative cells is robust, but which cells they are is not: about 5 of the 13 change between their shifted bootstrap and my percentile bootstrap (for example N20_EMA9_CHOP@15m: q 0.010 vs 0.055). Per-cell power is low (CI half-widths of 0.2-0.6R), so 'no cell survives' says little about any single cell. The strong evidence is the pooled result together with the 5-year data.

findings.claim: Live matches the 5-year backtest. The 5-year every-signal result is negative in 69 of the 70 cells that had signals. In both live and 5-year data the loss per trade is about the round-trip cost: gross directional edge is roughly zero.
findings.evidence: 5-year (fiveyear_ref, profiles_binance): 69/70 cells have mean net return per notional below 0, 65 have t < -2, and 67 are negative in both the IS and CF windows. Median net per notional: 5-year -0.141% vs live every-signal -0.149% (41 cells with n>=20). Median 5-year gross per notional (net + 0.14% round trip): -0.002%. Live later runs (v3b+v4), gross R before fees and slippage: 15m +0.102R (CI -0.115..+0.393), 30m +0.008R (CI -0.117..+0.165). Fees+funding: 0.165R (15m) and 0.116R (30m). Slippage: 0.066R and 0.046R. Net: -0.130R and -0.154R. Signal generation is faithful: live vs 5-year signals/day Spearman 0.979, median ratio 0.95 (60 cells). Sources: gross_ci.py, summary_stats.txt.
findings.implication: The 5-year numbers are a trustworthy prior for these entries. Just to break even, an AI trader needs about 0.23R per trade of added value at 15m and about 0.16R at 30m (the median cost share). Nothing in the rule data shows such value exists yet.

verification.recomputed: fiveyear_ref profiles_binance at 15m/30m: 70 cells have signals; 69 have mean_ret_notional <0, 65 have t<-2, 67 have IS<0 and CF<0. Median net per notional: 5-year -0.1418%, live -0.1488% (41 cells with n>=20). 5-year gross (net+0.14%): -0.0018%. Later runs: gross +0.102R (15m) and +0.008R (30m); fees+funding 0.165R and 0.116R; slippage (2*0.0002/stop_frac) 0.066R and 0.046R; net -0.130R and -0.154R. Signals/day live vs 5-year (60 cells over 0.5/day): Spearman 0.979, median ratio 0.945. Live vs 5-year per-notional across cells: Spearman -0.112 (p 0.49). Cross-cell SD: 5-year 0.012% vs live 0.121%. Scripts: fivey.py, payoff.py.
verification.note: The numbers reproduce. 'Live matches 5-year' is true for the level only, not the ranking (cell Spearman -0.11). The 5-year data say the cells are nearly identical (SD 0.012% per notional), so live differences between cells, ten times larger, are mostly noise. The 5-year 'gross' ignores funding, which the 5-year code charges on both sides, so it is slightly understated. The 0.23R/0.16R hurdle is the mean all-in cost at today's low volatility (15m median stop 0.60-0.75%). At the wider 15m stops of the 5-year data (about 1-2% per the design doc) the same 0.14% round trip is roughly 0.07-0.14R.

findings.claim: By the pre-set tier rules, no cell is A. 4 cells are B, all at 30m: N10_HA_PSAR, S4_BB_BBP, N20_EMA9_CHOP and N24_DMI. 22 are D and 46 are C; 8 of the C cells never fired live. Every B cell's confidence interval includes zero.
findings.evidence: Rules were fixed before reading the results. A = n>=30, mean>0, CI lower bound >0, positive in every run with n>=5 (at least 2 runs), side-flip excess >0, and 5-year not negative. D = n>=20, mean<0, 5-year negative (t<-2), and either negative in every run with n>=5 or CI upper bound <0. B = n>=20, mean>0, positive in most runs. Everything else is C. The B cells: N10_HA_PSAR@30m +0.088R [-0.094,+0.253] n 49. S4_BB_BBP@30m +0.110R [-0.179,+0.413] n 42. N20_EMA9_CHOP@30m +0.086R [-0.269,+0.458] n 56. N24_DMI@30m +0.007R [-0.293,+0.246] n 44. A is impossible here because the 5-year result is negative in 69/70 cells. Source: cards_15_30.csv (tier column), cards.py.
findings.implication: None of the 36 strategies at 15m/30m is a verified non-loser, so none meets the owners' goal today. Any AI trader built on them is an experiment, not the deployment of a proven strategy.

verification.recomputed: I applied the stated tier rules to my own cells: B 4, D 22, C 46, with zero tier mismatches against cards_15_30. N10_HA_PSAR@30m +0.088 [-0.093,+0.259] n 49. S4_BB_BBP@30m +0.110 [-0.175,+0.423] n 42. N20_EMA9_CHOP@30m +0.086 [-0.272,+0.450] n 56. N24_DMI@30m +0.007 [-0.287,+0.248] n 44. 8 cells have no signals (cells.py, cmp2.py).
verification.note: Small wording fix. The A rule's 5-year gate excludes only cells with 5-year mean <0 and t<-2 (65 cells), not 69/70. N03_ADX_GC@30m (t -1.6), S1_EMA_RSI_CHOP@15m (t -1.7) and N15_KC_AO@30m (t -0.2) could in principle have been A. A was impossible in practice because no cell had a CI lower bound above 0.

findings.claim: Rankings do not carry over from one run to the next. Every cell that was positive in v3a turned negative later. No cell is positive in all three runs; 11 are negative in all three.
findings.evidence: Every-signal mean R, v3a vs v3b+v4 (33 cells with n>=10 in both): Spearman -0.131 (p 0.47). The 4 cells positive in v3a (N09_ALLIG_AROON@15m, N12_ICHI_AO@15m, S4_BB_BBP@30m, N10_HA_PSAR@30m) were all negative later. v3b vs v4: Spearman -0.111 (19 cells). The same-side-relative measure also fails to carry over (Spearman -0.07 to +0.13). Of 29 cells with n>=5 in all runs, 0 are positive in all three and 11 are negative in all three. Sources: summary_stats.txt and the per-run columns of cards_15_30.csv.
findings.implication: A November promotion based on a few weeks of account P&L will mostly pick noise. Promotion should rest on every-signal results with time-cluster CIs and criteria fixed in advance. For a +-0.1R interval a cell needs roughly 11-14 days of every-signal data at best (N04_ST_KLINGER@15m, N10_HA_PSAR@30m) and 30-60+ days for typical cells (column es_days_for_ci_halfwidth_0.1R).

verification.recomputed: v3a vs later, 33 cells with n>=10 in both: Spearman -0.131 (p 0.467). The 4 v3a-positive cells were all negative later: N09@15m -0.288, N10@30m -0.039, N12@15m -0.578, S4@30m -0.040. v3b vs v4, 19 cells: -0.111 (p 0.65). 29 cells with n>=5 in all runs: 0 positive in all three, 11 negative in all three. Under independence with per-run negative shares of 0.90/0.76/0.55, 10.9 cells would be all-negative by chance. Days needed for a ±0.1R CI using cluster-robust SEs: N04_ST_KLINGER@15m 16 (4h clusters) to 34 (day clusters); N10_HA_PSAR@30m 15.5 to 26; N17_KC_RSI@15m 40-43; S4_BB_BBP@15m 141-174 (persist.py, days.py).
verification.note: The non-persistence finding stands. Two corrections. First, 11 cells negative in all three runs is exactly what chance predicts when nearly every cell is about -cost, so run-consistent negativity does not show that a cell is worse than the others; this undercuts the D criterion. Second, the 11-14 day estimate is optimistic: with cluster-robust SEs the best cells need about 15-35 days, and the noisy candidate S4@15m needs 140+ days. That is beyond 12/31 even at the every-signal level.

findings.claim: The 36 strategies show no ability to pick the right direction at 15m/30m. The only raw-significant side-flip cells are short-only or short-heavy strategies, and the market fell during v3b and v4. Once the run's same-side drift is removed, their excess is about zero.
findings.evidence: Pipeline side-flip (coinflip_sideflip.csv), kind level: 15m +0.0066R (n 1,087, p 0.46), 30m -0.0227R (n 536, p 0.65). Raw p<0.05 cells: N20_EMA9_CHOP@15m +0.28R, N20_EMA9_CHOP@30m +0.36R (long share 0.00), N24_DMI@30m +0.29R (long share 0.11). Minus the mean of other strategies' same-side flips in the same run x tf, these become -0.065, +0.059 and +0.015R (sideflip_pairs_15_30.csv). Equal-weight market: v3b -0.9%, v4 -2.6%. A day-level drift benchmark was tried first and dropped because it produced absurd adjustments (N17_KC_RSI@15m +0.88R).
findings.implication: Do not treat N20_EMA9_CHOP or N24_DMI's recent wins as skill. As AI traders they would be short-side regime bets, and they need a regime rule plus testing in a rising market before any real money.

verification.recomputed: Side flip at kind level: 15m +0.0065R (n 1,087), 4h-cluster CI [-0.166,+0.201], day CI [-0.061,+0.168]. 30m -0.0227R (n 536), CI [-0.128,+0.087]. Drift adjustment, recomputed as h minus the mean h of other strategies' same run x tf x side: N20_EMA9_CHOP@15m raw +0.280 → -0.065 [-0.33,+0.35]; N20@30m +0.359 → +0.059 [-0.32,+0.45]; N24_DMI@30m +0.287 → +0.015 [-0.34,+0.27]. Same-side drift in v4 15m: shorts h +0.461 (n 495), longs -0.628 (sideflip.py).
verification.note: Reproduces exactly. One addition: the 15m interval reaches +0.20R, about the size of the cost hurdle. 'No ability' should read 'no detectable ability'; a direction edge as large as the costs cannot be ruled out.

findings.claim: Under the house ladder, which locks profit at ROE levels, R per signal falls as leverage rises. In addition, 50x with margin equal to the leverage percentage can almost never be sized with a 2 ATR stop at 15m/30m.
findings.evidence: Fixed-leverage replay of all 1,891 15m/30m signals from v3b+v4 (levreplay.py, using the repo's obsshadows.variant_settings). Paired with the live rule on the same closed signals, 15m: 10x +0.162R (n 1,036), 20x +0.061R, 30x +0.018R, 40x -0.087R (n 926), 50x -0.404R (n 176). 30m: 10x +0.019R, 20x +0.061R, 30x +0.005R, 40x -0.001R. Share of signals that can be sized: 40x 78% (15m) and 33% (30m); 50x 14.3% (15m) and 0% (30m). Rejection reasons: loss at stop > 15% of equity, stop too close to liquidation, and the inferred brackets. Mark-inclusive mean R at 15m: 10x -0.020, live -0.128. Source: levreplay_summary.csv.
findings.implication: With house stops, the plan of 20-50x by AI confidence will mostly fail to place 50x. If exits stay ROE-based, the highest-confidence trades would systematically get worse R. The coded exits should be in price, ATR or R units so that leverage only changes size. Treat 50x at 15m/30m as unavailable unless the margin share or stop rule changes.

verification.recomputed: I wrote my own fixed-leverage replay: the repo's daily3._alone on live_bars, obsshadows.variant_settings, inferred brackets, funding 0 (myreplay.py, levan.py). Paired against the live-rule replay, 15m: 10x +0.159 [4h CI -0.200,+0.525], 20x +0.055 [-0.131,+0.286], 30x +0.024 [-0.010,+0.070], 40x -0.088 [-0.233,+0.008] (sized 78.0%), 50x -0.403 [-1.299,+0.215] (sized 14.3%, n 176). 30m: 10x +0.020, 20x +0.053, 30x +0.004, 40x -0.001 (sized 33.2%), 50x sized 0%. The signals that can be sized at 50x have a median stop of 0.39%, against 0.61% for all 15m signals.
verification.note: The point estimates reproduce, but 'high confidence' is not warranted. Every paired difference has a cluster CI that includes zero, and at 30m the pattern is not monotone (10x +0.02, 20x +0.05, 30x 0.00, 40x 0.00). The 50x subset is a narrow-stop, high-cost-share selection. The finding that 50x cannot be placed applies only to margin = leverage % with the 15% loss cap. The AI design v2 already uses R-based exits (§3-4: the ROE ladder converted to R at 20x) and risk-per-stop sizing (§4-3). At 3% risk a 0.63% stop gives notional of about 4.8x equity, which is about 9.6% margin at 50x and can be placed. The 10/7 owner change back to 20-50x leaves the sizing rule pending.

findings.claim: N10_HA_PSAR is the least-bad base among the 36 at 15m/30m. It is the only strategy that beat its same-side peers in all three runs at both timeframes. Its absolute expectancy is still about zero, and the 5-year result is clearly negative.
findings.evidence: N10_HA_PSAR@30m: every-signal +0.088R [-0.094,+0.253], n 49. Without the best 4h block: +0.046. Without the best day: +0.032. By run: v3a +0.21 (25), v3b +0.04 (13), v4 -0.13 (11); later -0.039R. Excess vs same-side peers +0.288R [0.115,0.440], BH q 0.005 (the only positive measure surviving BH). Account: +0.146R, n 16, PF 2.07, worst DD 16%. Side-flip -0.002R (n 22). 5-year: -0.132% per notional, t -19.3. 12.5 signals/day. N10_HA_PSAR@15m: -0.038R [-0.249,+0.170], n 109, later +0.066, same-side excess +0.20 [0.01,0.38], 24.7 signals/day. With 29 cells eligible, about 3.6 would be all-runs-positive on the relative measure by chance, so the run consistency alone is not strong. Source: cards_15_30.csv.
findings.implication: If the owners want one 15m/30m AI trader from the 36, N10_HA_PSAR (30m primary, 15m secondary) has the most support. It should be run as a pre-registered test of whether the AI's filtering adds R over the same signals, not as a proven earner.

verification.recomputed: N10_HA_PSAR@30m: n 49, +0.088 [-0.093,+0.259]. Without the best 4h block +0.046; without the best day +0.032. By run: v3a +0.211 (25), v3b +0.039 (13), v4 -0.132 (11); later -0.039. Same-side excess +0.288, my bootstrap [0.109,0.439], percentile p 0.001 → BH q 0.057 over 52 cells. Cluster-robust t: 4h one-sided p 0.0034 (19 clusters), which gives BH q of about 0.18; day clusters p 0.0099. Relative excess by run: v3a +0.443, v3b +0.223, v4 +0.010. N10@15m and N10@30m are the only all-runs-positive relative cells out of 29 eligible. Unresolved signals for N10@30m: 10 of 59 (sameside.py, ct.py).
verification.note: The descriptive numbers reproduce. 'BH q 0.005, the only positive measure surviving BH' does not hold up: it depends on the shifted-bootstrap p. Under percentile or cluster-t p-values it misses BH at 0.05 (q 0.057-0.18). The BH family also leaves out the other measures that were scanned (raw, side flip, adjusted side flip, coin flip). In the most recent run (v4) the relative excess is about 0 (+0.010, n 11). 'Holds up without the best day' means +0.03R. Low confidence is the right label.

findings.claim: S4_BB_BBP is the second candidate. At 15m it was strongly positive in v4 and has the largest favourable moves (MFE) of the 36, but it was negative in v3a and its 5-year result is negative.
findings.evidence: S4_BB_BBP@15m: every-signal +0.025R [-0.416,+0.616], n 95. By run: v3a -0.25 (56), v3b -0.14 (5), v4 +0.51 (34); later +0.42R. Account: +0.226R, n 22, PF 1.87, worst DD 15%. Mean MFE 1.43R; 19% of signals reach +1R. Side-flip +0.39R (n 39, p 0.10). 5-year: -0.152% per notional, t -38.7. 20.6 signals/day. S4_BB_BBP@30m (B): +0.110R, n 42, but later -0.04R.
findings.implication: S4_BB_BBP suits a trial of AI exit management, because its large MFE means exits matter. The positive v4 numbers could be the falling market and the quiet period. Keep it as a rule account in parallel so the AI's added value can be measured.

verification.recomputed: S4_BB_BBP@15m: n 95, +0.025 [-0.418,+0.609]. By run: -(56) -(5) +(34); later +0.422. Side flip raw +0.390 (n 39, p 0.098); drift-adjusted +0.252 [-0.32,+0.96]. 5-year -0.152%, t -38.7. 20.6 signals/day. Largest mean MFE among replay cells with n>=20: 1.565R (v3b+v4). Share reaching +1R: 36% of v3b+v4 signals. The analyst's 19% divides by all 95 rows, 43 of which (v3a skipped shadows) have no MFE; among the 52 rows that have MFE it is 34.5% (chk2.py). Days needed for ±0.1R: 141-174 (days.py).
verification.note: '19% of signals reach +1R' is a denominator error; the true share is about 35%. The cell's interval is about ±0.5R, and validating it to ±0.1R would take about 5 months of every-signal data. It cannot be confirmed before 12/31. The positive v4 result is mostly short signals in a falling market (side flip after drift +0.25 with a CI spanning zero).

findings.claim: Account P&L is a poor guide. Accounts see only 15-35% of signals, and some top leaderboard cells are negative on every signal.
findings.evidence: S2_ST_ROC@15m: account +0.171R (n 39, PF 1.50), every-signal -0.198R (n 236). N07_ICHI_CMO@30m: BH-better than coin flips on account trades (q 0.014), but on only 8 trades against a 24-trade coin-flip pool. Its every-signal is +0.118R [-0.26,+0.49], n 14. Account vs every-signal mean R across 41 cells: Spearman 0.72, so they are related but not interchangeable. Source: cards_15_30.csv (acct_* vs es_* columns, cf_* from coinflip_pooled.csv).
findings.implication: Choose AI strategies, and promote or retire them, on every-signal replay statistics, not dashboard P&L.

verification.recomputed: From raw trades.csv: S2_ST_ROC@15m account n 39, +0.171R, PF 1.50; every-signal n 236, -0.198R. N07_ICHI_CMO@30m account n 8, +0.67R; every-signal n 14, +0.118 [-0.25,+0.48]. Account vs every-signal mean R over 41 cells: Spearman 0.719. Account trades as a share of every-signal rows (43 cells with n>=20): median 30%, IQR 21-46%, range 9-64% (acct.py).
verification.note: Small correction: account coverage is about 9-64% (median 30%), not 15-35%. The conclusion is unchanged.

findings.claim: These cells are clearly not worth a 15m/30m AI trader: negative live in every run or with a CI below zero, and negative in the 5-year backtest.
findings.implication: Do not spend Sonnet or Opus traders on these at 15m/30m. If they stay on, keep them as zero-cost rule accounts for monitoring only.

verification.recomputed: Means, CIs and run signs reproduce for all listed cells (cells.py). The 5-year t values range from -10.9 to -54.9. Under my percentile bootstrap some q-values move: N20_EMA9_CHOP@15m 0.055 (theirs 0.010), N18@30m 0.022, OBV_B@15m 0.016, N17@30m 0.047.
verification.note: The facts hold. They do not make these cells worse than the C cells. Their 5-year per-notional means (-0.12% to -0.18%) are the same as everyone else's; the large 5-year |t| values reflect signal counts; and 'negative in every run' is what chance predicts. The implication (no AI trader at 15m/30m) applies equally to nearly all of the 36.

findings.claim: 16 of the 72 cells fire too rarely to support or validate a dedicated AI trader before 12/31.
findings.evidence: 8 cells never fired in the 4.6 days of every-signal data and fire 0-0.1 times/day in 5 years: N14_ICHI_RSI, N15_KC_AO, N21_ST_RSI_ADX, S1_EMA_RSI_CHOP, at both timeframes. 8 more fire under about 1/day live and in 5 years: N03_ADX_GC, N08_ICHI_WR, N11_BREAKAWAY, S5_DONCHIAN_MFI, at both timeframes. Source: live_sig_per_day and y5_per_day in cards_15_30.csv.
findings.implication: Leave these off the AI list. A trader that sees under one signal a day cannot gather enough trades to show any skill by 12/31.

verification.recomputed: Live signals/day (SUBMITTED / 4.81 run-days) and 5-year per_day: N14, N15, N21, S1 are 0 live and 0-0.10/day in 5 years at both TFs. N11 0.42/0.21 live (0.35/0.16 in 5 years); N08 1.04/0.62; S5 0.83/0.83; N03 0.83/0.83 (5-year 0.61/0.28) (fivey.py, my_sigperday.csv).
verification.note: Reproduces. N08_ICHI_WR@15m is right at about 1/day.

findings.claim: The house payoff structure needs a win rate of about 60% (15m) or 68% (30m) to break even, above the observed 53% and 59%. 30m is cheaper than 15m in R terms.
findings.evidence: Later runs: average stop-out -1.21R at 15m and -1.15R at 30m; average lock exit +0.82R and +0.53R. Breakeven win rate about 59.5% (15m) and 68.5% (30m); observed 53.1% and 59.3%. Median round-trip cost: 0.23R (15m) vs 0.16R (30m). 63% (15m) and 59% (30m) of signals reach +0.5R; 26.5% and 9.8% reach +1R. 25% of 15m stop-outs (13% at 30m) had first reached +0.5R. Sources: every_signal_rows_15_30.csv, pooled_15_30.csv.
findings.implication: For AI entries, 30m costs about 0.07R less per trade. Early take-profit can only reshape the payoff; it cannot create profit when gross is about zero. The AI's value has to come from which signals it takes.

verification.recomputed: Later runs. 15m: SL mean -1.209R, LOCK +0.822R, breakeven win rate 0.595, observed 0.531. 30m: -1.147R, +0.528R, breakeven 0.685, observed 0.593. Median round trip / stop: 0.222 and 0.157. MFE >=0.5R: 63.4% and 59.3%; >=1R: 26.5% and 9.8%. SL exits that first reached +0.5R: 25.0% and 13.2%. Gross: 15m +0.102, 30m +0.008 (payoff.py).
verification.note: The numbers reproduce. Caveat on the implication: 30m is cheaper in cost, but under the house ROE ladder it locks at a smaller R (+0.53 vs +0.82), and in the later runs its net (-0.154) and gross (+0.008) were no better than 15m (-0.130 / +0.102). The breakeven figures apply to the current ladder only; the planned R-based exits change them. The exit rule is not neutral here: the looser-lock and 10x variants move the point estimates by +0.06 to +0.16R, though not significantly.

findings.claim: The three runs are not like-for-like. v3a used tier-walk leverage, mostly 50x, which by itself lowers R, and v3b/v4 took place in a quiet, falling market. Differences between runs mix leverage, regime and noise.
findings.evidence: v3a 15m leverage mix 50:736 30:376 40:248 20:28, vs later 30:950 40:151 50:34. 50x vs the live rule costs -0.40R per signal at 15m (paired, n 176). Median 15m stop: 0.58% (v3a), 0.75% (v3b), 0.60% (v4). Long share at 15m in v4: 0.355. Sources: pooled_15_30.csv, levreplay_summary.csv.
findings.implication: Do not read the better v4 numbers at 15m (-0.025R vs v3a -0.322R) as improvement. Part of the gap is the lower leverage, and part is short-heavy signals in a down market.

strategy_note_problems: N10_HA_PSAR@30m: 'same-side excess BH q 0.005' is method-dependent. With a percentile cluster bootstrap q is 0.057; with a cluster-robust t (4h) p is 0.0034, giving BH q of about 0.18 over 52 cells. 'Holds up when the best day is removed' overstates it: the mean drops from +0.088 to +0.032R. In v4 the relative excess is +0.010 (n 11).
S4_BB_BBP@15m: '19% reach 1R' divides by 95 rows, 43 of which (v3a skipped shadows) have no MFE. Among signals with MFE data about 35% reach +1R (36% in v3b+v4).

N17_KC_RSI@15m: 'the v4 gain came with long-side mean-reversion during a crash' is wrong. In v4 the 87 longs averaged -0.007R; the small v4 gain (+0.04R) came from 8 shorts at +0.52R. '(most negative)' fits only the t value (-71.2), which is driven by its signal count. Per notional, -0.165% is not the most negative: N11_BREAKAWAY@30m is -0.183%, N17_KC_RSI@30m -0.180%, OBV_B@30m -0.171%.
N03_ADX_GC@30m: '(least negative 5y)' is wrong. N15_KC_AO@30m is -0.022% (t -0.15) and N14_ICHI_RSI@15m is +0.117% on 2 signals; N03 is least negative only among cells with hundreds of signals.
N20_EMA9_CHOP@15m (and F10): 'BH q 0.010' becomes 0.055 under a percentile cluster bootstrap. Its D grade rests on CI hi -0.04 with 4h clusters only.

Throughout the D grades: 'negative in all three runs' is what chance predicts (10.9 expected vs 11 observed among 29 cells). The 5-year t values mostly reflect signal counts. Per notional, D cells (-0.12% to -0.18%) do not differ from C cells, so D vs C does not rank the strategies.

All other sampled numbers reproduce: N10@15m, S4@30m, N20@30m, N24@30m, N13@15m, N23@15m, S2@15m, N01@15m, N09@15m, N12@15m, V39@15m, V45@15m, DOGE@15m, N02@15m, N07@15m, N16@15m, N18@15m, N19@15m, N22@15m, N07@30m, OBV_S@30m, N23@30m, N01@30m, N06@30m, N15@30m, S1@15m/30m, N05@15m, S3@15m, OBV_S@15m, N02@30m, N16@30m. All 72 grades match the stated tier rules.
verifier_missed: Leverage-rule confound in the headline: the pooled 15m loss comes mostly from v3a's 50x tier walk (-0.32R) against v4 (-0.03R). Under the rule in use now (v3b+v4) the every-signal CIs include zero at 15m ([-0.35,+0.15]) and reach zero at 30m. With KST-day clusters the all-runs 15m CI also crosses zero ([-0.50,+0.03]).

Direction x regime dominates cell results. Within each run, long vs short mean R differ by 0.6-0.9R (15m v3a long -0.00 / short -0.69; v4 long -0.61 / short +0.30), and the sign flips between v3a and v3b/v4. A cell's long share explains 10-29% of cross-cell variance within a run, with the sign flipping (r +0.45 in v3a, -0.54 in v3b, -0.31 in v4). Live cell rankings are mostly long share x market direction.

The 5-year data say the 72 cells are nearly identical: cross-cell SD of mean return per notional is 0.012%, against 0.121% live. Live cell differences are about 10x what the long-run data support, so the D/C/B split and live leaderboards carry little strategy information.

Baseline under the planned AI exits: design v2 §3-4 uses the current ROE ladder converted to R at 20x. That equals the lev20 replay, with every-signal mean R of -0.097 (15m, n 1,085) and -0.113 (30m, n 544) in v3b+v4. This is a less negative starting point than the live rule (-0.130 / -0.154). The design's bar-close-only lock updates differ from the engine's 1m locking, so this is approximate.

The design docs already contain F6's recommendations: R-based exits and stop-distance leverage / risk-per-stop sizing (AIBOT_DESIGN_KO_v2 §3-4, §4-3). MY_REVIEW_KO shows the 10/7 change back to 20-50x fixed with the sizing rule pending. Design v2 (D15) also recommended that the AI NOT judge 15m/30m signals because of signal volume and cost, which conflicts with the owners' 10/7 noon decision. The lens does not cost the 15m/30m signal volume per trader (for example, N10 15m+30m is about 37 signals/day).

Duplicate events: 52% of every-signal rows share coin, bar and side with another strategy (3,638 rows = 2,479 unique events). The pooled n overstates independent evidence, and BH across cells runs on positively dependent tests.

Validation horizon: with cluster-robust SEs, even the best cells need 15-35 days of every-signal data for ±0.1R, and S4_BB_BBP@15m needs 140-174 days. A November promotion or the 12/31 'verified non-loser' goal can only be judged at pooled or strategy-group level, or on a pre-registered AI-minus-rule difference, not per cell.

The cost hurdle depends on volatility. The 0.23R/0.16R figures reflect the current quiet market (15m median stop 0.60-0.75%). At the 15m stops typical of the 5-year data (about 1-2%), the same 0.14% round trip is roughly 0.07-0.14R, so the hurdle and any AI 'value added' will move with the regime.

Unresolved and missing rows: 222 of 1,337 signals at 30m (17%) and 245 of 2,768 at 15m (9%) are excluded across runs. v3a's shadow day 10-03 alone has 365 unresolved rows spread over the whole day, which points to a data-horizon problem; v3a entered positions open at the end are also dropped.

The v3a every-signal set mixes account-equity leverage and live fills (entered trades) with fresh-account leverage and Binance final klines plus funding (skipped shadows). The effect is small, but the two halves are not like-for-like.
limits: Every-signal data covers only 4.57 days: v3a 2.52 + v3b 0.62 + v4 1.43, in a quiet market (median 15m stop 0.6% of price) that fell during v3b and v4 (equal-weight -0.9% and -2.6%). Regime dependence cannot be judged; rising markets and high volatility are not represented.

Time clusters are few: a pooled cell has 15-31 four-hour clusters, and v3b alone has 5, so its intervals are too narrow to trust. The 4h-block bootstrap still treats blocks as independent, which understates uncertainty on trending days.

The runs differ in more than time. v3a used tier-walk leverage (mostly 50x, which costs R under the ROE ladder), v3b/v4 used quality_v1 (mostly 30x), and v3b has no skipped shadows (it uses the replay instead). Differences between runs mix leverage, market and noise.

545 v3a skipped shadows (all timeframes) were unresolved when the nightly job ran and are excluded; the bias sign is unknown. In the replay, the 10-12% of signals still open at the end are excluded from the main mean; marking them to the last close changes cell means by up to about 0.1R (columns *_incl_unres_mark).

The every-signal R measures the raw signal under house exits with one position per signal. It does not represent the planned AI behaviour (skipping, early take-profit or stop, near-signal entries, event reactions). The data cannot say whether an AI filter adds value; only a shadow comparison of the AI's picks against the same signals can.

The side-flip test assumes the opposite trade fills at the same quote (about 1bp in the flipped side's favour) and is confounded by market drift. The run-level same-side adjustment is a rough benchmark (it uses other strategies' timing), and a day-level version was rejected as unstable.

The 5-year reference is every signal under the OLD tier-walk leverage, example brackets and the $1,000 sizing equity, reported per notional. It shows the net loss is about the cost, but its per-cell spread is tiny (about +-0.02% per notional), so it cannot rank strategies within the 36.

The fixed-leverage replay uses brackets inferred from the export, not Binance's live table, so the bracket rejections at 50x for BCH/LTC may be overstated. Pairs exclude signals still open at the end, which tilts lower-leverage variants (longer holds) toward their faster exits.
The coin-flip bootstrap on account trades uses tiny pools (24 coin-flip trades at 30m). Its single BH-significant cell in this lens (N07_ICHI_CMO@30m) rests on 8 trades and is not trustworthy.

The tier rules were fixed before reading the results, but thresholds such as n>=20 are judgement calls (for example, DOGE@30m is C by rule but clearly negative). No cell can reach A while the 5-year result is negative for all of them.

findings.claim: Neither the live runs nor 5 years show a directional edge at 1h or 4h for our 36 strategies. 1h/4h only lose less, because costs are a smaller share of the wider stop. The signals themselves are no better.
findings.evidence: 5-year every-signal simulation under today's live rules (fy_sim.py -> tf_summary_5y.csv; 36 strategies x 6 coins, 2021-08..2026-09, CI clustered by UTC day). Net mean R: 15m -0.172 [-0.180,-0.165] (n 1,113,807), 30m -0.126 [-0.133,-0.118], 1h -0.094 [-0.103,-0.086] (n 222,665), 4h -0.051 [-0.073,-0.029] (n 13,487). Gross R (cost added back) is ~0 at every timeframe: 15m -0.003, 30m -0.006, 1h -0.005 [-0.014,+0.003], 4h +0.011 [-0.011,+0.033]. Mean cost in R: 0.169 / 0.120 / 0.089 / 0.062. Live every-signal R, all 3 runs (live_cells.py -> tf_summary_live.csv; cluster = run x 4h block): 15m -0.235 [-0.373,-0.072] n 2529; 30m -0.205 [-0.293,-0.109] n 1117; 1h -0.091 [-0.219,+0.051] n 580 (by run: v3a -0.008, v3b -0.373, v4 -0.052); 4h +0.151 [-0.161,+0.456] n 55. Own simulation vs the repo's 5-year reference profiles: Spearman 0.87 over 55 cells.
findings.implication: Do not pick 1h/4h as 'where the edge is'. A 1h/4h rule account is the cheapest way to lose slowly, not a path to the 12/31 'not losing' bar. An AI trader cannot gain an edge by watching 1h/4h unless it adds something the rules lack.

findings.claim: With the house 2 ATR stop and the 1 ATR liquidation buffer, 4h is almost untradable, and the planned 20-50x leverage is impossible at 1h/4h. 4h rule accounts trade only BTC/ETH (SOL in quiet weeks), at 20x.
findings.evidence: lev_feas.py -> lev_feasibility.csv (paperbot.sizing.size_position, quality_v1, $5,000, inferred brackets). Share of 5-year signals sizable at >=50x / >=40x / >=30x / >=20x: 15m 7.4% / 35.7% / 81.1% / 97.6%; 30m 2.2% / 13.5% / 56.7% / 92.4%; 1h 0.4% / 3.6% / 26.9% / 77.4%; 4h 0% / 0% / 1.1% / 19.3%. 4h sizable at 20x by coin: BTC 55%, ETH 26%, SOL 4%, DOGE 8%, LTC 13%, BCH 9%. Live signals (quiet market): 1h >=50x 1.7%, >=30x 68%; 4h >=20x 46%. Replay of v3b+v4 (replay_signals.csv): every one of 39 BCH/DOGE/LTC 4h signals was REJECTED_SIZING; the 28 traded 4h signals were BTC 3, ETH 12, SOL 13, all at 20x. Account-level rejections for our 36 (sizing_rejections.csv): v3a 4h 35 (DOGE 13, BCH 10, LTC 7, SOL 5), v3a 1h 8, v3b 4h 8, v4 4h 12.
findings.implication: With a 2 ATR code stop, leverage set 'by AI confidence' would be cut by sizing most of the time. At 15m, 50x fits only 7% of signals (5-year) to 28% (live quiet market), and at 1h/4h nothing above 30x/20x fits. Either decide the stop rule for 40-50x first, or cap AI leverage per timeframe at the level that actually fits. 4h rule accounts are BTC/ETH accounts in practice.

verification.recomputed: verify/vlev.py -> v_lev.csv. Share of 5-year signals the house sizing (size_position, v3_settings, 'best' group, $5,000, inferred brackets) allows at >=50/40/30/20x: 15m 7.4/35.7/81.1/97.6%; 30m 2.2/13.5/56.7/92.4%; 1h 0.4/3.6/26.9/77.4%; 4h 0.0/0.0/1.1/19.2%. 4h at >=20x by coin: BTC 55.0%, ETH 25.4%, SOL 4.4%, DOGE 7.6%, LTC 12.9%, BCH 9.2%. Account rejections: v3a 4h 35, v3a 1h 8, v3b 4h 8, v4 4h 12. Splitting the rules: with the liquidation-buffer rule alone (max_loss_frac disabled), 15m >=50x = 33.4% (house 7.4%), 1h >=50x 6.9% (0.4%), >=40x 15.8% (3.6%), >=30x 38.7% (26.9%); 4h >=30x 3.3% (1.1%). With the max-loss rule alone, the shares equal the house numbers at every level >=30x. At 20x the liquidation buffer binds (house = liq-only).
verification.note: The numbers reproduce exactly, but the stated cause is partly wrong. Above 20x the binding limit is the 15%-of-equity max-loss rule combined with quality_v1's margin = leverage% (50x uses 50% margin), not the 1 ATR liquidation buffer. The buffer binds only at 20x, which covers all of 4h. This changes the design choice for the AI. 'Leverage by confidence' is capped by the margin-fraction and max-loss rule at 30-50x, so decoupling margin from leverage would let about 33% of 15m signals fit at 50x. At 1h/4h, even the buffer alone keeps 40-50x below 16% (1h) and 1% (4h), so the 1h/4h conclusion stands. Minor: the bracket MMR depends on notional, so at a $500 account BCH/LTC 4h fits rise only to 11%/17%.

findings.claim: Over 5 years, a 15m/30m signal that agrees with the 1h/4h state does slightly better than one that disagrees (+0.01 to +0.09R, same sign in IS and CF for 18 of 20 definitions). The agreeing signals still lose clearly, so watching 1h/4h trims losses but creates no edge.
findings.evidence: fy_htf.py -> fy_htf_pooled.csv / fy_htf_groups.csv. Agree-minus-against within strategy x tf, SE clustered by day, IS 2021-08..2024-06 then CF 2024-07..2026-09. 15m examples: market 4h regime +0.090 (t 2.0) then +0.067 (t 1.5); market 1h EMA20 side +0.024 (2.2) then +0.016 (1.2); same strategy's 4h signal in the last 16h +0.027 (2.2) then +0.020 (1.3); same strategy's 1h signal +0.013 (1.0) then +0.012 (0.9). 30m effects are similar or smaller. findings.claim: Entering a 15m/30m signal while the same strategy's 1h/4h position is already open in the same direction is worse than entering with no open 1h/4h position. Piling on is a late entry, not a confirmation.
findings.evidence: fy_htf_pooled.csv agree-minus-neutral for same_pos (the same strategy's simulated 1h/4h house-exit trade still open at the signal time): 15m same_pos_4h -0.182 (t -6.1) IS, -0.078 (t -3.1) CF; 15m same_pos_1h -0.057 (t -5.5) IS, -0.036 (t -3.4) CF; 30m same_pos_4h -0.108 (t -3.8) IS, -0.062 (t -2.5) CF; 30m same_pos_1h -0.043 (t -5.2) IS, -0.022 (t -2.3) CF. Group means for 15m same_pos_4h, IS/CF: agree -0.339/-0.243, no position -0.163/-0.168.
findings.implication: The AI should not treat 'the 1h/4h rule account is already long' as a reason to add or upsize a 15m/30m long. If anything it is a reason to skip or size down. Put this rule in the trader prompt and the exit code, and test it in the shadow account.

verification.recomputed: verify/vhtf.py with two position definitions: posA (as the analyst's: latest sized same-coin HTF signal still open, here with 5m-resolution exit times) and posB (a real one-position rule account across the 6 coins). verify/vhtf_confound.py adds gross R and fixed effects by strategy x tf x cost decile. Net agree-minus-neutral 15m posA_4h: -0.227 (t -6.4) IS, -0.089 (t -2.97) CF. posB_4h: -0.258 (t -6.7) IS, -0.086 (t -2.65) CF. Their -0.182/-0.078 reproduce in their own file. But gross R for 15m posA_4h is -0.030 (t -0.95) IS and +0.060 (t +2.05) CF; with cost-decile FE -0.050 (t -1.7) and +0.028 (t 1.0). For 15m posA_1h: gross +0.003 / +0.012, cost-FE 0.000 / +0.003. For 30m posA_4h: gross -0.025 / +0.021. Mean cost per 15m signal: 0.35R while a 4h position is open (agree) and 0.38R (against), vs 0.16R with no position. 'Against' is worse than 'agree': agree-minus-against for 15m posA_4h is +0.043 IS, +0.110 (t 2.5) CF.
verification.note: The net-R gap reproduces, but the stated mechanism ('piling on is a late entry') is not supported. A sized 4h/1h position exists mostly in quiet markets (the 20x/30x sizing needs a small HTF ATR). In those markets the 15m stop is tight, so round-trip cost per R doubles. Once cost is added back or controlled, the effect is about 0 in both windows. An open opposite-side position is just as bad as a same-side one. Implication fix: do not write a 'the 1h/4h account is long, so skip' rule into the trader prompt. The usable rule is a stop-width/cost filter on 15m/30m entries (skip or downsize when 2 ATR is small relative to the 0.14% round trip), and that rule applies whatever the HTF account holds.

findings.claim: The live data cannot confirm the HTF-agreement effect. The bot's own ctx htf_regime almost never shows a trend in these quiet days, and the alternative definitions give large but unstable estimates driven by market drift.

findings.claim: No 1h/4h strategy can be verified 'not to lose money' by 12/31. That would need about 1,500-1,700 trades per cell, and the 4h cells produce a few per week after sizing.

Sized signals per day over all 36 strategies x 6 coins (5-year): 1h 118, 4h 7.15. Per strategy (cards fy_sized_per_day): 1h 0.01-14.7, 4h 0.00-0.82. A one-position account takes fewer.

strategy_note_problems: N23_HA_ST 4h: 'misses the preset B bar by t 0.0004' is a knife-edge. Independent recomputation gives IS gross t 2.009 (tf bars) and 2.43 (5m exits), so it meets B. Net falls to +0.008R (t 0.44) with 5m exits, and BH q with week clusters is about 0.03-0.05, not 0.004 (verify/vn23.py, v_cells_1h_4h.csv).

N17_KC_RSI 1h: 'Its 15m every-signal looked OK live (+0.113, n 109)' uses only the v3b+v4 replay. All three runs give -0.283 (n 270): v3a -0.552 (n 161), v3b +0.626 (14), v4 +0.037 (95) (v_live_es.csv).

OBV_B 4h (D): 'Negative in both halves even before costs' quotes the NET IS/CF values (-0.085/-0.111). Gross by half is t -0.51 / -0.89, and overall gross is -0.035 (t -1.0, BH q 0.87), so the D grade rests on a point estimate.
DOGE 1h (D): the grade rests on 8 live signals in 6 clusters (CI [-0.90,-0.005]). Its 5-year gross is the best of the 1h cells (+0.023, t 1.55; +0.025, t 1.89 with 5m exits).
N16_BBRSI 1h and S5_DONCHIAN_MFI 1h (D): both flip to C with 5m-resolution exits (gross -0.016 t -1.04; +0.006). Their D rests on gross point estimates of -0.03 with |t| <= 1.8.

N17_KC_RSI 4h (D): gross -0.088 (t -2.93) has BH q 0.074 over the 72 cells at tf bars (0.023 with 5m exits; 0.37 with week clusters), so 'clearly not a candidate' should be worded as 'likely negative'.
N22_VORTEX_PSAR 4h: IS gross t is 1.50 in my recomputation (1.4 quoted). Minor; the conclusion is unchanged.
N23_HA_ST 4h: 'live sizing rejects 3+4 (DOGE)'. The 4 account-level rejects are DOGE 3 + BCH 1, so the label names only the replay coins. Trivial.
verifier_missed: The 5-year sim resolves exits on the signal's own bars (4h bars for 4h signals), while the live engine uses 1m bars and arms the ROE ladder within minutes. Re-simulated on 5m bars: 4h win rate goes from 62% to 75%, SD from 0.68 to 0.59, pooled 4h net from -0.051 to -0.057, N23 4h net from +0.024 to +0.008, the lev10 gain disappears, and 2 D grades flip. Conclusions at the timeframe level are robust; cell-level net figures and the exit/leverage implications are not (verify/vsim.py, v_tf_summary.csv, v_exits.csv, v_cards.csv).

F4's position-state effect is a cost/stop-width confound. Sized 4h/1h positions exist mostly in quiet markets, where 15m stops are tight, so mean cost per 15m signal is 0.35R with a 4h position open vs 0.16R without. In gross R or with cost-decile fixed effects the effect is about 0. The actionable AI rule is a stop-width/cost filter on 15m/30m entries, not 'skip when the HTF account is in a position' (v_htf_confound.csv).

Leverage feasibility above 20x is limited by the 15%-of-equity max-loss rule combined with quality_v1's margin = leverage%, not by the liquidation buffer. If the AI design decouples margin from leverage, about 33% of 15m signals (5-year) fit at 50x on the buffer alone, against 7.4% under house rules. At 1h/4h, 40-50x stays mostly infeasible either way (v_lev.csv).

The live every-signal pool mixes leverage regimes: v3a used the old 50x tier walk, and because the ladder is ROE-based, R is not leverage-free. It is also censored: v3a skipped shadows that were still open (21% at 1h, 20% at 30m) are dropped without a mark price. Neither point is disclosed in F1/F5/F13.
The positive live 4h result is ETH-only. Account trades: ETH 13 at +0.64R, BTC 9 at -0.24R, SOL 9 at -0.19R; the v4 replay shows the same pattern.

Day clustering may understate uncertainty for 4h signals, whose trades overlap across days. With ISO-week clusters, N23 4h's gross t drops from 3.85 to 3.18 and its BH q from 0.004 to about 0.05. No pooled timeframe conclusion changes.

The preset grade rule is fragile in both directions. B hinges on a t-threshold that independent recomputation crosses. D accepts a gross point estimate <= -0.02 with no significance requirement, or a live CI from 8 signals. Only N17 1h has a BH-significant negative gross. A rule that requires BH-significant gross for both B and D would give 1 B, 1-2 D and the rest C/U.

N23 4h's gross edge is not long drift (shorts gross +0.074, t 2.2), and it was larger in the last 12 months (net +0.058, n 425, tf bars). It still cannot be verified by 12/31; this only supports keeping it as a logged rule account.
limits: The live sample is 4.8 days in a quiet, mostly falling market. At 4h every cell has at most 5 every-signal outcomes, and the 4h total is 55 outcomes in 20 clusters, so per-cell live inference at 4h is impossible and at 1h very weak (n at most 59).

v3a has no live_bars. Its every-signal R combines exact entered-trade R with skipped-shadow R rebuilt from ROE using the tier-walk leverage. That leverage was reproduced for 95.7% of entered trades, and R is exact when it matches. 570 v3a shadows had no R (unresolved or not entered) and are excluded. The shadows used Binance final klines, while the entered trades used live fills.
Live replays still open at the run end are excluded from mean R (censoring). At 4h this is 30-60% of traded signals and biases the live 4h mean upward (censoring_check.csv).

The 5-year simulation is my copy of research/strategy_profiles/profiles.py::_scan, run on the signal-timeframe bars of the locked Binance signal cache. On a bar touching both stop and target it assumes the stop first. Funding is a constant 0.01%/8h, paid by both sides. Brackets are inferred from live trades. It uses only the quality_v1 'normal' group (30x, else 20x): strength-based 40/50x is not modeled. Every signal runs alone on $5,000; no account path, one-position limit or skipping. The cache ends 2026-09-30, so 5-year and live periods do not overlap. As a sanity check, my simulation agrees with the reference profiles (Spearman 0.87 over 55 cells).

The 5-year HTF states use the bot's own regime classifier (paperbot.context.regime) and simple momentum/EMA states on closed 1h/4h bars. same_pos uses the simulated 1h/4h exit of the latest sized signal, which only approximates a one-position rule account's real position. Live HTF states have warm-up gaps: in v3b (17h) the 4h momentum state was unavailable, and v3a prices are approximated from signal reference prices and fills.

Multiple testing: 20 pooled contrasts (10 definitions x 2 timeframes) per window are shown without correction; the per-strategy scan (505 cells with at least 30 per group) used BH, with 2 survivors and neither replicated in CF at t>2. The 72-cell grades use BH only for the 5-year gross test. The grading rule was written after seeing the per-timeframe aggregates but before reading per-cell results. N23_HA_ST 4h misses it by t 0.0004 and is flagged rather than regraded.

Cluster choices (run x 4h block live, UTC day for 5 years) may not capture all dependence, such as multi-day regimes. Live bootstrap CIs with 3-4 clusters, common at 4h and in v3b, are unreliable and should be read as descriptive.

Exit what-ifs (fy_exits.py) charge taker fee plus slippage on take-profit exits, which is conservative, and use an approximate liquidation price, which matters only on liquidation gaps. The 15m/30m rows use a 60k-signal sample per coin.

Nothing here measures what the AI's discretion (early take-profit, skips, near-signal entries, event reactions) would add. The data only show that the rule signals plus 1h/4h states carry no edge for the AI to amplify.
The DeepSeek ds200 1h/4h cells are outside this lens and were not graded.

findings.claim: No DeepSeek definition earns a dedicated AI trader at 15m or 30m. Nothing survives multiple testing in the live every-signal replay, and every 15m/30m cell is negative after costs in the 5-year test.
findings.evidence: Live (v4, 1.50 days, out/cards_deepseek.csv from cards.py + grade.py): 61 testable cells (>=10 replayed trades and >=8 one-hour clusters; 31 at 15m, 20 at 30m, 10 at 1h). 0 of them have BH q<=0.10 for mean R>0. The smallest raw one-sided cluster-t p is 0.137 (F16_FIB500@15m, +0.29R, n13). 5-year (research/deepseek200/out/results.csv): all 88 definition x tf cells at 15m and 30m have negative pooled net mean (periods 1+2) under both PREREG exits. Best is -0.083%/trade at 15m and -0.076% at 30m, both F15_OPEN0930. 0/342 candidates. Grades over the 88 15m/30m cards: A 0, W 1 (F9_IFVG@15m), C 49, D 13, X 16, N 9.
findings.implication: Do not use AI-trader budget on DeepSeek definitions as 12/31 candidates. Keep all 44 as cost-free rule accounts. If DeepSeek gets any AI slot, it is an exploratory slot outside the judged set (see DS14).

Min one-sided p(mean>0) is 0.1366 (F16_FIB500@15m, +0.286R, n13). Min BH q(>0) is 1.0. v2_5y.py on research/deepseek200/out/results.csv: all 88 config rows at 15m and all 88 at 30m have mean12 < 0. findings.claim: The v4 live window is essentially one directional move, so per-definition live results mostly measure how short-heavy a definition was during the 10/07 sell-off, not skill.
findings.evidence: ds200 replay (replay_signals.csv; split at the run midpoint 10/06 21:37 KST). 15m first half: longs -0.37R (n296), shorts -0.20R (n350). Second half: longs -0.86R (n234), shorts +1.27R (n240). 30m second half: longs -0.90R, shorts +0.91R. Across the 51 testable 15m/30m cells, long share vs mean R has Spearman -0.45 (p 0.0008). Cell mean R in the first half vs the second half has Spearman -0.59 at 15m (n31, p<0.001), -0.41 at 30m (n20, p 0.07) and -0.55 over all testable cells (n59) (out/diagnostics.csv, halves.csv). Equal-weight 6 coins fell 2.6% in v4 (market_backdrop.csv).
findings.implication: Never rank DeepSeek (or any) strategies for AI slots on the v4 leaderboard. Use side-balanced R and R vs same-moment peers. The AI's direction calls in its first weeks will be scored in whatever regime comes next, and a single trend can flip any ranking.

verification.recomputed: v3_halves.py: midpoint 10/06 21:37 KST. 15m H1: longs -0.366 (n296), shorts -0.198 (n350). 15m H2: longs -0.859 (n234), shorts +1.273 (n240). 30m H2: -0.897 / +0.905. v4_cells.py: long share vs mean R rho -0.455 (n51, p 0.0008); with the 9 merged children removed, -0.41 (p 0.008). H1 vs H2 rho: 15m -0.592 (p 0.0004), 30m -0.408 (p 0.074), all cells -0.56 (n61). v5_market.py (live_bars, equal-weight log return): H1 +0.31%, H2 -2.94%, total -2.64%. Most of the drop came between 10/07 09:35 and 12:35 KST (-0.86% to -3.03%). n-weighted R2 of cell mean on long share: 0.14 at 15m, 0.28 at 30m. After removing what side composition predicts, the H1 vs H2 rho is still -0.40 (p 0.026).
verification.note: The numbers reproduce, but two parts of the framing do not hold. (1) The window was not one directional move. The first 30 h were flat chop in which BOTH sides lost (15m longs -0.37R, shorts -0.20R), followed by one sharp sell-off. (2) 'Mostly measures how short-heavy' is overstated: long share explains 14-28% of the cross-cell variance. The implication still stands: do not rank on the v4 leaderboard.

findings.claim: Costs, not signal direction, decide the 15m result. ds200 15m signals were gross-positive in this window but lost after fees, funding and slippage. In the 5-year, gross is already negative at every timeframe.
findings.evidence: tf_summary_ds.csv (every replayed signal; cluster-t 95% CI with one-hour clusters). 15m: n1120, mean -0.065R [-0.21,+0.08], gross +0.18R, fees+funding 0.177R, slippage 0.071R, median stop 0.60% of price. 30m: n586, -0.132R [-0.26,-0.01], gross +0.04R, costs 0.12+0.05R. 1h: n330, -0.112R [-0.23,+0.00]. Net per trade on notional: 15m -0.061%, 30m -0.115%, 1h -0.150%, 4h -0.233%. That is the same order as the 5-year net (15m -0.151% period 1 / -0.141% period 2, 30m -0.160/-0.149). 5-year gross before costs: 15m -0.047%, 30m -0.053%. At 30x, a 0.14% round trip is about 4.2% ROE per trade.
findings.implication: A DeepSeek AI trader at 15m must add about +0.25R per trade over the rule just to break even (+0.17R at 30m). Exits, skipping and cheaper entries would have to create that. Signal choice alone has never shown it.

verification.recomputed: v1_tf.py with my own R and cost columns. 15m: n1120, mean -0.0652, 1h-cluster CI [-0.214,+0.084], gross +0.183, fees+funding 0.177R, slippage 0.071R, median stop 0.600%. 30m: -0.132 [-0.258,-0.007], gross +0.039, costs 0.122+0.049. 1h: -0.112 [-0.227,+0.004]. Net per notional: 15m -0.061%, 30m -0.115%, 1h -0.150%, 4h -0.233%. 5-year trade-weighted: 15m net P1 -0.151% / P2 -0.141% / gross P1 -0.047%; 30m -0.160 / -0.149 / -0.053. With 4h clusters, 15m CI is [-0.36,+0.23] (deff 9.35) and 30m CI is [-0.28,+0.015], which is no longer significant. Including the 52/34/38 unresolved signals marked to the last close: 15m -0.077, 30m -0.142, 1h -0.125. Unique signals: 15m -0.080, 30m -0.108.
verification.note: All the numbers reproduce. The break-even sentence is mis-stated. +0.25R / +0.17R is the round-trip cost in R. It is the needed gross edge only if the rule's gross is zero. In this window the AI had to beat the rule by +0.065R (15m) / +0.13R (30m). Under the 5-year gross (about -0.08R at a 0.6% stop) it needs about +0.33R. The cost in R also depends on volatility: 0.25R comes from a quiet market (15m stop 0.60%). Calling 30m significantly negative depends on using 1h clusters.

findings.claim: The one-position account results (the dashboard leaderboard) are a poor estimate even of the window's own every-signal result.
findings.evidence: 141 ds200 accounts traded (median 3 trades, max 12). 52 were profitable, and 27 of those turn negative without their best trade (luck_concentration.csv). Account total: 563 trades, -$37,091, mean R -0.201. Examples: F12_MSS@15m is the 3rd-best account (+$1,229 on 4 trades) but its every-signal replay is -0.10R (n24). F3_HHHL@15m account is -$1,715 (6 trades, -1.20R) but its replay is +0.20R (n41). Spearman of account mean R vs replay mean R: 0.42 at 15m, 0.65 at 30m (diagnostics.csv).
findings.implication: Judge strategies on every-signal replays or shadow books, never on single-position account PnL. The AI trader is also one-position, so its realized R will be even noisier than the replay.

verification.recomputed: v6_accounts.py and v6b.py. 141 of 171 accounts traded (median 3, max 12). 563 trades, -$37,091.1, mean R -0.2012. 52 profitable. 27 have pnl_ex_best <= 0, but 13 of those are single-trade accounts (ex-best pnl exactly 0); only 14 turn strictly negative. F12_MSS@15m: 3rd by pnl, +$1,228.7, n4, replay -0.103 (n24). F3_HHHL@15m: -$1,714.6, -1.204R, replay +0.196 (n41). Account mean R vs replay mean R on testable cells: 15m 0.346 (n31, p 0.057), 30m 0.729 (n20). On all cells with an account: 0.61 / 0.57. findings.claim: DeepSeek direction skill against a coin flip at the same moments is weak, and about a third of it is market drift.
findings.evidence: Pipeline side-flip (coinflip_sideflip.csv): ds200 15m excess +0.073R (1107 pairs, 35 clusters, cluster p 0.024); 30m -0.028R; all timeframes +0.032R (p 0.14); no definition x tf cell significant after BH. Drift-neutral version (equal-weight long and short excess, sideflip_drift.py -> out/sideflip_drift.csv): 15m +0.049R (p 0.08), 30m -0.023R (p 0.68), all +0.028R (p 0.17). For comparison, the core 36 at 15m: +0.089R raw but -0.084R drift-neutral. The 5-year gross per trade is negative, so the 5-year shows no direction skill either.
findings.implication: There is no reliable directional edge for an AI to amplify. The 15m drift-neutral +0.05R (p 0.08, one of 8 kind x tf looks) is a reason to keep recording, not a reason to choose.

verification.recomputed: v7_sideflip.py. Pipeline table: ds200 15m +0.0728 (1107 pairs, 35 clusters, p 0.0236), 30m -0.0277, all +0.0319 (p 0.138). ds200 strategy_tf min BH q 0.61. My sign-flip test with 20k draws: 15m drift-neutral +0.0492 (p 0.074 with 1h clusters, 0.151 with 4h clusters), 30m -0.0228 (p 0.69), all +0.0284 (p 0.17). findings.claim: The 44 definitions are about 35 distinct streams. Nine definitions duplicate or nest inside a parent, and two definitions emit the same stream on several timeframes.
findings.evidence: dup_pairs_ds.csv (signal level: bar_close, coin, side). F5_BOX_HTF = F5_BOX (identical 10/10 at 15m, 4/4 at 30m). F13_RAID_PD is inside F11_RAID (36/38 at 15m, identical at 1h and 4h). F11_TSOUP: 22 of 25 signals at 15m are also F11_RAID signals. F17_Z_HL is inside F17_Z (47/50 at 15m, identical at 1h and 4h). F12_MSS_DISP is inside F12_MSS (12/12 at 15m). F13_FVG_PD and F10_M2022 are inside F9_FVG. F16_FIB618 is inside F10_OTE (14/14 at 15m, identical at 4h). 75% of F7_RF_ONLY signals are F7_RF_TRIPLE signals. F15_OPEN0000 emits one identical stream at 15m/30m/1h (12/12), and F15_OPEN0930 is identical at 15m/30m; only the ATR stop differs. The F1 divergences overlap 60-80%. Use the child filters (HTF ADX, premium/discount, half-life, displacement) as context the AI sees, not as separate traders. Count families, not definitions, when correcting for multiple testing.

findings.claim: Between-definition differences in the 5-year do not persist across periods, so 'least-bad in the 5-year' is also a weak selector.
findings.evidence: diagnostics.csv: Spearman of period-1 vs period-2 net mean across the 44 definitions (exit picked on period 1): 15m -0.14 (p 0.36), 30m -0.15 (p 0.34), 1h +0.15, 4h -0.03. Period 1 vs period 3: +0.12 / +0.09 / +0.07 / -0.04. Live replay mean R vs 5-year rank: 15m +0.02 (p 0.90), 30m +0.33 (p 0.15). The 15m 5-year range across definitions is only -0.189% to -0.083% per trade.
findings.implication: Choosing DeepSeek AI traders by 5-year rank is close to random. If slots are given, choose them by families, signal frequency (learning value) and non-duplication, and say openly that the choice is exploratory.

verification.note: Reproduces. One exception matters for DS14: F6_VWAP_CROSS X2 ranks 11/3/6 at 15m and 14/1/5 at 30m across periods 1/2/3. That consistency, not its pooled rank, is the only 5-year support for F6.
