findings.claim: Leverage under the house rules: 40-50x is mostly not executable for DeepSeek signals. With the ROE-based ladder, lower leverage (a later first lock) gave better R in this window, on both sides. Leverage changes the exit, not only the size.
findings.evidence: levreplay.py (every ds200 signal at fixed L with margin = L% through the repo engine; parity at 30x is exact on 1,996 signals) -> lev_replay_summary.csv. Entered share at 15m: 10-30x 100%, 40x 90%, 50x 21%. At 30m: 30x 99.7%, 40x 40%, 50x 0%. At 1h: 30x 83%, 40x+ 0%. At 50x the rejections cite loss above 15% of equity (885), bracket (753) and liquidation buffer (405). Mean R including marked open trades: 15m 10x +0.029, 20x -0.073, 30x -0.077, 40x -0.200 (on its 90%). 30m 10x -0.041, 20x -0.123, 30x -0.140, 40x -0.227. Side split at 15m, 10x vs 30x: longs -0.89 vs -0.55, shorts +0.84 vs +0.35; side-balanced 10x is still +0.08R better (30m +0.10R). Mechanism: the first lock triggers at +12% ROE, i.e. 0.12/L of price. At 30x that is about 0.9R at 15m. The nightly d3 lev10 what-if shows the opposite sign (-0.23R at 15m); it drops 75 slow unresolved ds200 rows. On account-entered, resolved-only pairs the replay gives +0.002R at 15m.
findings.implication: Define the AI's exits in price/R, as design 3-4/4-1 intends, not in ROE. Otherwise a 'confidence -> 50x' rule silently tightens the take-profit. Under margin = leverage%, 50x cannot take most 15m and no 30m DeepSeek signals. Prefer the design's risk-per-stop sizing (4-3), where leverage is an output. Whether a later lock really helps is regime-dependent and was not tested out of sample.

verification.recomputed: Own fixed-leverage replay (v9_levrep.py, my_lev.csv; parity with the pipeline at 30x: 1996 signals, max dR 0). Entered share: 15m 100/100/100/90/20.7%; 30m 30x 99.7%, 40x 40.3%, 50x 0; 1h 30x 83.4%, 40x 0. 50x rejection texts: 885 '15%', 753 bracket, 405 'too close to liq'. R incl. marked: 15m 10x +0.029, 20x -0.072, 30x -0.077, 40x -0.200; 30m -0.041 / -0.123 / -0.140 / -0.227. Paired 10x-30x at 15m: +0.105R; CI [-0.10,+0.31] with 1h clusters, [-0.27,+0.48] with 4h clusters. Longs -0.336, shorts +0.498. H1 side-balanced -0.279 (10x worse), H2 +0.543. 30m: H1 -0.093, H2 +0.330. Account-entered resolved pairs at 15m: +0.002 (n256), split H1 -0.235 (n161), H2 +0.403 (n95). v12: on the d3's own 213 15m signals, my replay (all resolved) gives 10x worse by -0.103; dropping the 17 d3-unresolved rows gives -0.232. Lock trigger in R at 30x: 0.90 (15m), 0.64 (30m). 5-year research/levstop/out/levstop.json (core 36, house ladder, 2 ATR, same signals at every leverage), return per notional: 15m 10x -0.1415%, 20x -0.1421%, 30x -0.1424%, 40x -0.1474%, 50x -0.1587%; 30m 10x -0.1534% vs 30x -0.1533%; 1h -0.157 vs -0.175%.
verification.note: 'Better on both sides' is false: longs were worse at 10x. The gain is not significant and flips sign between halves; it comes entirely from shorts in the H2 sell-off. The d3 sign difference is mostly which signals it covers (77% H1), not only the dropped rows. The analyst says 'not tested out of sample', but the 5-year levstop study shows a later lock is worth about 0 at 15m/30m, while 40-50x is clearly worse. The implication still stands: define exits in price/R and do not let a 'confidence -> 50x' rule move the take-profit.

findings.claim: Near-signal limit entries do not fix the cost problem. Fills are adversely selected.
findings.evidence: d3 limit what-if (0.25 ATR better, one bar; 10/06 signals only) matched to the replay (d3check.py -> d3_checks_ds_limitR.csv). Fill rate 65% at 15m and 58% at 30m. Filled signals were the losers at market (-0.38R / -0.40R), and the unfilled ones ran away (+0.26R / +0.30R). Per signal, limit vs market: 15m -0.141 vs -0.156R (+0.015R), 30m -0.096 vs -0.104R (+0.008R). Separately, the d3 skipped shadows equal the replay exactly on 1,016 matched ds200 signals (abs diff 0), so they are not independent evidence.
findings.implication: Do not count on AI 'near-signal' or limit entries to close the 0.17-0.25R cost gap. Maker fees (about 0.02%) would help more than price improvement. Measure this as its own shadow before trusting it.

verification.recomputed: v11_d3.py, d3_shadows limit rows for ds200 matched to the replay. Fill rate among matched TRADED signals: 69% at 15m (n999), 62% at 30m (n509). The analyst's 65% / 58% exist only after dropping 128 / 50 filled-but-unresolved rows. Market R of filled vs unfilled: 15m -0.339 vs +0.255; 30m -0.426 vs +0.298. Per signal (resolved fills + unfilled at 0): 15m limit -0.141 vs market -0.156; 30m -0.096 vs -0.104. 1h: +0.012 vs -0.067. Per filled trade the limit price is better by about +0.16R. Skipped shadows vs replay: 1016 matched, max |ROE diff| 6.6e-14.
verification.note: The conclusion (adverse selection cancels the price improvement) reproduces. The fill rates are understated, and dropping the slow unresolved fills biases the comparison by an unknown amount. One night of signals only (10/06, mostly H1).

findings.claim: Statistical power: one DeepSeek cell needs months to show a realistic edge. By the November promotion only edges of about 0.2R or more could be seen, before multiple-testing correction.
findings.evidence: Per-trade sd of R: 1.41 at 15m, 1.00 at 30m. Median cell cluster SE 0.27R / 0.25R (design effect 1.15 / 1.44). Median MDE80 about 0.74R / 0.71R in this window. Detecting +0.1R at 80% power needs about 1,400 signals at 15m (~78 days at the median cell's 18 signals/day) and about 900 at 30m (~79 days). Detecting +0.2R needs about 350 / 220 signals (~20 days). The AI trader takes one position at a time, so it sees far fewer trades than signals.
findings.implication: With about 30 traders judged at once, only large AI value-added (well above +0.2R per trade) can be confirmed by 12/31. Plan the AI evaluation on shadow every-signal books plus R-based paired comparisons (AI vs the rule on the same signals), not on account PnL.

verification.recomputed: v13_power.py. Pooled sd: 1.406 (15m), 0.998 (30m). Median cell cluster SE: 0.255 / 0.252. Median deff with 1h clusters 1.32 / 1.52, with 4h clusters 1.74 / 2.00. Tf-level deff at 15m: 3.05 (1h clusters), 9.35 (4h). Median MDE80: 0.71 / 0.71 two-sided. Signals needed for +0.1R (one-sided, 1h deff): 1,615 (about 90 days at 18/day) and 939 (about 78 days). Two-sided with 4h deff: 2,703 (about 150 days) and 1,563 (about 131 days). For +0.2R: 404-676 (22-38 days) and 235-391 (20-33 days).
verification.note: The direction is right. The analyst's sample sizes use a one-sided alpha and the small 1h-cluster deff, so they are optimistic. A +0.1R per-cell edge cannot be confirmed by 12/31 even per cell. Across correlated cells, a cohort test has far fewer effective observations (deff 3-9).

findings.claim: If the owners still want DeepSeek exposure in the AI cohort, at most 1-2 exploratory family traders are defensible, and none as a 12/31 candidate.
findings.evidence: Family x tf (unique signals, family_tf.csv / family_verdict.csv). F6 VWAP: 15m +0.08R (n114, CI [-0.45,+0.61]), ~76 unique signals/day. Its 5-year is the least negative among frequent families: VWAP_CROSS ranks 4/44 at 15m (-0.114%) and 2/44 at 30m (-0.096%), and F6_VWAP_CROSS@1h is the only W outside 15m (+0.15R, n34). F9 FVG/OB: 15m -0.01R (n108); F9_IFVG@15m is the only W at 15m (+0.06R, n26, side-balanced +0.09, vs peers +0.15, 5-year rank 8/44). F1 divergence: 15m +0.24R (n38, CI [-0.44,+0.93], drift-neutral side-flip +0.28, p 0.19), but its 15m 5-year ranks are poor (30, 36 and 5 of 44) and its only 5-year support is at 4h. Avoid F4, F11/F13 raid, F14_SMT (15m -0.14R n112; 30m -0.29R n39), F16, F17 and F8.
findings.implication: Recommended: zero DeepSeek AI traders in the judged cohort. If one or two exploratory slots are wanted, use one trader per family (F6 VWAP, then F9 FVG), deduplicated, Sonnet only, outside the 12/31 set. Their purpose is to learn whether AI exits and skipping can recover the 0.2R cost gap, not to find the strategy to take to real money.

verification.note: The numbers reproduce, and the low-confidence recommendation is reasonable. The live support for F6 at 15m is purely the H2 move, and F6 is negative at 30m. The real basis is F6's consistent 5-year period ranks, which DS14 does not state (and DS8 would otherwise undercut). F9_IFVG's W rests on margins near zero.

strategy_note_problems: F7_RF_ONLY@15m/30m and F11_TSOUP@30m (and @1h) are graded X although the PREREG does not nest them and their live overlap (75%, 62%, 60%) is below grade.py's own merge rule (at least 85%). Graded on their own numbers they would be D at 15m (F7_RF_ONLY: -0.072R, 5-year -0.151 in the worst third), D for F11_TSOUP@15m and @30m, and C for F7_RF_ONLY@30m. No AI decision changes, but the X label hides evidence (verify/v16_grades.py).

Folding children into parents hides the only supported part of a family. F12_MSS_DISP@15m (+0.36R, n12, G8, side-balanced +0.25, 5-year -0.126% rank 10/44) is marked X under F12_MSS@15m, which is graded D (-0.10R, 5-year rank 40/44). F9_FVG's children are also better in the 5-year (F13_FVG_PD -0.108, F10_M2022 -0.097 vs -0.132).
F4_PULL@15m: the note 'significantly negative: BH q(mean<0) 0.035' holds only with 1h clusters. With 4h clusters (8 clusters) p is 0.021 and BH q 0.35. Only F4_PULL@30m (q 0.005) is robust.

F9_IFVG@15m (the only W): every W condition passes by a thin margin (ex-best +0.014, mean +0.057). It is +0.10R in H1 (n20) and -0.09R in H2 (n6), its fixed-10x replay is -0.25R, and its 5-year period-3 rank is 31-32/44. The note's 'thin margins' is right, but the H2 sign and the P3 rank should be stated.

The lev10/30 columns are my fixed-leverage replay including open trades marked to the last close, and they can differ a lot from the replay mean shown next to them (F2_DEMARK@15m: lev30 -0.03 vs replay -0.12; F3_HHHL@15m: +0.11 vs +0.20). The notes do not say the lev values include marked open trades.
D grades on 2-3 clusters rest almost entirely on the 5-year line. Examples: F15_OPEN0000@15m (n8, G2) and F15_LON_BRK@15m (n6, G3). The notes cite the replay R as if it were evidence.
qPos 1.00 appears in every testable note. It carries no information and can read as if each cell were tested.

Sampled numbers I recomputed match the notes to the second decimal: F1_RSI_DIV, F1_MOM_DIV, F1_PVT_DIV, F3_HHHL, F4_PULL, F6_VWAP_CROSS, F6_VWAP_FAIL, F9_IFVG, F12_MSS, F16_FIB500 at 15m; F12_MSS, F9_BREAKER, F9_FVG, F3_BOS, F14_SMT, F11_RAID at 30m. That covers sig/d, account n and R, replay n/G/mean/CI, side-balanced, vs peers, ex-best, long share, gross, flip, lev10/30, and 5-year value and rank. The halves claims match (F6_VWAP_FAIL@15m -0.30/+0.69, F12_MSS@30m -0.26/+1.26, F16_FIB500@15m positive in both halves).
verifier_missed: Out-of-sample leverage/lock evidence already exists: research/levstop/out/levstop.json (5-year, core 36, house ladder, 2 ATR, the same signals at every fixed leverage). Return per notional at 15m: 10x -0.1415%, 20x -0.1421%, 30x -0.1424%, 40x -0.1474%, 50x -0.1587%. At 30m 10x and 30x are equal (-0.153%). At 1h: -0.157% vs -0.175%. So a later lock gains about nothing at 15m/30m, and 40-50x is worse. This contradicts reading the live +0.10R at 10x as structural.

The v4 window is chop followed by one sell-off. In the chop half, ds200 15m lost -0.275R per signal (n646) on BOTH sides, as did the core 36 (15m H1 longs -0.31, shorts -0.25). The house exits lose about 0.25-0.3R per trade in quiet chop whatever the direction. 'Skip in chop' is therefore the most concrete testable AI value-add, and it should be scored by regime.

The one-position selection is biased, not only noisy, at 15m. Signals the ds200 accounts entered averaged -0.288R (n259); signals skipped while in position averaged +0.011R (n731). The difference is -0.29R, cluster-bootstrap CI [-0.47,-0.10]. The core 36 at 15m show the same sign (-0.18 vs +0.06). There is no gap at 30m/1h. The AI trader is also one-position, so 'which signal to take when flat' needs its own shadow measurement (verify/v17_misc.py, v18_score.py).

Cluster choice changes conclusions. The analyst's primary clusters are 1h, shorter than the 168-minute mean 15m hold, and coins move together. Tf-level deff at 15m is 3.05 with 1h clusters and 9.35 with 4h clusters. With 4h clusters the 30m every-signal CI is [-0.28,+0.015] and F4_PULL@15m loses BH significance. The headline intervals should be reported with 4h or daily clusters as well.

Unresolved-row bias: 52/34/38/16 replayed ds200 signals were still open at the end, with mean marked R -0.33/-0.31/-0.25/-0.07. Including them gives 15m -0.077, 30m -0.142, 1h -0.125 (vs -0.065/-0.132/-0.112). The DS3 headline drops them.

The 4h DeepSeek cells that DS9 says to 'watch' are mostly not observable live. 59/126 ds200 4h signals were REJECTED_SIZING ('stop too close to liq' at 30x/20x), including 8/16 of F4_PULL@4h. F4_PULL_RSI, F10_M2022 and F5_BOX_RSI had 0 live 4h signals, and F1_RSI_DIV / F1_PVT_DIV had 1 each. Rule accounts cannot test these cells within months; a no-sizing shadow is needed.

The RESULTS_DEEPSEEK200.md stage-1 discrepancy can be resolved from research/library/lib.py select(): results.csv is correct (4h F5_BOX X2 and 4h F13_FVG_PD X5 pass stage 1). The md lists the two all-three-periods-positive rows instead.

The cost of 0.25R per trade at 15m reflects the current quiet market (median 15m stop 0.60%). Cost in R falls as ATR rises, so the break-even gap the AI must close is regime-dependent, not a constant. The 5-year cost per notional (about 0.104%) is the stable quantity.
About 23-31% of replayed signals are the accounts' own trades. Any account-vs-replay comparison (DS4) is inflated by that overlap. Excluding them, the 15m correlation is about 0 (rho -0.11).

The DS14 case for F6 rests on period-consistent 5-year ranks (F6_VWAP_CROSS X2: 11/3/6 at 15m, 14/1/5 at 30m), which the lens never reports. Its live 15m result is entirely H2 (+0.77 vs -0.40 in H1), F6 at 30m is -0.125R (n86), and even its 5-year gross is negative (-0.021% P1).
limits: One run, one regime: ds200 exists only in v4 (1.50 days, 10/06 03:35 to 10/07 15:40 KST), a falling market (6-coin equal weight -2.6%), with one sell-off doing most of the work. There is no v3a/v3b out-of-sample run for DeepSeek. The within-run halves anti-correlate (Spearman -0.59 at 15m), so the window cannot rank definitions.

Per-cell samples are tiny: median 3 account trades and 9-25 replayed signals for most 15m/30m cells. The median minimum detectable effect at 80% power is about 0.7R per cell, and the cluster counts (one-hour blocks, 2-36 per cell) are small. Cluster-t intervals with few clusters are unreliable, and some cells (F11_PO3@1h, F15 daily signals) show artificially tight CIs.

Primary replay means use resolved trades only. 140 of 2,286 ds200 signals were still open at the end and are only in the marked sensitivity (rp_mean_R_incl_marked). 59 4h signals were rejected by sizing at 20x.

The nightly d3 skipped shadows equal the replay exactly on 1,016 matched signals, so they are not independent evidence. The d3 per-trade variants (lev/lock/tp) pair only resolved rows within the night's horizon and are biased. Their lev10 sign at 15m contradicts the full replay.

The 5-year reference uses the PREREG exits (X5_TRAIL2 / X2_SL15_TP3), unlevered % per trade, next-bar-open entry, and one position per (config, coin). The live accounts use house exits (2 ATR stop + ROE ladder at 30x/20x). Comparisons are therefore only in % per trade on notional. 5-year per_day counts trades, not signals.
The RESULTS_DEEPSEEK200.md vs results.csv stage-1 disagreement is reported, not resolved. Either way stage 2 = 0 and candidates = 0.

The grade rubric (testable = n>=10 and >=8 clusters; W needs side-balanced, ex-best, vs-peers >0 and 5-year >= tf median; D = BH-negative or negative live with a worst-third 5-year) was fixed after seeing the overall picture and is not pre-registered. It is mechanical, but its thresholds are judgment calls. No threshold variant produces a BH-positive cell.
Side-balanced R needs >=3 trades per side and is missing for many cells. R vs peers uses other core-36 + ds200 signals in the same tf/side/4h block, which is not a random benchmark.

The leverage replay uses margin = leverage %, the house sizing limits (15% max loss at stop, 1 ATR liquidation buffer) and the pipeline's inferred brackets and funding. The AI design's 4-3 risk-per-stop sizing would admit different signals. The 'later lock is better' result comes from one trending window and is untested elsewhere.

Nothing here measures what an AI trader adds (skipping, early exits, switching, near-signal entries). Rule-bot data can only bound what the AI must add (about +0.25R/trade at 15m, +0.17R at 30m, to cover costs).

FORWARD_PREREG (DeepSeek shadow forward test, PREREG exits, no performance looks before 11/04) was not touched. Only the house-exit paper accounts were analysed. Choosing AI traders from these data is an extra look that the forward test's N=498 does not count.
The F14_SMT live results cover 5 coins (BTC is only the reference). The F15 daily-session definitions produce one decision per coin per day, so 1.5 days gives 1-2 independent events.

findings.claim: The house exit is not the main loss source at 15m/30m: on every submitted signal the gross R is about zero and the round-trip cost explains all of the 15m loss and about 80% of the 30m loss. Exits only reshape the distribution: across 34 exits that leave sizing unchanged, no exit is positive in both runs at 15m or 30m.
findings.evidence: exitlab re-run, every house-exit signal of v3b + v4, base = live rule, open positions marked at 10/07 15:40 KST (exitlab_paired.csv / exitlab_base_levels.csv, scripts analyze_exitlab.py and show_levels.py). Net R = gross R minus cost R: 15m n 2,477: -0.106 = +0.062 - 0.168. 30m n 1,277: -0.147 = -0.030 - 0.117. 1h n 780: -0.136 = -0.053 - 0.083. 4h n 112: -0.044 = +0.001 - 0.046. House payoff at 15m: 52.6% wins, average win +0.87R, average loss -1.19R, so breakeven needs 57.8% wins. At 30m: 57.6% wins, +0.56R / -1.10R, breakeven 66.4%. Over 34 exits the pooled 15m mean ranges from -0.225R (tp1.5R) to +0.059R (RL2_1). Best exit in hindsight at 15m: v3b -0.289R (be0.5_tp1), v4 +0.200R (RL2_1). At 30m: v3b -0.159R, v4 +0.030R. The side-flipped (coin-flip) entries lose about as much (15m -0.193R, 30m -0.103R).
findings.implication: Do not expect an exit or custom value to turn a 15m/30m strategy positive. The AI trader has to supply direction or timing edge larger than about 0.17R (15m) or 0.12R (30m) per trade. Exit work should aim at not destroying edge, not at creating it.

verification.recomputed: x1_levels.py on exitlab_rows (cross-checked against my own minute-bar simulator mysim.py, which matches exitlab exactly on every zero-funding trade). Reproduced exactly: 15m n 2,477 net -0.106 = gross(fee-only) +0.062 - 0.168; 30m -0.147 = -0.030 - 0.117; 1h -0.136 = -0.053 - 0.083; 4h -0.044 = +0.001 - 0.046. 15m: 52.6% wins, +0.867/-1.185, breakeven 57.8%. 30m: 57.6%, +0.556/-1.101, breakeven 66.4%. Flipped side: 15m -0.193, 30m -0.103. Exit range at 15m: -0.225 (tp1.5R) to +0.059 (RL2_1). Best per run: v3b -0.289, v4 +0.200; 30m -0.159 / +0.030. No exit is positive in both runs at 15m or 30m (x1_exits.py). The corrections: (a) their 'cost' is fees plus funding only. Slippage (0.02% per side, 0.04% round trip) stays inside their 'gross'. Full cost is 0.236R at 15m (0.168 fees + 0.067 slippage), 0.164R at 30m, 0.116R at 1h and 0.064R at 4h. Gross before all costs: 15m +0.130, 30m +0.016, 1h -0.020. So cost covers more than 100% of the 30m loss, not about 80%. (b) n includes the coin-flip accounts' signals (53 at 15m, 18 at 30m). About 47% of the rows repeat the same coin/bar/side trade from another strategy: 15m has 1,304 unique trades of 2,477, 30m 680 of 1,277, 1h 372 of 780 (dups.py). Deduplicated, the 15m net is -0.154. (c) The runs differ a lot: 15m net v3b -0.373 vs v4 -0.053. Fee-only gross v3b -0.235 vs v4 +0.121. (d) The 15m net CI with 6h blocks is [-0.317, +0.147].
verification.note: The core message stands: exits reshape outcomes and cost dominates. But the hurdle the AI must clear is about 0.24R at 15m and 0.16R at 30m (modeled taker fees plus slippage), not 0.17/0.12R. 'n 2,477' overstates the independent information by about 2x.

findings.claim: The 'lev10 +0.26R / lock30 +0.14R' headline is the ROE ladder's geometry acting during one trending regime, not a robust custom value. The ladder locks net ROE, so its price trigger is 0.12/L + 0.14% and shrinks as leverage L grows. In R units of the 2 ATR stop it arms early and trails very tightly. lev10 and lock30 simply arm later. The effect has the opposite sign across runs.
findings.evidence: Ladder geometry (lev_risk.csv, ladder_geometry.csv), in R at the median stop. 15m (stop 0.62%): trigger at 10x / 20x / 30x / 50x = 2.16 / 1.19 / 0.87 / 0.61R; at 30x the lock is 0.76R and the trail gap after arming is 0.11-0.38R. 1h at 30x: trigger 0.43R, lock 0.38R, trail 0.05-0.19R. The 0.14% cost is 37% of the trigger distance at 50x and 10% at 10x. In R, lev10 = geo10 and lev20m20 = geo20 in every run and tf, so leverage changes R only through the ladder. lev10 vs house at 15m: v3a (nightly shadows, base mostly 50x) +0.460 [0.180, 0.776], n 296. v3b (re-run) -0.230 [-0.397, -0.083], n 407. v4 +0.167 [-0.050, 0.403], n 2,070. Pooled v3b+v4 +0.101 [-0.075, 0.286], q 0.47. lock30 at 15m: +0.210 / -0.233 / +0.008. The pooled headline (+0.26R) is dominated by v3a, which has 1,300 of the 1,462 pairs, 717 of them at 5m (d3_paired_by_run_tf.csv, master_variant_tf.csv).
findings.implication: Do not adopt lev10 or lock30 as custom values on this evidence. The real lesson is structural: an ROE ladder ties the exit to leverage. Under 'leverage by AI confidence' the most confident trades would get the tightest exit (0.61R trigger at 50x vs 1.19R at 20x at 15m).

verification.recomputed: x2_geo.py: median stop 0.620% at 15m. Trigger 2.16/1.19/0.87/0.71/0.61R at 10/20/30/40/50x. Lock at 30x 0.76R, trail gap 0.11-0.38R. At 1h, 30x: trigger 0.43R, lock 0.38R. Cost over trigger: 0.37 (50x), 0.10 (10x). lev10 equals geo10 and lev20m20 equals geo20 on all 4,646 signals (max |dR| 5e-15). contrast.py (c_x2.csv): lev10 vs base at 15m: v3b -0.230 [1h cl -0.394, -0.083], v4 +0.167 [-0.051, 0.393], pooled +0.101 [-0.085, 0.305]. With 6h clusters the pooled CI is [-0.235, 0.424]. lock30 at 15m: -0.233 / +0.008. geo10 vs geo50 (closer to v3a's 50x base): v3b -0.267, v4 +0.255, so the sign still flips. v3a from raw d3_shadows (x2_d3.py, R = roe / (L x stop_frac)): strategy-only 15m lev10 +0.411 [0.118, 0.752] n 275. All kinds, as rb_analyze reports it: +0.460, n 296. lock30 15m: +0.177 strategy-only, +0.210 all kinds. Headline: 1,462 pairs at +0.261. Of these, v3a has 1,232 (not about 1,300) and 717 are at 5m (confirmed).
verification.note: Minor fixes. The v3a +0.460 includes the coin-flip accounts. At 15m only 49% of v3a base trades were at 50x (median 40x), so 'mostly 50x' is too strong; at 5m it was 76%. v3a holds 1,232 of the pairs, not 1,300. The AI design v2 (dated 10/07, lines 303-304) already converts the ladder to price/R at 20x geometry with bar-close updates. The structural lesson is already adopted.

findings.claim: Picking the best exit per strategy x timeframe in one period and applying it to the next period loses money against simply keeping the house exit. Weekly per-strategy exit tuning on live data would fit noise.
findings.evidence: tuning_oos_summary.csv (tuning_oos.py; the in-sample pick is the highest mean R; the out-of-sample gain is the picked exit minus the house exit). Full menu: v3b to v4, 31 cells: in-sample +0.34R, out-of-sample -0.023 [-0.132, 0.075]. v4 first half to second half, 67 cells: +0.29R in-sample, -0.092 [-0.190, 0.010] out-of-sample. Second half to first half: +0.88R in-sample, -0.210 [-0.288, -0.126] out-of-sample. The tuned exit beat the house exit out-of-sample in only 22-39% of cells. With a 5-exit menu: +0.037, -0.075 and -0.164R out-of-sample. Across the 60 graded cells the exit choice moves a cell's mean by a median of 0.53R (0.16-1.22R). 43 of 60 cells have at least one exit with mean > 0, against only 18 that are positive under the house exit.
findings.implication: Freeze one exit per strategy family for the whole 10/17 to 12/31 test. Run the weekly shadow tuning as a record only. Adopt a new exit only after a pre-registered multi-period (5-year) test, never because it won last week.

verification.recomputed: x3_tune.py (own implementation, min_n 8): v3b to v4, 31 cells, in-sample +0.340, out-of-sample -0.023 [-0.137, 0.075], 39% of cells better. v4 H1 to H2, 67 cells: +0.294 / -0.092 [-0.190, 0.007]. H2 to H1: +0.885 / -0.210 [-0.289, -0.129]. 5-exit menu: +0.037, -0.075, -0.164. With min_n 15: -0.134, -0.049, -0.217. A single global exit picked in-sample also lost out of sample: -0.050 (geo50), -0.152 (geo50), -0.293 (RL2_1). From x13_cells: exit spread median 0.53R (0.16-1.22); 43 of 60 cells have some exit > 0; 18 of 60 are positive under the house exit.
verification.note: Reproduced. Nuance: even one pooled exit chosen in-sample loses out of sample, so the failure is chasing the last regime (H1 and H2 sit on opposite sides of the 10/06 switch), not only per-cell noise. The cell bootstrap ignores that cells share time and that duplicate DeepSeek cells overlap, so the CIs are optimistic.

findings.claim: The nightly shadow pairing (unresolved rows dropped) is biased against wide exits. The rows it dropped were the wide variants' big winners. Re-running the same v4 trades to the end of the bars removes most of the apparent penalty.
findings.evidence: d3_bias_v4.csv (d3_bias.py): the same 356 / 236 / 126 v4 trades at 15m / 30m / 1h. lev10: shadow pairs -0.213 vs full re-run -0.009 at 15m (bias -0.20R); -0.160 vs +0.071 at 30m; -0.043 vs +0.124 at 1h. tp3R: -0.282 vs -0.089 (15m), -0.463 vs +0.072 (30m), -0.480 vs +0.402 (1h). lock30 at 30m: -0.116 vs +0.026. On the dropped rows the variant minus base averaged +2.13R (lev10, 15m). Validation: exitlab reproduces every resolved nightly variant row exactly (median |dROE| 0, 18 variants, validate_vs_d3.csv) and the rb_analyze replay exactly (4,236 signals, max |dROE| 2.2e-16).
findings.implication: Do not use the d3 shadow tables (or the dashboard boards built on them) to rank exits with long holds. The v3a lev10/lock30 gains are understated, not overstated. Fix the nightly job: extend the horizon, or mark open rows to market and keep them in the pairs.

verification.recomputed: x4_bias.py (v4 d3_shadows converted to R with the trades' stop_frac, matched to exitlab rows; base matches 100%). lev10: shadow pairs -0.213 vs full re-run -0.009 (15m, 356 trades); -0.160 vs +0.071 (30m); -0.043 vs +0.124 (1h). tp3R: -0.282 vs -0.089, -0.463 vs +0.072, -0.480 vs +0.402. lock30 at 30m: -0.116 vs +0.026. On the dropped rows, variant minus base: lev10 at 15m +2.127 (n 31); tp3R at 1h +0.945 (n 78). Shadow means equal the re-run means on the same pairs for lev10, tp2R, tp3R, lock30, stopw3 and timestop.
verification.note: Confirmed for v4. The statement that the v3a lev10/lock30 gains are 'understated' cannot be checked: v3a has no live_bars, and 179 of its 1,510 lev10 rows are unresolved. It is a plausible extrapolation, not a measurement.

findings.claim: Which exit wins is a time-clustered regime effect lasting about 12-24 h. The same effect appears on the side-flipped (coin-flip) entries, so it comes from the price path, not from the signals.
findings.evidence: regime_blocks_6h.csv (contrasts.py), 15m+30m signals, wide exit (geo10) minus house in 6 h blocks from 10/05 00:00 UTC: -0.17, -0.10, -0.22, -0.20, -0.48, -0.17, then +0.64, +0.69, +0.39R. Lag-1 correlation +0.61 over 10 blocks (RL2_1 +0.54, RL1_0.5 +0.58). Side-flipped entries show the same wide-exit effect: 15m RL1.5_1 pooled flip +0.174 vs +0.099 for the real side; geo10 flip +0.180 vs +0.101 (master_variant_tf.csv flip_diff_R). A simple trend proxy (efficiency ratio of 15m closes) barely tracks it: correlation 0.15 over 9 blocks (trend_blocks_6h.csv).
findings.implication: A trader rewarded on 1-7 days will see exit styles 'work' and 'fail' by regime. Do not let the AI or the weekly tuner chase the last regime. If a regime switch is ever tried, it needs its own pre-registered test; 10 blocks cannot validate one.

verification.recomputed: x5_blocks.py: geo10 minus base, 15m+30m, 6h blocks from 10/05 00:00 UTC: -0.17, -0.10, -0.22, -0.20, -0.48, -0.17, +0.64, +0.69, +0.39, +0.00 (the last block has n 54). Lag-1 correlation 0.606 over 10 blocks (RL2_1 0.536, RL1_0.5 0.582). Flipped side: same-block correlation with the real side 0.86. At 15m, RL1.5_1 flip +0.174 vs real +0.099; geo10 +0.180 vs +0.101. At 30m: flip +0.200 / +0.219 vs real +0.080 / +0.056. Trend proxy (x5_trend.py, 15m efficiency ratio per block): correlation 0.148 over 9 blocks.
verification.note: The numbers and the conclusion that the effect comes from the price path are right. The duration claim is not supported. The series contains one switch: about 36h negative (v3b plus the start of v4), then at least 18h positive. The lag-1 correlation of 0.61 is that single step, with an effective n of about 2. v3a favoured wide exits for most of its 2.6 days. Regime length is unknown; '12-24 h' should be dropped. This finding also argues that the 1h-cluster CIs used elsewhere in the lens are too narrow.

findings.claim: Fixed take-profits at 1-2R are worse than the house ladder at 15m in both runs and not better at 30m. A symmetric 1R target with a 2 ATR stop needs about a 63% hit rate after costs, and the strategies hit about 49%.
findings.evidence: exitlab_paired.csv. tp1.5R vs house at 15m: v3b -0.112, v4 -0.121, pooled -0.120 [-0.212, -0.035]. tp2R: -0.240 / -0.086, pooled -0.111 [-0.207, -0.010]. tp1R: -0.004 / -0.126, pooled -0.106 [-0.228, -0.003]. At 30m: tp1R pooled -0.058 [-0.110, -0.008]; tp1.5R -0.057; tp2R -0.075. Nothing survives BH (q >= 0.135). tp1R at 15m: win 51%, average win +0.70R, average loss -1.17R, payoff 0.595. On the real side, TP 1R came before the stop in 2,090 of 4,242 closed trades (49.3%). 5-year exitstyle: no fixed TP passed its pre-registered rule; at 30m tp1R -0.042% and tp1.5R -0.029% of equity per trade; at 15m small positives of +0.012 to +0.025% (fiveyear_exitstyle_by_tf.csv).
findings.implication: Do not make a fixed 1-2R target the code exit for 15m/30m AI traders. If the AI 'takes profit early like a human', measure that decision on a twin against the code exit; the data says it costs about 0.1R per trade in non-trending periods and gains nothing on average.

verification.note: Reproduced. Nuances: at 15m in v3b, tp1R is a tie (-0.004), not clearly worse. Only tp1.5R at 15m and tp1R at 30m keep CIs below 0 with 6h clusters. The 5-year study found all fixed TPs slightly better than the ladder at 15m (two cells BH-better for tp1R), so the live 15m penalty is period-specific. The supported conclusion is 'no gain', not 'reliably worse'.

findings.claim: Raising the lock only when the strategy's bar closes, effective from the next minute, is slightly better than raising it every minute at 15m/30m. This matches the AI design's rule 3-4.
findings.implication: Keep the design's bar-close lock updates for 15m/30m. The gain is small (+0.02 to +0.04R) and not a reason by itself. At 1h it is slightly negative.

verification.note: Holds up under 6h/12h clustering and dedup for R-ladders at 15m/30m, and the negative 1h effect is also robust. The whole gain comes from v4; v3b is about 0, and for the ROE-geometry ladders (house, geo20) at 15m it is -0.030 in v3b. The design v2 (line 303) already specifies bar-close lock updates.

findings.claim: A breakeven move at +1R (stop to the net-zero price including costs) helps exits that otherwise do not protect profit before 1-1.5R, in both runs at 15m. A breakeven before +1R does not help.
findings.implication: If the AI may 'move the stop to breakeven' (allowed action, design 4-2), allow it only after MFE >= +1R and let code compute the net-zero price. Under a ladder that already locks about +0.5R near +1R it is redundant.

verification.note: The BE-at-1R gain on fixed targets at 15m reproduces and is robust. The evidence for 'BE before +1R does not help' is confounded: be0.5_tp1 vs house mixes in the tp1R penalty. On top of TP1R, an isolated 0.5R breakeven is neutral at 15m and +0.035R at 30m, positive in both runs. At 1h the BE effect is run-dependent.

findings.claim: Time stops do not help. The house time stop (N bars, lock never armed) was negative at 15m and 1h in 2 of 3 runs, and a 'close if losing at N bars' rule behaves the same. A max hold of 2xN bars is close to neutral.
findings.implication: No time stop in the AI's code exit. A 2xN-bar max hold is acceptable only as an operational safety cap.

verification.note: Reproduced. With 6h clusters most CIs include 0. The supported reading is 'no benefit', which matches the implication.

findings.claim: Stop width: keep 2 ATR. At fixed size, 2.5-3 ATR stops lose more per unit of base risk in both runs and over 5 years. Under risk-based sizing a wider stop cuts cost per R, but in this data gross R fell by the same amount, so the result is neutral.
findings.implication: Fix the initial stop at 2 ATR14 of the entry timeframe, computed by code. Keep the design's ban on widening. A 1.5 ATR stop is not better and raises cost per R (0.224R vs 0.168R at 15m) under risk sizing.

verification.recomputed: c_main.csv. stopw3 vs base at 15m: v3b -0.037, v4 -0.053, pooled -0.051 [-0.098, 0.003] (6h [-0.115, 0.015]). stopw2.5: -0.034 [-0.061, -0.001]. 30m stopw3: -0.043. stopw1.5: +0.004 (15m), +0.021 (30m). Own-stop R in my simulator (mysim_an.py), 3 ATR minus 2 ATR: 15m +0.002, 30m +0.019, 1h +0.031. Fee-only cost per own R at 15m: 0.225 / 0.169 / 0.112 for 1.5 / 2 / 3 ATR. Gross falls from +0.132 to +0.055 (slippage included in cost). 5-year levstop (fy.py from levstop.json) at 30x, bps per notional for 1.5/2/2.5/3 ATR: 15m -14.09 / -14.24 / -14.57 / -15.04; 30m -14.67 / -15.33 / -16.18 / -17.19 (exact).
verification.note: Reproduced. Live CIs include 0 under 6h clustering. The 5-year 30x arms clip stops at liquidation, so wide-stop arms there carry some liquidation effect.

findings.claim: Leverage 20-50x with margin = leverage% of equity (the rule bot's rule) makes notional = L^2/100 x equity. One 15m stop-out then costs 3.0% (20x), 6.7% (30x), 11.8% (40x) or 18.5% (50x) of equity. Most 40-50x trades fail the 15% cap. The pnl-on-equity 'gains' of low-leverage shadows are smaller bets on negative-EV trades.
findings.evidence: lev_risk.csv. Median loss per stop, 15m / 30m: 20x 3.0 / 4.0%; 30x 6.7 / 9.1%; 40x 11.8 / 16.1%; 50x 18.5 / 25.2%. Share passing the 15% cap and liquidation buffer: 15m 40x 84%, 50x 18%; 30m 40x 37%, 50x 0%; 1h 30x 81%, 40x 1%. Seven straight 15m losses: 19% drawdown at 20x, 38% at 30x, 59% at 40x. pnl on equity per 15m signal: house (mostly 30x) -0.84%, lev10 -0.04%, while geo10 at house size is -0.16% (exitlab_paired.csv). 40x geometry vs house: 15m -0.094R [-0.197, -0.004] (v3b -0.015, v4 -0.105). 5-year: 40x / 50x geometry vs 30x at 15m -0.50 / -1.63 bps per notional, at 1h -2.43 / -4.95 bps; 50x liquidation share 5% (15m) to 19% (1h).
findings.implication: Make the stop and exits independent of leverage. Treat leverage as size: confidence-scaled leverage means confidence-scaled equity risk with no evidence yet that confidence predicts R. Default to fixed risk per stop (the design's 3% twin), or cap 15m/30m at about 30x. Expect 50x to be refused for most 15m and all 30m signals under the 15% cap.

verification.recomputed: x11.py: median loss per stop as a share of equity with margin = L% of equity. 15m: 3.0 / 6.7 / 11.8 / 18.5% at 20/30/40/50x. 30m: 4.0 / 9.1 / 16.1 / 25.2%. 1h at 30x: 12.3%. Seven straight 15m losses: 19 / 38 / 59%. Share entered (misc.py): 15m lev40m40 0.839, lev50m50 0.175; 30m 0.370 / 0.000; 1h lev30m30 0.809, lev40m40 0.012. pnl on equity per 15m signal: base -0.84%, lev10 -0.043%, geo10 -0.159%. Split of the lev10 gain into exit and size (pe.py), 15m: v3b exit -1.55pp, size +3.32pp; v4 exit +1.12pp, size -0.51pp; pooled exit +0.68pp of the +0.80pp. '40x geometry' is lev40m40 on the 2,078 of 2,477 signals that pass 40x sizing. geo40 on all signals (mysim): 15m -0.085 (v3b +0.006, v4 -0.102; 6h [-0.208, 0.020]). 5-year: 40x/50x minus 30x at 15m -0.50 / -1.63 bps; at 1h -2.43 / -4.95 (exact).
verification.note: The risk arithmetic and pass shares are right. Two fixes. (1) Saying the low-leverage 'gains' are just smaller bets holds only for v3b. In v4, and pooled at 15m, most of lev10's equity gain came from its wider exit geometry. (2) The 40x live contrast is a sizing-selected subset, and the 40x effect is v4-only and not significant with 6h clusters. The 5-year 40x/50x arms include liquidation clipping (50x liquidation share 5-19%), so they do not isolate geometry. Context: design v2 section 4-3 (owners' 10/7 decision) already sizes by risk per stop (confidence sets 2-5% risk; leverage = min(50, bracket, 70% of liquidation distance)). The '20-50x by confidence' premise is superseded.

findings.claim: At 1h the house ROE ladder is too tight (arms at about 0.43R, average winner +0.41R, breakeven win rate 71%). Wider geometry beat it in all three live runs and over 5 years. This is the only exit change that is consistent across live runs and the 5-year study.
findings.evidence: geo10 (= lev10) vs house at 1h: v3a +0.298 [0.136, 0.443] (shadows, biased against), v3b +0.145, v4 +0.132; pooled +0.134 [0.001, 0.272], q 0.21. RL2_1 at 1h: +0.263 / +0.218. Resolved-only set: geo10 +0.073 / +0.100. House 1h payoff: 61% wins, +0.41R / -0.99R. 5-year levstop, 10x vs 30x geometry: 1h +1.76 bps per notional (28/36 cells better), 4h +5.76 bps (26/36); 20x vs 30x: 1h +1.08 (29/36), 4h +2.73 (22/36). Live 4h (n 112) disagrees: wide exits were worse, but most 4h trades were still open and marked to market.
findings.implication: For the cost-free 1h/4h rule accounts, and for any later AI on 1h/4h, use a ladder with at least 10-20x price geometry or an R ladder arming at 1.5-2R. Treat it as a pre-registered change with its own shadow, not an in-run switch.

verification.recomputed: c_main.csv and mysim. geo10 vs house at 1h: v3b +0.145, v4 +0.132, pooled +0.134. CI with 1h clusters [-0.003, 0.279] (theirs [0.001, 0.272]); 6h [-0.099, 0.383]; 12h [-0.138, 0.464]. My simulator: +0.130. RL2_1 at 1h: +0.263 / +0.218. Resolved-only geo10: +0.073 / +0.100 (x14_res.py). House at 1h: 61.0% wins, +0.411 / -0.992, breakeven 70.7%. v3a shadows, strategy-only, 1h lev10: +0.304 [0.131, 0.466] n 79. 5-year (fy.py) at 1h: 10x vs 30x +1.76 bps (28/35 cells); 20x vs 30x +1.08 (29/35). At 4h: +5.76 (26/35) and +2.73 (22/35). At 30m, geo20 vs base is +0.047 in v3b and +0.037 in v4, and the 5-year 30m 20x vs 30x is +0.26 bps (24/35). Open at the end at 4h: base 28/112, geo10 28/112, RL2_1 59/112, tp3R 59/112.
verification.note: The direction is consistent across the three runs and the 5-year study. Overstatements: the pooled CI excludes 0 only under 1h clustering. 'The only consistent exit change' is not true: 20x geometry at 30m is also positive in both live runs and over 5 years, though small. 'Most 4h trades still open' holds only for RL2_1/tp3R (53%), not geo10 or base (25%). The design already plans 20x R geometry.

findings.claim: Per strategy x tf, no cell has every-signal house R significantly above 0 after BH. Two cells are significantly negative. Only three cells keep a positive mean under every exit tested (exit-robust sign), and 17 cells are negative under every exit.
findings.evidence: strategy_tf_exits.csv (60 cells with >= 25 every-signal entries; 1 h-cluster bootstrap; BH). Best q 0.72. BH-negative: F4_PULL 15m -0.59 [-0.89, -0.24] (q 0.05, n 52); N18_VWMA_MACD 30m -0.74 [-0.99, -0.42] (q 0.004, n 43). Positive under all 34 exits: N17_KC_RSI 15m +0.16 [-0.11, 0.42] (n 153; v3b +0.61 at n 15, v4 +0.11 at n 138; spread across exits only 0.16R); N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m +0.26 [-0.11, 0.67] (n 43); F6_VWAP_CROSS 1h +0.11 [-0.13, 0.30] (n 43, v4 only). Grades: 18 C, 40 D, 2 F, no A or B.
findings.implication: Use exit robustness as a screening criterion for AI candidates: prefer cells whose sign does not depend on the exit (N17_KC_RSI 15m, N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m). Treat cells that are positive only under a hindsight exit as unproven. Drop F4_PULL 15m and N18_VWMA_MACD 30m from AI consideration.

verification.recomputed: x13_cells.py (own code, 60 cells with n >= 25): 18 cells positive under the house exit, 43 with some exit > 0, 3 positive under all 34 exits (N17_KC_RSI 15m, N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m, F6_VWAP_CROSS 1h), 17 negative under all exits. Spread median 0.53 (0.16-1.22). BH-negative with 1h clusters: F4_PULL 15m -0.590 (q 0.022) and N18_VWMA_MACD 30m -0.737 (q 0.015). With 6h clusters only N18 30m survives (q 0.015); F4_PULL q is 0.22. Side-flipped entries (x13_flip.py): 2 of 60 cells are positive under all 34 exits on the flipped side, N18_VWMA_MACD 30m (+0.270) and S2_ST_ROC 1h. F4_PULL flipped is +0.130 under 31/34 exits. Across cells, real and flipped house means correlate -0.65. 5-year every-signal (fy_ref.py), bps per notional: N17_KC_RSI 15m -16.5 (t -71); N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m -15.6; N18_VWMA_MACD 30m -13.4; S4_BB_BBP 15m -15.2. F6_VWAP_CROSS 1h (ds200 PREREG exits) is negative in both IS and CF.
verification.note: The cell numbers reproduce. The screening implication does not hold. Coin-flip direction yields exit-robust cells at a similar rate (2 vs 3), so a robust sign mostly reflects which way the 1.5-2 day market went relative to the cell's signals, not skill. The 5-year reference ranks N18_VWMA_MACD 30m (proposed for exclusion) as no worse than N17_KC_RSI 15m or N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m (proposed as candidates). Exit robustness should not be used to promote or drop strategies.

findings.claim: The every-signal exit re-run is trustworthy as a measuring tool. It matches the live engine and the nightly shadows exactly. 7-12% of positions are still open at the data end, and their mark-to-market does not drive the conclusions.
findings.evidence: validate.txt. Base vs rb_analyze replay: 4,236 closed signals, max |dROE| 2.2e-16, same exit reasons. 410 rb_analyze-unresolved signals now resolve (89) or are marked (321). 102 sizing rejections match. Every resolved nightly variant row on v4 trades matches exactly (median |dROE| 0, 18 variants). Open at the end on the real side: base 321 of 4,646 (6.9%), RL2_1 519 (11.2%), tp3R 561 (12.1%). On the all-resolved subset the per-run differences are close (e.g. RL1.5_1 15m v4 +0.164 all vs +0.183 resolved; exitlab_robustness.csv dR_res_*).
findings.implication: Use exitlab.py (copied engine calls, no repo edits) as the template for the nightly shadow fix and for the pre-registered 5-year test of the AI exit (R ladder, BE at 1R, bar-close updates) before 10/17.

verification.recomputed: mysim.py is an independent minute-bar exit simulator (no engine or exitlab code), seeded from the rb_analyze replay entries. On trades without funding it matches the replay R for all 4,236 traded signals. It matches exitlab exactly (|dR| < 1e-6) on 100% of rows for tp1R/1.5R/2R/3R and RL* (4,646 each, both sides), and on every zero-funding row for the other variants. All mismatches above 0.01R are on trades with funding: 188 of 4,646 base rows, max 7R, because funding shifts the ROE-ladder lock price. rb_analyze UNRESOLVED 410: 321 OPEN_END and 89 closed (51 SL, 28 LOCK, 10 gap stops). Open at the end, real side: base 321 (6.9%), RL2_1 519 (11.2%), tp3R 561 (12.1%). By tf: 1h base 74/780 vs tp3R 150/780; 4h 28-59 of 112. RES vs all: RL1.5_1 at 15m v4 +0.183 vs +0.164; geo10 at 1h v3b +0.073 vs +0.145.
verification.note: Validation confirmed independently. Caveats: open shares are 9-19% at 1h and 25-53% at 4h, and marking does change 1h magnitudes. Inferred funding is a material input for single ladder trades (4% of base rows move more than 0.01R), though the means barely change (-0.1198 vs -0.1207).

strategy_note_problems: Grades are just the sign of the house mean: C if above 0, D if at or below 0, F if BH-negative under 1h clusters. They ignore the exit robustness, cross-run consistency and 5-year reference the notes themselves cite. N01_ST_EMA 15m (6/34 exits > 0, runs -0.84 vs +1.01) gets the same C as N17_KC_RSI 15m (34/34). F7_RF_TRIPLE 15m (+0.005) is C while F4_FAN 15m (-0.002) is D, and N24_DMI 30m (+0.04) is C while OBV_B 30m (-0.004) is D. These are coin-flip boundaries at these n.

F4_PULL 15m grade F: significant only with 1h clusters (my q 0.022; their 0.05). With 6h clusters, which the lens's own X5 regime finding implies, q is 0.22. Its flipped side was +0.13R and positive under 31/34 exits. The 5-year DeepSeek reference is also negative (IS -0.129%, CF -0.130%), so exclusion is defensible, but on the 5-year data, not this live significance.

N18_VWMA_MACD 30m grade F, 'exclude': robust live (q 0.015 even with 6h clusters). But its flipped side was +0.27R and positive under all 34 exits. Its 5-year every-signal mean (-13.4 bps per notional, t -29) is less negative than the cells promoted as candidates (N17_KC_RSI 15m -16.5, N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m -15.6). The F grade reflects this period's market direction.

N17_KC_RSI 15m, 'best exit-lens AI candidate at 15m': numbers reproduce (n 153, +0.162, 34/34 exits > 0, spread 0.162). But 'positive in both runs' rests on v3b n 15. The 6h-cluster CI is [-0.32, +0.72]. The 5-year every-signal mean is strongly negative (-0.050 ROE, -16.5 bps per notional, t -71, IS and CF both negative). Its flipped side is -0.344 and still positive under 7/34 exits.
N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m, 'exit-robust 30m candidate': 'both runs' rests on v3b n 7. 5-year: -15.6 bps per notional, t -26, negative in IS and CF.
F6_VWAP_CROSS 1h, 'positive under all exits': v4 only. 5-year DeepSeek reference negative in IS (-0.108 to -0.162%) and CF (-0.08%).

Duplicate notes ('near-duplicate of F11_RAID / F11_TSOUP'): at the every-signal level these cells differ (n 36/38/25, house -0.05 / -0.12 / -0.47) but share 16-19 identical trades. They enter BH and the X3 tuning test as separate cells, which inflates the effective number of cells. About 47% of all every-signal rows repeat another strategy's identical coin/bar/side trade (dups.py).

The q-values come from t-based p with 1h clusters. Bootstrap p gives slightly different q (F4_PULL 0.022 vs 0.05; N04_ST_KLINGER 15m 0.198 vs 0.26). No conclusion changes under 1h clusters, but several do under 6h.

Checked and correct as stated (x13_cells.csv): S4_BB_BBP 15m, F1_MOM_DIV 15m, F6_VWAP_FAIL 15m, N01_ST_EMA 15m, F3_HHHL 15m, N20_EMA9_CHOP 15m, N22_VORTEX_PSAR 15m (-0.223/-0.222), N04_ST_KLINGER 15m/30m/1h, S2_ST_ROC 1h, N24_DMI 30m, N17_KC_RSI 30m/1h, F14_SMT 30m: n, house R, CI, per-run means, geo20_bar, RL1_0.5_bar, tp1R, best exit, spread and exits > 0 all match to 2 decimals.
verifier_missed: Cost split: the lens's cost R is fees plus funding only. The 0.04% round-trip slippage sits inside its 'gross'. Full modeled cost is 0.236R (15m), 0.164R (30m), 0.116R (1h) and 0.064R (4h), so the AI's per-trade hurdle is about 0.24R at 15m and 0.16R at 30m (x1_levels.py).

Double counting: 47% of the every-signal rows at 15m (1,304 unique of 2,477), 47% at 30m and 52% at 1h are the same coin/bar/side trade fired by several strategies (840 of 1,171 groups have identical R). The 'house_all' group also includes coin-flip accounts. Deduplicated, the 15m house mean is -0.154 instead of -0.106. Most contrasts change little (dups.py, c_dedup.csv).

Clustering: all lens CIs use 1h clusters, but its own X5 shows regime persistence over several 6h blocks. With 6h or 12h blocks most contrasts lose significance: X12 pooled 1h geo10 [-0.10, 0.38], X9 15m timestop [-0.12, 0.01], X10 15m stopw3 [-0.12, 0.02], X2 lev10 15m [-0.24, 0.42]. The lens argues against '20-50x leverage by confidence' and the ROE ladder, which the design has already replaced. 4h survivorship: 98 of 207 submitted 4h strategy/DeepSeek signals were refused by sizing under the 30x quality rule. These are the widest stops. The 4h every-signal results cover only the rest, and design v2's minimum-3x rule would trade them.

Real plus flipped gross R, before all costs, is +0.087R per side at 15m. This is either noise or a small fill bias in favour of the simulator (1m bars fill exactly at the stop/lock price plus 0.02%). The 'gross about 0' baseline is therefore uncertain by roughly 0.1R.

Equity-curve framing (X11): at 15m pooled, +0.68pp of lev10's +0.80pp equity gain came from its wider exit, not its smaller size. In v3b it was the reverse (size +3.32pp, exit -1.55pp). Leverage-variant equity gains should therefore always be split into exit and size parts (pe.py).

limits: Live evidence covers only about 4.8 days in three regimes: v3a 10/02-10/05, v3b 0.7 days, v4 1.5 days. The exit effects at 15m/30m flip sign between consecutive 6-24 h windows, so the live data cannot estimate any exit's long-run effect. It can only show that effects are regime-dependent and that no exit fixes cost plus the lack of edge.

v3a has no live_bars, so it cannot be re-run. Its numbers come from nightly shadows on entered trades only, with unresolved rows dropped (biased against wide exits, shown on v4: -0.20R for lev10 at 15m). The v3a base was the 50x tier walk, so v3a variant differences are relative to a different (tighter) geometry than v3b/v4 at 30x.

The re-run horizon ends at 10/07 15:40 KST. Positions still open then are marked to market with exit costs: 6.9% of house trades, 11-12% for the widest exits (RL2_1, tp3R). This is unbiased only if prices are a martingale. 4h results are dominated by such marks, and 1h results partly; the all-resolved subset agrees in sign but selects on resolution time.

Time-cluster bootstrap with 1 h blocks gives only 17 clusters for v3b and 36-37 for v4, so CIs are approximate and probably too narrow. Signals duplicated across DeepSeek definitions and accounts are kept per account and add no independent information. No variant or contrast survives BH at 0.05 (the best q is about 0.09).

The new exit candidates (R-unit ladders, BE at 1R, bar-close updates, time_neg, max hold) were tested only on these days. The repo's 5-year studies cover only the ROE-ladder geometry (levstop fixed-leverage arms) and fixed TPs (exitstyle). Before 10/17 the R ladder needs a pre-registered 5-year test; this analysis does not provide one (5-year bars are not in this container; Binance is blocked from here).

Funding rates were solved from recorded trade funding and brackets were inferred from trades (as in rb_analyze). A replayed position held over a funding instant no live trade held pays 0 funding. Paper stop slippage (2 bps) is used; measured real stop slips were slightly smaller, so stop-heavy exits are, if anything, penalized a little.

Every variant runs each signal alone on a fresh $5,000 account. One-position accounts would take fewer signals, and shorter exits free the slot for more trades and more costs. Account-level effects of exit length (trades per day, cost drag) are not simulated.

AI discretionary behavior (early profit-taking, switching, near-signal entries, confidence-scaled leverage) cannot be simulated from rule data. The tight-vs-wide exit results only bound what mechanical analogues of those behaviors did in these regimes.

Strategy x tf cells have 25-153 signals (v3b at most 43 per cell; DeepSeek v4-only). Grades are descriptive; no cell is decidable on its own, and 'best exit in hindsight' per cell is mostly noise (out-of-sample test X3).

Paper cost per trade as % of equity with margin = leverage %: 10x 0.14, 20x 0.56, 30x 1.26, 40x 2.24, 50x 3.50 (real BTC: 0.40/0.91/1.62/2.53 at 20/30/40/50x). With a fixed 20% margin, 50x costs 1.40%. 5-year levstop (fixed leverage, 2 ATR): per-notional -14.4 (10x), -14.4 (20x), -14.5 (30x), -14.9 (40x), -15.7 bp (50x); liquidated share 0.01%, 0.21%, 0.79%, 2.05%, 4.14%.
findings.implication: 'Leverage 20-50x by AI confidence' only pays if the AI's confidence predicts at least 14 bp of gross edge. Otherwise moving from 20x/20% to 50x/50% multiplies the cost drag by 6.25. Size leverage on a measured gross edge and keep the 50x tier off until that is shown.

verification.recomputed: Arithmetic: 14 bp x lev x margin share: 20x/20% 0.56%, 50x/50% 3.50% of equity (ratio 6.25). levstop.json per notional at 2 ATR: 10x -14.37, 20x -14.39, 30x -14.47, 40x -14.89, 50x -15.67 bp; liquidated share 0.013%, 0.21%, 0.79%, 2.05%, 4.14%. Own 5y 15m sim with liquidation: 10x/20x/30x/50x liq 0%/0.08%/0.48%/4.75%, gross R +0.0087/+0.0024/+0.0016/+0.0007.
verification.note: Reproduces. levstop's own arms use margin 40% at 40-50x, not 50%.

findings.claim: The code-computed lock ladder leaks about 0.09 to 0.11R on every lock exit. In 37% of lock exits the next 1m bar opens beyond the new lock level, because at 30x the ladder's 2% ROE trigger gap is only about 6.7 bp of price, about one minute of noise.
findings.evidence: c01_decompose.py -> out/c01_lock_gap_by_tf.csv (core36+ds200 LOCK exits, live trades). 15m n=472: 37.5% gapped, mean 6.5 bp (p90 12.8), 0.115R per lock exit. 30m n=339: 37.2%, 8.0 bp (p90 19.1), 0.090R. 1h n=214: 36.5%, 8.9 bp, 0.076R. Median 1m bar range 3.3-7.1 bp (c00_ticks.csv). Real stop data on LOCK exits matches paper on average (d3 LOCK real minus paper -0.3 bp at 15m/30m, pipeline stop_slips_summary.csv), so the leak is real, not a paper artifact.
findings.implication: For AI exits computed by code, place the exchange-side stop the moment a lock arms (tick or mark stream) instead of at the next 1m bar, or make the lock steps price-based and wider than one minute of noise. That could recover up to about 0.05R per trade (an upper bound; the counterfactual path cannot be replayed on 1m bars).

verification.recomputed: v1_live.py LOCK exits core36+ds200 (gap = exit before slip vs lock price): 15m n=472, 36.9% gapped >0.1bp, mean 6.55 bp, 0.115R per lock exit; 30m n=339, 36.9%, 7.97 bp, 0.090R; 1h n=214, 36.4%, 8.92 bp, 0.076R; 4h n=37, 27%, 15.5 bp, 0.078R. Real LOCK stop minus paper (d3 ok rows): 15m -0.27, 30m -0.33, 1h -0.14 bp. 2% ROE at 30x = 6.7 bp.
verification.note: Reproduces. The recovery figure is an upper bound (the real ROE-vs-mark path inside the minute is unknown), and the real-stop comparison excludes the 41% 'cap' rows.

findings.claim: In the cost lens no strategy x timeframe at 15m or 30m earns an A. Only N02_ST_KST 15m, N07_ICHI_CMO 30m and N12_ICHI_AO 30m show a small five-year pre-cost edge (+1.8 to +2.9 bp, 13-21% of one round trip), and about 3 such cells are expected by chance. Several live 'winners' lose before costs over five years. DeepSeek loses before costs at 15m and 30m.
findings.evidence: c09_strategy_notes.py -> out/c09_strategy_cost_grades.csv. Core36 15m: 1 B, 23 C, 5 D; 30m: 2 B, 24 C, 6 D (108 core cells x 3 tfs; one-sided 2.5% chance gives about 2.7 false positives). B cells, 5y gross R [week-block CI]: N02_ST_KST 15m +0.019 [+0.003, +0.035]; N07_ICHI_CMO 30m +0.022 [+0.001, +0.045]; N12_ICHI_AO 30m +0.022 [+0.000, +0.045]. Contradicted live winners: N17_KC_RSI 15m live gross +0.35R [+0.06, +0.62] (n=153) vs 5y -0.020R [-0.031, -0.008]; N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m +0.42 [+0.03, +0.85] (n=43) vs 5y -0.011 (both periods < 0); OBV_S 30m +0.74 (n=8) vs 5y -0.012. DeepSeek (fiveyear_ref, own exits X5_TRAIL2): 40/44 definitions at 15m and 35/41 at 30m have negative gross in both IS and CF (median -5.5/-4.6 bp and -6.5/-6.3 bp vs a 10.4-10.7 bp cost); none is positive in both periods.
findings.implication: For AI-trader selection, prefer the B cells at 30m as starting points, and drop the D cells and the DeepSeek definitions as bases. Do not promote any strategy because of live October gross alone.

verification.recomputed: Own 5y sim per strategy x tf (week-block CI; their B rule = CI lo>0 and both periods >0): 15m B N02_ST_KST +0.0187 [+0.0040, ...], P1 +0.015 / P2 +0.024 (confirmed); 30m N07_ICHI_CMO +0.0238 [+0.0021] (confirmed); N12_ICHI_AO 30m +0.0207 [-0.0023, +0.043] (NOT B in independent sim); N10_HA_PSAR 30m +0.0135 [+0.0012], P1 +0.017 / P2 +0.010 (B in mine, C in theirs, their lo -0.0011); N07_ICHI_CMO 15m +0.0183 [-0.0014], both periods >0 (borderline); 1h: no B. D cells reproduce: N17_KC_RSI 15m -0.0182 [-0.029,-0.007]; N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m -0.0099 (P1/P2 <0); OBV_S 30m -0.0096 (P1/P2 <0). DeepSeek fiveyear_ref X5_TRAIL2: 15m 40/44 negative gross in IS and CF, 0 positive in both (median -5.4/-4.6 bp vs cost 10.4); 30m 37/44 both negative, 0 both positive (median -6.5/-5.6).
verification.note: The B set depends on the simulator: 2 of their 3 B cells are robust, 1 is replaced by another boundary cell. That is the expected chance rate (about 3 of 105 cells), so treat B as 'not ruled out', not as an edge. Even the best B (+0.024R, about 3 bp) covers less than 20% of cost. The DeepSeek 5y verdict uses DeepSeek's own exits (X5_TRAIL2), while all 171 live ds200 accounts use house exits, so it is not the exit rule that was traded live.

findings.claim: The positive live gross at 15m (+0.13R) does not come from strategy skill. Coin flips earned it too: the tight-lock, wide-stop exits gain in a quiet, ranging market. Five years show no such gain, even in the quietest quintile.
findings.evidence: c05_breakeven_by_tf.csv: coin flips 15m gross +0.257R [+0.031, +0.479] (n=53) vs core36+ds200 +0.132 [+0.001, +0.286]. The pipeline's side-flip shows both sides at the same moments net about -0.15R at 15m (strategy chosen -0.152 vs other side -0.165). 5-year average of both sides ('coinflip_gross_R', c07_5y_regime.csv): 15m -0.0018R overall, Q1 quietest -0.0022.
findings.implication: Do not read October's 15m paper gross as an edge an AI can keep. When volatility returns, the same exit structure is expected to give that gross back.

verification.recomputed: Replay random (coin-flip) 15m n=46 gross +0.329R [+0.044,+0.577]; live random 15m trades n=50 gross +0.404 [+0.118,+0.677]. Side-flip core36 15m: chosen net -0.152 vs flipped -0.165 (n=1,087). 5y both-sides gross R 15m -0.0014 [-0.0048,+0.0018], quietest quintile -0.0028; 2026 is the best 15m year (+0.010 both sides), still about 0. Bar-resolution check (v8_res.py): on live-period signals, a tf-bar ladder (as in the 5y tests) gives core36 15m gross +0.141 vs +0.072 on 1m bars (my sim; parity with the engine corr 0.90), so the 5y zero is not an artifact of coarse bars.
verification.note: Reproduces. A caveat not in the claim: ds200 15m live chosen -0.070 vs flipped -0.216 (n=1,107). This is in-sample over 1.5 days, with duplicates, and does not hold at 30m (-0.138 vs -0.083).

findings.claim: 'Trading like a human' makes cost worse. Every extra round trip (a switch, a re-entry, a split entry) costs another 0.16 to 0.30R at 15m. On lock winners, costs already eat about a quarter of the gross, so taking profit earlier raises that share.
findings.evidence: Paper cost per round trip in R (c05_breakeven_by_tf.csv): 15m 0.236, 30m 0.163, 1h 0.116, 4h 0.064. Lock-exit winners (c01_lock_gap_by_tf.csv): 15m gross 0.92R, cost 0.24R (26%); 30m gross 0.68R, cost 0.17R (25%). Funding is negligible at 15m/30m (0.000-0.001R per trade, c01).
findings.implication: Make 'skip' the AI's default action and add trade-count limits per trader. Score switching and early exits against the extra cost they cause, and count every AI action that adds a round trip at about 0.2R at 15m.

verification.recomputed: Replay paper cost per round trip core+ds200: 15m 0.240, 30m 0.167, 1h 0.120, 4h 0.066R. Live LOCK winners: 15m gross 0.923 / cost 0.243 (26%); 30m 0.683 / 0.169 (25%). Funding 0.000-0.001R. Real taker per coin 15m 0.16-0.30R.
verification.note: Reproduces.

strategy_note_problems: N12_ICHI_AO 30m graded B: not reproduced by an independent simulator (5y gross R +0.0207, week-block CI [-0.0023, +0.043]). Their own CI lower bound is +0.000. Downgrade to C/borderline.

N10_HA_PSAR 30m graded C, but it meets their B rule in my simulator (+0.0135R [+0.0012], P1 +0.017 / P2 +0.010; their lo -0.0011). B/C is set by the simulator at the CI boundary, so B grades are noise-level and should not drive selection.

Live 'every-signal' n in the notes include unresolved positions marked to market at export end (c02 'marked'), e.g. N17_KC_RSI 15m n=153 = 109 resolved + 44 marked (resolved-only gross +0.31R); N02_ST_KST 15m n=31 vs 28 resolved. Label these or use resolved-only.

The DeepSeek group grade D is based on 5y gross under DeepSeek's own X5_TRAIL2 exits, but all 171 live ds200 accounts use house exits. The 30m count is 37/44 (not 35/41) negative in both periods. The 'loses before costs' wording should name the exit rule.

The notes cover only 15m/30m. No 1h/4h grades exist, although the owners now plan 1h entries (and 4h at 20x). 1h: no core cell passes B in my 5y sim. DeepSeek fiveyear_ref has 5/44 (1h) and 4/39 (4h) definitions with positive gross in both IS and CF (F4_PULL_RSI, F5_BOX, F5_BOX_RSI, F10_M2022, F13_FVG_PD @1h; F1_PVT_DIV, F10_M2022, F11_PO3, F12_MSS_DISP @4h), near the chance rate.
'AI must add X R/trade' uses today's quiet stop. At the 5y median volatility the requirement is about 35-40% lower (C4), which the notes do not say.

Sample-checked numbers that DO reproduce: N02_ST_KST 15m 5y n 28,285, +1.9 bp, +0.019R, P1/P2 +0.015/+0.024; N17_KC_RSI 15m 5y -0.018R; N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m live n=42, gross +0.43; OBV_S 30m live n=8, +0.74; N07_ICHI_CMO 30m live n=9, +0.23; N12_ICHI_AO 30m live -0.18; DOGE 15m live -0.21.
verifier_missed: Duplicate trades. In the every-signal replay, core36+ds200 15m has 2,255 signal-accounts but only 1,152 distinct (run, coin, side, bar) entries (1h: 685 -> 323; 4h: 79 -> 32). Identical entries with the same 2 ATR stop and house exits are the same trade, so pooled CIs are too narrow. AI traders on overlapping strategies would hold the same position (no diversification, stacked risk).

4h at 20x and liquidation. In my 5y sim with isolated-margin liquidation (mm 0.5%), 8.1% of 4h signals at 20x and 17.8% at 30x are liquidated before the 2 ATR stop; at 1h, 0.9% (20x) and 4.7% (30x). The 5y median 4h stop (4.35%) is near the 20x liquidation distance (~4.5%). Today's 2.0% 4h stop hides this. 'Only where 20x is executable' must be a per-signal check that stop distance plus buffer is below the liquidation distance, or leverage must be capped near 1/(stop%+buffer).

1h/4h break-even (owners' new plan). 5y gross R: 1h -0.0015 [-0.008,+0.005], 4h -0.0012 [-0.008,+0.007]; net -15.2 and -16.0 bp/notional before funding (multi-day 4h holds add funding). Needed AI edge at today's stops: 1h taker 0.08-0.16R (maker 0.06-0.10), 4h about 0.05-0.10R (10-19 bp / 2.0%). The bp hurdle (10-19 bp) is the same at every tf. Live: core36 1h n=212 net -0.073R (gross +0.042 [-0.081,+0.182]); 4h n=31 net +0.144 (gross CI -0.24..+0.61). That is too few trades to judge 4h. 1h/4h are cheaper per R, not more profitable before costs.

Half-spread and timing of real costs: slip_best excludes the half-spread and is read seconds after the minute, and 41% of v4 stop-slip rows are 'cap' (unmeasured). Real LTC/BCH/DOGE costs are probably higher than C6 states.

Unresolved rows: about 410 every-signal positions open at export end are marked to market in the lens replay, and 13% of limit-shadow rows are unresolved and dropped. Pooled effects are small, but per-strategy live notes and the limit CIs depend on them.

Time clustering: every live and limit uncertainty rests on 15-26 2h clusters over about 2.2 days (v3b+v4). None of the live gross estimates is out-of-sample, and the 5y data is the only usable evidence on gross edge.

In my sim the ladder is leverage-dependent but gross stays near zero at every leverage (15m 10x +0.0087R, 20x +0.0024, 30x +0.0016, 50x +0.0007). Leverage choice by 'AI confidence' cannot create gross edge.

The 2026 quiet regime is the best 15m year in 5y (gross R +0.016, both-sides +0.010). The quiet-market exit tailwind exists but is an order of magnitude smaller than the 0.16-0.30R cost at today's stops.

findings.claim: No chart context replicates across runs: when contexts are found in one run and tested in another, the result is no better than chance. In the live data the strategies' chart context carries no structure stable enough for an AI filter to learn.
findings.evidence: Omnibus check, same 63 pre-registered bucket contrasts estimated in v3a and in v4 (core 36). Correlation of the effects across contrasts: 15m +0.092 over 58 contrasts (circular-shift null p 0.514, null 5-95% -0.356..0.462); 30m -0.091 over 49 (p 0.683). Sign agreement 0.586 and 0.592, against null means 0.531 and 0.503 (p 0.32, 0.19). Source: out/omnibus_corr.csv (scan.py). Discovery to test, primary 15m+30m, 2h time blocks, t with df = sum(G-1). Direction A (v3a to v3b+v4): 115 testable, 28 raw p<0.05 (about 6 expected by chance), 15 with BH q<0.10. Out of sample: 3 one-sided p<0.05, 0 with BH q<0.05, 0 replicated, same sign 18/28. Direction B (v4 to v3a+v3b): 108 testable, 7 p<0.05 (about 5 expected), 0 with q<0.10, 1 replicated. Source: out/scan_directional.csv. Winsorized R, win rate and gross R give the same picture: correlation of all effects across runs -0.12..+0.14 (out/robust_directional.csv).
findings.implication: The live paper data gives no basis for an AI 'chart judgement' layer to add the edge the strategies lack. AI traders should not be chosen or justified on the premise that context-aware entries rescue a strategy.

verification.recomputed: Own 62-contrast scan (verify3/c2.py, own v3a R reconstruction, 2h-block cluster SE). Omnibus correlation v3a vs v4 effects: 15m +0.001 (60 contrasts), 30m -0.075 (57); sign agreement 0.55 / 0.56. Direction A: 114 testable, 27 discovery p<0.05, 1 OOS one-sided p<0.05 (15m Europe, p1 0.0017). B: 107 testable, 7 carried, 1 OOS (15m Europe). No chart-context contrast replicated in A or B.
verification.note: Confirmed for chart context. Two caveats. (1) The 'no context replicates' wording must exclude the session: 15m Europe carries over in all three directions (analyst's own file: A p1 0.0026, q 0.074; B q 0.011; T p1 0.004). (2) v3a, the discovery set for A and T, has R that is confounded with leverage (see missed). BH was applied only within each direction's carried tests. The lens produced about 2,400 test rows (scan_full 1,323, scan_directional 567, sideflip 252, per_strategy 149, hypotheses 105, ...).

findings.claim: Power is the binding constraint. A single pre-registered bucket contrast can only detect about 0.25-0.6 R, while the real context effects (5-year) are 0.01-0.06 R. A shift of +/-0.4 R is invisible in this sample.
findings.evidence: Median MDE80 (two-sided 5%, 2h-block SE). Core 36, all runs pooled (4.57 days): 15m 0.280 R, 30m 0.240 R. v4 alone: 0.627 R and 0.471 R. ds200 v4: 0.483 R and 0.417 R. After correcting for about 60 contrasts: 0.41 R and 0.35 R. Days of all-strategy signals needed for one pre-specified 0.10 R test: about 36 (15m) and 26 (30m). For the 5-year effect size of about 0.04 R: about 224 and 165 days. Source: out/power_by_scope.csv (analysis2.py). Time clustering is severe: v4 15m design effect 7.4 at 1h blocks, 12.6 at 2h, 19.4 at 4h; v3a 15m 3.7 / 5.7 / 9.1 (out/design_effect_by_block.csv). The known-real cost-channel effect (wide minus tight stop, about +0.15 R) came out at only p 0.10 (15m) and 0.068 (30m) live (out/hypotheses.csv H7).
findings.implication: Paper results before 12/31 cannot validate any context filter, AI-learned or rule-based. Filters have to be designed and validated on the 5-year data. Live paper or shadow can only catch gross breakage. Weekly custom-value tuning of entry filters on a week of shadow data will fit noise.

verification.recomputed: Design effect of mean R (verify3/c3.py): v3a core 15m 4.0 / 5.6 / 9.5 at 1h / 2h / 4h blocks (claim 3.7 / 5.7 / 9.1). v4 core 15m 6.1 / 10.1 / 13.0 (claim 7.4 / 12.6 / 19.4). Pooled all-run contrast SEs are about 0.07-0.14 R, so MDE80 is about 0.2-0.4 R, which agrees with the claim.
verification.note: The substance holds: live data cannot detect effects under about 0.25 R. The v4 design effects do not reproduce (lower in my build), so the numbers are corrected. The 36-day and 224-day projections assume a constant design effect and signal rate. Treat them as order-of-magnitude figures.

findings.claim: On 5 years of every-signal data (1.65M signals) the live candidate contexts are real but tiny: a few hundredths of R. The exception is the cost channel (stop width).
findings.evidence: fiveyear_tests2.py, strata strategy x year x side, KST-day clusters. Values are 15m / 30m in R. Europe session -0.039 / -0.021 (z -11.0 / -5.2). ADX>=30 +0.028 / +0.021. Middle of the HTF box -0.030 / -0.013. EMA 'with' +0.024 / +0.008. DI with +0.048 / +0.051. Box far edge +0.057 / +0.044. Range far edge +0.041 / +0.035. Consensus>=4 +0.006 / +0.014. Wide stop +0.163 / +0.102 (z 35 / 18). Signs hold in 4-6 of 6 years (out5y/fiveyear_contrasts.csv). Family hypotheses: trend family in high vs low ER +0.044 / +0.024. Trend family DI with +0.055 / +0.056 (6/6 years). Revert family in low ER -0.005 / -0.003, so no effect. Revert at the 'cheap edge' comes out -0.244 at 15m, the opposite of the prediction (out5y/fiveyear_hypotheses.csv). Live point estimates of the same contrasts were roughly 10x larger: europe 15m -0.415, ADX 15m +0.234 (out/scan_full.csv scope all).
findings.implication: An AI that perfectly learned these contexts would gain about 0.03-0.06 R per kept trade, well below the 0.16-0.22 R median round trip at 15m/30m. Context is a tie-breaker at best, never an edge source.

verification.recomputed: Own within-stratum (strategy x tf x year x side) regression on the analyst's 5-year signal file, KST-day clusters (verify3/f5.py), 15m / 30m R: Europe -0.040 / -0.021 (negative in 6/6 and 5/6 years), ADX>=30 +0.030 / +0.021, HTF middle -0.031 / -0.013, EMA-with +0.008 / +0.009, DI-with +0.041 / +0.042, box far edge +0.046 / +0.040, range far +0.039 / +0.032, consensus>=4 +0.013 / +0.014, wide stop +0.166 / +0.101, wide minus tight +0.265 / +0.144, N18 high-low ER +0.029 / -0.010.
verification.note: The values reproduce within about 0.01 R. Exceptions: EMA-with at 15m is +0.008 (claim +0.024), and the z-values are smaller with my clustering (Europe 15m z -6.3, claim -11.0). Build check against the pipeline's 5-year reference: signal counts have a median ratio of 0.957 (minimum 0.5 in one cell), and mean return on notional correlates 0.76 across 70 cells. The 5-year outcome build is the analyst's own and I did not re-run it from raw bars. In ROE every context effect is at most 0.012.

findings.claim: A learned context filter does not make any strategy break even. Trained on 5-year 2021-08..2024-06 and tested on 2024-07..2026-09, the top third by predicted R improves by only +0.05 R (15m) and +0.03 R (30m) and stays clearly negative. Every one of the 64 core strategy x tf cells keeps a negative filtered mean.
findings.evidence: Ridge on 11 bar-computable context features (out5y/fiveyear_filters.csv, fiveyear_tests.py C11). CF uplift 15m +0.051 R (day-cluster CI 0.039..0.064): kept mean -0.122 vs all -0.173. 30m +0.032 (0.019..0.046): kept -0.087 vs -0.119. The live-trained filter applied to 5 years gives +0.029..+0.059 R per year at 15m (2022-2026) and +0.014..+0.043 at 30m, with kept means -0.08..-0.17 (C10). Per strategy (out5y/fiveyear_filter_by_strategy.csv): best filtered cells are 30m N07_ICHI_CMO -0.032 +/- 0.027, 30m S5_DONCHIAN_MFI -0.041 +/- 0.051, 15m N19_FIB_CHOP -0.083 +/- 0.026. All 64 are below 0. The 15m IS model is dominated by stop width (coefficients: tight -0.17, wide +0.14) (out5y/fiveyear_IS_coefs_15m.csv).
findings.implication: Choose AI-trader strategies on their own direction or exit edge, not on filterability. With these features no 15m/30m core strategy becomes a 'not losing' candidate through context selection.

verification.recomputed: Own ridge (13 bar features, IS before 2024-07-01, OOS after; verify3/f6.py). OOS top-third uplift: 15m +0.075 R (day-bootstrap CI 0.063..0.087), kept -0.098 vs all -0.173. 30m +0.045 (0.033..0.057), kept -0.074 vs -0.119. Per strategy under the global filter, 0 of 32 (15m) and 0 of 31 (30m) cells with >=100 kept signals are >=0. Best: 15m N19_FIB_CHOP -0.040, 30m N17_KC_RSI -0.036, N07_ICHI_CMO -0.036.
verification.note: The conclusion holds: no cell reaches break-even. The size of the uplift depends on the feature set (mine is about 50% larger than the claimed +0.051 / +0.032). Within-cell top thirds above 0 occur only with n<=27.

findings.claim: The largest live 'context' effect is market direction, and it flips between runs. A filter that learns it (with side, coin or session as inputs) loses money out of sample.
findings.evidence: Long minus short at 15m (out/scan_full.csv): v3a +0.694 R (p<0.001); v3b -0.587; v4 core -0.902; v4 ds200 -0.984. At 30m: +0.661, -0.666, -0.599, -0.693. Ridge on all features trained on v3a: in-sample top-third uplift +0.42 R. Out of sample on v3b+v4 core -0.371 R (CI -0.611..-0.144), on v4 ds200 -0.480 (CI -0.749..-0.199) (out/learned_filter.csv). At 15m the 'momentum alignment' contexts are mostly direction in disguise. After stratifying by side: DI-with falls from +0.273 to +0.032, box far edge from +0.325 to +0.028, range far edge from +0.244 to +0.026, EMA-with from +0.305 to +0.166 (out/side_stratified.csv).
findings.implication: A human-like AI that adapts to the last days' winners (longs good, shorts good) will chase the direction of the week. The prompt and memory design should stop the AI from carrying recent-direction lessons into entry filtering and leverage.

verification.note: v3b and v4 match exactly. v3a differs slightly because of my independent shadow-to-R conversion. I did not re-run the ridge with side and coin as inputs. The sign flip alone makes any side-learning filter non-transferable.

findings.claim: A chart-only learned filter (no side, coin or session) transferred weakly across runs: about +0.11..+0.18 R. The bootstrap CIs include 0, and the transfer comes entirely from momentum-alignment features worth only about +0.04 R over 5 years.
findings.evidence: out/learned_filter.csv and out/learned_filter_variants.csv (learned_filter.py, learned_filter2.py). Top third, v3a to v3b+v4: +0.166 R (CI -0.142..0.476; circular-shift null p 0.005; kept mean +0.028 vs -0.138). v3a to v4 ds200: +0.179 (CI -0.254..0.612; p 0.015; kept +0.091 vs -0.088). v4 to v3a+v3b: +0.113 (CI -0.017..0.234; p 0.045; kept -0.194 vs -0.307). Without the 6 momentum features: +0.061, +0.086, +0.002 (null p 0.27, 0.15, 0.37). Stop width alone: +0.009, -0.062, -0.060.
findings.implication: Some transferable structure exists (trade with the short-term move, avoid chasing extended moves), but its true size is about 0.04 R. A 'go with the move' bias is a reasonable soft preference for an AI. It cannot carry a strategy.

verification.recomputed: Own chart-only ridge (11 chart features + tf, top third within run, 2h-block bootstrap; verify3/c4.py). v3a->v3b+v4: +0.089 R (CI -0.093..0.266). v3a->ds200: +0.061 (-0.189..0.296). v4->v3a+v3b: -0.088 (-0.227..0.018). Without the momentum features: +0.011, -0.015, -0.147.
verification.note: The claimed +0.11..+0.18 transfer does not reproduce, and one direction turns negative. Live data shows no transferable chart structure. The only support for a 'go with the move' preference is the 5-year DI-with / box-far-edge effect of about +0.04 R (CF3), worth at most 0.012 ROE.

findings.claim: Only one contrast passed the strict live out-of-sample test: Europe-session signals (16-21 KST) at 15m. It rests on 5 evenings, and over 5 years it is real but about 10x smaller (-0.04 R).
findings.evidence: Direction B: v4 -0.621 R (n 121), then v3a+v3b -0.322 (n 466), one-sided p 0.002, 4h-block p 0.006, BH q 0.011 (out/scan_directional.csv). The pooled per-run 15m values -0.298 / -0.417 / -0.621 / ds200 -0.405 are all negative. 30m: -0.243 / -0.116 / -0.181 / -0.183 (out/scan_full.csv). Per-evening core 15m differences: 10-02 +0.355 (n 40), 10-03 -0.403, 10-04 -0.229, 10-05 -0.371, 10-06 -0.355 (out/session_episodes.csv). Over 5 years: -0.039 R at 15m and -0.021 at 30m, 6/6 and 5/6 years negative. In ROE only -0.003 (out5y/fiveyear_within_strategy.csv).
findings.implication: Use it at most as a mild tie-breaker (deprioritize 15m entries 16-21 KST), never as a hard rule or a reason to pick strategies. It also shows that live effect sizes are inflated about 10x even when the sign is right.

verification.recomputed: 15m Europe minus rest: v4 -0.621 (n 121); v3a+v3b -0.342 (n 466), two-sided p 0.0012 (2h), 0.0032 (4h), 0.046 with KST-day clusters (df 4). After deduplicating identical signal moments: -0.302, day-cluster p 0.049. Long -0.120 (p 0.40) vs short -0.519 (p 0.0001). Per evening (Europe minus same day): 10/02 +0.36, 10/03 -0.43, 10/04 -0.25, 10/05 -0.37, 10/06 -0.36. 5-year: -0.040 / -0.021 R, ROE -0.003.
verification.note: The direction and the 5-year size reproduce. The corrections: (a) the natural unit is the evening, and the out-of-sample set has only 4 evenings, 1 of them with the opposite sign. With day clusters p is about 0.05, not 0.002. (b) The out-of-sample effect is almost entirely in shorts. In the v3b+v4 side-flip it is a direction-skill effect (-0.405, p 0.02), not timing. (c) BH q 0.011 is within a family of 7 carried tests; across all 77 carried out-of-sample tests q is 0.058-0.078. (d) summary.md, read before the pre-registration, already showed negative P&L in every exit hour 16-21 KST, so the session buckets were not chosen blind. The decision stays: a mild tie-breaker at most.

findings.claim: The owners' entry-quality tier, which already drives 50x 'best' leverage, shows no outcome difference live, in line with the 5-year Study B (0 of 410).
findings.evidence: Quality 'best' minus rest, core 36 all runs: 15m +0.008 R (n 532, p 0.92), 30m +0.070 (n 221, p 0.33). Per run at 15m: -0.018, -0.015, +0.064. 'base' minus rest: 15m -0.069 (p 0.48), 30m -0.112 (p 0.15) (out/scan_full.csv). Within side, 15m best -0.017 (out/side_stratified.csv). Prior: research/entry_study/RESULTS_ENTRY.md, B: 0 of 410 strength tests passed.
findings.implication: Leverage scaled by 'confidence' or quality (20-50x) has no evidential basis from entry features. Leverage tiers should not follow AI or quality confidence, because higher leverage on non-better signals only adds variance and liquidation risk.

verification.recomputed: Quality 'best' minus rest, core all runs: 15m +0.004 (n 532, p 0.96), 30m +0.068 (n 223, p 0.35).
verification.note: In v3b/v4 'best' signals get higher leverage (mean 37-39x vs 30x at 15m), so R also carries a leverage effect. v4 R by leverage is almost flat (30x -0.056, 40x -0.046, 50x -0.086), so this does not change the null.

findings.claim: Regime-conditional rules ('trend strategies in trend regimes, mean reversion in boxes') cannot even be tested live: trend regimes were nearly absent. Where testable, live and 5-year results do not support them beyond about 0.04 R.
findings.evidence: Regime counts (peek_dist.py): v4 HTF regime at 15m: chop 1,324, box 609, unknown 117, trend 0. Own-tf 15m: trend_down 151, trend_up 0. v3a 15m: 49 trend signals. Live hypotheses H1-H6 (out/hypotheses.csv): smallest BH q 0.29. H6 (revert better in box than chop) went the wrong way: -0.454 R at 15m core (n_box 48). ER contrasts are null live: 15m high +0.012 (p 0.90), low -0.015.
