DiD 'trend family more ER-sensitive than revert': 15m -0.25 (SE 0.24), 30m +0.31 (SE 0.24) (out/did_er_family.csv). 5-year: H1 +0.044 / +0.024 R, H2 about 0 (out5y/fiveyear_hypotheses.csv). Repo prior docs/regime5y.md: regime switch 0 of 92 cells BH; mean ROE by regime -3.4% to -3.9%.
findings.implication: Do not give AI traders a 'regime gate' as their edge. The current quiet chop market would leave trend strategies idle and not profitable.

verification.recomputed: v4 15m signals with an outcome (core + ds200): HTF regime chop 1,269, box 584, unknown 52, trend 0. Own-tf trend_down 68, trend_up 0. v3a 15m own-tf trend 42.
verification.note: The counts differ from the claim (151, 49) because I counted only signals with a resolved R, but the conclusion is the same: trend regimes were nearly absent. I did not recompute H1-H6. 5-year ER and DI figures as in CF3.

findings.claim: The robust 'context' is mechanical cost: signals whose 2 ATR stop is wide relative to the round trip do better in R. In money (ROE) the gain is small.
findings.evidence: 5-year within strategy, wide minus rest: 15m +0.163 R (z 35), 30m +0.102 R (6/6 years). In ROE only +0.003 / +0.006 (out5y/fiveyear_within_strategy.csv). 5-year H7, wide minus tight: +0.264 / +0.144 R (out5y/fiveyear_hypotheses.csv). Live: 15m +0.180 (p1s 0.10), 30m +0.138 (p1s 0.068), v4 15m alone -0.237 (out/hypotheses.csv). Live 15m median 2 ATR stop is 0.59% of price (peek_dist.py). The established median round trip is 0.22 R at 15m vs 0.16 R at 30m.
findings.implication: The defensible custom value is cost-aware: prefer 30m (and 1h) over 15m, and skip or downsize entries whose stop is under about 0.5% of price. Because ROE gains are tiny at fixed margin and leverage, this reduces drag rather than creating profit.

verification.recomputed: Live wide minus tight: 15m +0.206 (p 0.14), 30m +0.143 (p 0.13); v3a 15m +0.336, v4 15m -0.237. In v3a, tight-stop signals ran at 49.5x mean leverage and wide ones at 30.3x. Wide minus rest within leverage strata: 15m -0.003, 30m +0.071 (raw +0.288 / +0.219). 5-year, same 30x group, mean ROE: 15m tight -0.043 vs wide -0.043; 30m tight -0.039 vs wide -0.045. In R: 15m -0.398 vs -0.138.
verification.note: The live support is a v3a leverage artifact. The 5-year R effect is real, but in money it is zero: at the bot's fixed margin x leverage sizing, wide- and tight-stop signals have the same ROE. The R gain is a units effect (same P&L divided by a larger risk). So 'skip stops under 0.5%' and 'prefer 30m over 15m for cost' save no money unless sizing becomes risk-based (fixed USD risk per trade). The claim's own implication ('reduces drag') overstates the benefit.

findings.claim: Per-strategy context tests: 25 were testable, 1 survived BH (N18_VWMA_MACD 15m, low-ER signals much worse, consistent across 3 runs). Over 5 years the same contrast is +0.03 R, about 35x smaller.
findings.evidence: out/per_strategy_live.csv (per_strategy.py): 25 testable (at least 10 per side), 2 raw p<0.05, 1 with BH q<0.05. N18 15m high minus low ER: +1.068 R (q 0.00005). Low-ER mean R per run: -1.29 (n 7), -0.39 (14), -0.82 (21); high-ER: -0.28 (88), +0.47 (6), +0.50 (16). Low-ER losers come in bursts (6 BTC/ETH longs within one hour on 10-06). Over 5 years N18 15m: +0.029 R (z 2.0), 30m -0.010 (out5y/fiveyear_hypotheses.csv). The 5-year trend family as a whole: +0.044 R at 15m.
findings.implication: Strategy-specific 'custom' context rules found on days of live data are almost always noise or hugely inflated. A rule like 'skip low-ER signals' for trend strategies has to be sized from 5-year data (about 0.03-0.05 R), not from live data.

verification.recomputed: N18_VWMA_MACD 15m high minus low ER: +1.114 R (2h p<1e-4; day-cluster p 0.002, df 5). Low-ER means per run -1.37 (n 7), -0.39 (14), -0.82 (21); high-ER -0.28 (88), +0.47 (6), +0.50 (16). The low-ER signals fall in only 4 / 4 / 6 two-hour blocks. 5-year +0.029 (z 2.1) at 15m, -0.010 at 30m.
verification.note: This is 1 survivor out of 25 per-strategy tests, in a lens with about 2,400 tests in total. It is about 38x larger live than over 5 years. The conclusion stands.

findings.claim: No context changes the strategies' direction skill. The side-flip decomposition finds nothing after BH; where a context matters, it matters for both directions (timing or volatility).
findings.evidence: out/sideflip_by_context.csv (analysis2.py, v3b+v4 replay, 216 testable bucket contrasts): R, any-direction mean (R+flip)/2 and direction skill (R-flip)/2 each have 0 with BH q<0.10. Raw p<0.05 counts are 16, 19 and 21 against about 11 expected. Example, middle of the HTF box at 15m core: d_R -0.230, any-direction -0.242 (p 0.002), direction skill +0.012 (p 0.96).
findings.implication: An AI cannot plausibly know in which contexts the strategy's direction call is right. Any contextual benefit is about when to trade at all, which is mostly the cost and volatility channel.

verification.recomputed: Reduced side-flip check (10 binary contexts x core/ds200 x 15m/30m = 40 tests, v3b+v4 replay; verify3/c3.py). Direction skill: 4 raw p<0.05, 0 BH q<0.10. Any-direction: 4 p<0.05, 4 q<0.10. HTF middle 15m core: dR -0.230, direction +0.012 (p 0.96), any-direction -0.242 (p 0.002). This reproduces the claimed example.
verification.note: 'Nothing survives BH for direction skill' holds. The generalization that context matters only for both directions does not: the one context that replicates across runs, 15m Europe, is a direction-skill effect in v3b+v4 (direction -0.405, p 0.02; any-direction -0.129, p 0.08), concentrated in shorts.

findings.claim: The support/resistance context is nearly constant, so it cannot filter. Consensus or conflict among strategies is noise.
findings.evidence: Share with level_before_lock=1: 85-97%. Share with support_before_stop=1: 96-100%. Median room to the next level 0.22-0.39 ATR (out/signals_bucketed.csv, per run and tf). Repo prior: research/entry_study/RESULTS_ENTRY.md, A: 2 of 290 S/R candidates, both market-wide. Consensus >=4 at 30m: live +0.438 R within side (z 2.4, out/side_stratified.csv) vs 5-year +0.014 (out5y/fiveyear_within_strategy.csv). At 15m: +0.173 live vs +0.006 over 5 years.
findings.implication: Give the AI no weight for 'resistance just ahead' or 'several strategies agree'. Neither is evidence for an entry, and these are exactly the stories a human-like LLM finds persuasive.

verification.recomputed: level_before_lock share 0.85-0.97, support_before_stop 0.955-1.00, median room 0.22-0.39 ATR (per run x tf). 5-year consensus>=4: +0.013 / +0.014 R.
verification.note: Near-constant S/R flags; consensus is negligible over 5 years. Note that 52% of core signals share an identical run/tf/coin/bar/side moment with another strategy, so 'consensus' is partly duplicated rows.

findings.claim: Discovery-then-test is not much helped by switching the strategy set either. Contexts found on core 36 (v3a) replicated on DeepSeek (v4) for 1 of 26 contrasts, and that one fails on core 36 in v3b+v4.
findings.evidence: out/scan_directional.csv, direction T: 115 discovery tests, 28 carried, 26 testable, 2 one-sided p<0.05, 1 replicated: 15m middle of the HTF box, v3a -0.335 then ds200 v4 -0.575 (q 0.016, 4h p 0.005). The same contrast on core 36 in v3b+v4: -0.252 (p1s 0.144), and in v3b alone +0.516 (out/scan_full.csv). Over 5 years: -0.030 R (15m) and -0.013 (30m) within strategy.
findings.implication: DeepSeek accounts cannot be graded on context either: 1.5 days, no cross-run replication, no 5-year context data. Treat them as untested.

verification.recomputed: Direction T (v3a core -> v4 ds200): 15m HTF middle v3a -0.358 -> ds200 -0.575, p1 0.0007. 15m Europe also carried over (v3a -0.324 -> ds200 -0.405, p1 0.002 in my SE; the analyst's own 4h p1 0.023 fails their rule). HTF middle on core v3b+v4: -0.252 (p1 0.144). 5-year -0.031 / -0.013.
verification.note: Confirmed. Across all 77 carried out-of-sample tests, HTF middle has q 0.047. ds200 includes identical duplicate signal streams (F11_RAID = F11_TSOUP = F13_RAID_PD etc.), so its n overstates the information; time-block clustering only partly absorbs this.

strategy_note_problems: N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m: all 56 live signals are shorts (long share 0.00) in mostly falling v3b/v4 markets. The positive side-flip (+0.36) and v4 +0.28 R are direction luck. The note does not say so.
Side-flip figures are (R - flip)/2 over v3b+v4 replays only (e.g. S4_BB_BBP 15m +0.390 = half of +0.779 on 39 signals), not labelled as half-differences or as excluding v3a.

N07_ICHI_CMO 30m is called the only core cell not clearly negative after 5-year filtering. With my filter, N17_KC_RSI 30m (-0.036, 6,327 kept) and N19_FIB_CHOP 15m (-0.040) are equally close, and N07's own SE (+/-0.027) overlaps them. It is not unique.

DeepSeek notes (F3_HHHL, F7_RF_TRIPLE, F6_VWAP_CROSS) rest on 2 KST days. F3_HHHL is 68% short in a falling market. Their positive side-flips are likely direction luck, and duplicate DeepSeek streams are not mentioned.
'C+' grades go to cells whose 5-year filtered mean is negative and whose live cluster SE is 0.15-0.45 R. The grade does not match the owners' 'not losing' criterion.
v3a cell means mix 20-50x leverage, and v3a R falls with leverage. Per-run v3a figures (e.g. N17_KC_RSI 15m -0.55, N25_DST_CCI 15m -0.67) are partly leverage, not strategy.
Sample check: S4_BB_BBP 15m/30m, N18 15m, N25 15m, N01 15m, N10 30m, N20 30m, N17 15m and F3/F7/F6/F4 15m reproduce within about 0.04 R (v3a varies slightly because of the R conversion).
verifier_missed: v3a leverage confound: mean R of core 15m+30m signals in v3a is -0.086 at 20x, -0.169 at 30x, -0.248 at 40x and -0.449 at 50x (the ROE-based ladder locks earlier at high leverage). Leverage was set by stop width (tight 49.5x vs wide 30.3x). Any v3a context correlated with stop width or leverage is biased, and v3a is the discovery set for directions A and T.
R versus money: at fixed margin x leverage, the 5-year stop-width R effect has zero ROE effect within the same leverage group. R-based 'cost' filters do not improve P&L unless sizing is risk-based.
Session buckets were not blind: summary.md (read before the pre-registration) showed negative P&L in every exit hour 16-21 KST.
The Europe effect is direction-specific (shorts) and a direction-skill effect in the side-flip. With evening clusters the out-of-sample test has 4 evenings (p about 0.05).

Duplicates: 3,646 core signals contain only 2,485 unique (run, tf, coin, bar, side) moments; 52% sit in duplicate groups. Tests count them as independent rows. After deduplication Europe is still p 0.002 (2h) but 0.049 (day).

Multiple testing: about 2,400 test rows across the lens tables, with BH applied only within small families (for example 7 carried tests). Across all 77 carried out-of-sample tests the best q is 0.047 (HTF middle) and 0.058-0.078 for Europe.
The live learned-filter results (CF6) are specification-fragile. A reasonable alternative ridge reverses the v4->v3a+v3b direction.

findings.claim: None of the 9 pre-declared discretionary-proxy exit rules helps out of sample. Zero rule x group cells pass the pre-registered test (positive in both v3b and v4, and BH q < 0.05). The best results are small: on core 30m, CUT05 (hard stop at -0.5R) +0.043R, NP4 (exit if no +0.3R within 4 bars) +0.032R and NP8 +0.021R. All three are positive in both runs but not significant, against a base of -0.146R.
findings.evidence: lens/ai_upside/out/rules_stats.csv. Built by rules_replay.py and rules_stats.py: every SUBMITTED signal run alone through the repo's PaperEngine on 1m live_bars. The base reproduces replay_signals.csv R exactly (max diff 0.0 on 4,236 traded and 410 open signals). Core 30m CUT05: n=639 (v3b 201 / v4 438), 53 hour-clusters, diff +0.043 (v3b +0.082, v4 +0.025), cluster-bootstrap CI -0.019..+0.101, two-sided sign-flip p 0.165, BH q 0.79. NP4: +0.032 (+0.053 / +0.022), p 0.22. 1h CUT05: +0.034, mixed by run (+0.163 / -0.018). Results are the same with open-at-end trades excluded (30m CUT05 +0.054). Lowest BH q anywhere is 0.029, and it is a HURT cell: DeepSeek 15m OPPH -0.061R.
findings.implication: Exit discretion cannot lift any timeframe's base (-0.08 to -0.15R per signal) to break-even. Do not choose AI traders, or AI timeframes, because of exit headroom. At most, put a 30m/1h loss-cut into code as a shadow rule. That is free and needs no Sonnet calls.

verification.recomputed: Own replay v3rep.py (every SUBMITTED house signal of v3b+v4 run alone through the repo PaperEngine; base parity with replay_signals.csv R: 4,646 signals, max diff 0.0); stats v3st.py -> v3rules.csv. Core 30m CUT05 +0.045 (v3b +0.077, v4 +0.030; cluster CI -0.012..+0.099; p 0.127; q 0.77; 53 clusters); NP4 +0.032 (+0.053/+0.022); NP8 +0.021. No rule x group cell passes (positive in both runs and q<0.05). Lowest q 0.036 = DeepSeek 15m OPPH, a hurt cell (-0.061).
verification.note: Numbers reproduce. Caveats: (1) PREREG.md mtime 08:56:38 is later than rules_replay.py (08:44:50) and rules_signals.csv (08:45:16) because the addenda were appended to the same file, so 'written before running' cannot be verified from the file. The run matches the text except CUT05, which used the entry price where PREREG says the reference price; this does not matter (the PREREG version gives +0.045). (2) CUT05 is a resting 1m hard stop at -0.5R, which is a tighter code stop, not discretion. The AI-visible version (close at the signal-tf bar close when <= -0.5R, CUT05C) gives core 30m +0.012, DeepSeek 30m +0.001, core 15m -0.041.

findings.claim: Human-style early profit-taking and breakeven moves cost R at 15m. They save the trades that would have hit SL, but they kill more trades that would later have won.
findings.evidence: rules_stats.csv, pooled v3b+v4. Core 15m (n=1,252): BE05 -0.058, TP1 (+1R take-profit, ladder kept) -0.063, PART1 (half off at +1R) -0.031. DeepSeek 15m (n=1,172, v4 only): BE05 -0.082, TP1 -0.095, PART1 -0.048. By run these are mixed: core BE05 is +0.076 in v3b and -0.120 in v4. rule_tradeoff.csv for BE05 on core 15m: it helped 138 trades by +1.24R each and hurt 245 trades by -0.99R each. Break-even needs 44.6% of the changed trades to be helped; the actual share was 36.0%. For TP1 the break-even share is 74.2%; actual 58.3%. disposition.csv: a trade still open 2 bars in at >= +0.3R did better held than exited, by +0.19R (n=334, CI -0.07..+0.40; v3b +0.18, v4 +0.19).
findings.implication: The AI prompt and code should not let a 15m trader take profit or move to breakeven below the ladder's first rung (about +0.86R at 30x). Allow it only after the AI's calls show more than 45% precision against twin code accounts. 'Trade like a human' (take quick profits, hold losers) is the wrong way round here.

verification.note: The point estimates reproduce exactly, but none is significant and in v3b all three core rules HELPED. 'Early profit-taking/breakeven costs R at 15m' is not established. The supported statement is 'not shown to help; the pooled estimate is negative, driven by v4'. At 30m/1h BE05 is about 0 to slightly positive (+0.011/+0.005). Keeping a default of no profit-taking below the first rung is reasonable, but as an unproven default, not a measured cost.

findings.claim: One state-based exit was consistent across runs and kinds: at 30m and 1h, a trade still open after 4 bars at <= -0.5R did worse if held than if closed then, by about 0.2-0.3R. This was found after the fact. At 15m the same state gives the opposite sign.
findings.evidence: disposition.csv (exit-now cost included; cluster bootstrap by run x hour). 30m: n=74, hold minus exit -0.220R, CI -0.320..-0.081, p 0.010 (v3b -0.242 n12, v4 -0.216 n62; core -0.231, DeepSeek -0.209). 1h: n=58, -0.287R, CI -0.376..-0.188, p < 0.001 (v3b -0.351, v4 -0.272). 15m: n=202, +0.122, mixed (v3b -0.154, v4 +0.166). The 30m cell surfaced in a scan of about 100 state cells (exit_now_by_state.csv, BH q 0.32), so it counts as a discovery, not a confirmation.
findings.implication: Shadow-test 'close at market if <= -0.5R after 4 bars' at 30m/1h as a code rule; about 11-12% of trades open at bar 4 hit this state. If it holds up, roughly +0.03R per signal sits in code at zero AI cost. It is not a reason to pay for an AI.

verification.recomputed: v3more.py (engine exit at the 4th tf bar close vs hold): 30m <= -0.5R n 74, -0.219 (CI -0.316..-0.069, p 0.010; v3b -0.242, v4 -0.215); 1h n 58, -0.286 (p<0.001, 14 clusters); 15m +0.122 (mixed). Threshold check: 30m <= -0.3R +0.006 (v4 +0.064, opposite sign); <= -0.7R -0.152. 1h <= -0.3/-0.5/-0.7: -0.247/-0.286/-0.201. Per-signal value of the rule (DEEP4): core 30m +0.014, core 1h +0.021, DeepSeek 30m +0.012, DeepSeek 1h +0.022, core 15m -0.013, DeepSeek 15m -0.007. Share in the state among trades open at bar 4: 30m 11.4%, 1h 19.1%.
verification.note: The state cell reproduces, but the analysis was not pre-registered (post hoc, as the analyst says). At 30m it depends on the -0.5R cutoff: at -0.3R it vanishes. It is robust at 1h, but with only 14 hour-clusters. The stated '+0.03R per signal' is about double the recomputed +0.012..+0.022, and '11-12% of trades' holds for 30m but is 19% at 1h. Worth a code shadow, mainly at 1h.

findings.claim: Giveback exists but is mostly a 15m effect, and it happens before the ROE ladder arms. 11-15% of 15m signals reach +0.5R and still stop out at about -1.2R. At 30m+ the ladder catches almost every +1R trade.
findings.evidence: giveback_kind_tf.csv, every-signal replay v3b+v4, share reaching +0.5R then SL: core 15m 10.6%, 30m 4.7%, 1h 1.5%; DeepSeek 15m 14.8%, 30m 5.5%, 1h 1.6%. Reached +1R then SL: 0-1.7%. Real trades, all 3 runs: core 15m 8.3% (n=630), DeepSeek 15m 17.4% (n=259). giveback_first_rung.csv: share that reached +1R but closed on the first 10% ROE lock: v3a core 15m 9.5% (50x tier walk), v3b 6.8%, v4 8.6%, v4 DeepSeek 15m 15.1%; those trades kept +0.60..+0.80R of an MFE of 1.12..1.68R. Hindsight upper bounds per trade (perfect breakeven on losers that saw +0.5R, plus cutting dead losers at -0.5R): core 15m 0.24R, 30m 0.15, 1h 0.12; DeepSeek 15m 0.31, 30m 0.19, 1h 0.14. Exiting exactly at MFE: 0.56-0.90R.
findings.implication: The theoretical room for AI exits is largest at 15m (about 0.24-0.31R per trade at most). AIH-1 and AIH-2 show that simple capture of it fails there, so any 15m exit edge would have to come from information beyond the price path. At 30m+ the code ladder already does most of what a human trailing stop would do.

verification.recomputed: v3more.py: share of signals reaching +0.5R and then SL: core 15m 10.6%, 30m 4.7%, 1h 1.5%; DeepSeek 14.8% / 5.5% / 1.6%; reached +1R then SL 0-1.7%. Hindsight upper bound (breakeven on losers that saw +0.5R, plus dead losers cut at -0.5R) by my definition: core 0.27 / 0.16 / 0.12; DeepSeek 0.34 / 0.21 / 0.14 (lens: 0.24/0.15/0.12 and 0.31/0.19/0.14).
verification.note: The giveback shares reproduce exactly. The headroom bounds have the same order, with a slightly different definition of a dead loser, and they are clearly labelled as hindsight upper bounds. The real-trade and first-rung (v3a) figures were not recomputed.

findings.claim: Most losers are dead from the start, and most stop-outs peak in the first 2 bars. Even so, cutting at -0.5R only breaks even at 15m, because it also kills trades that recover.
findings.evidence: time_to_mfe_stop.csv, every-signal base. Losers whose MFE never passed +0.2R: core 45% (15m), 45% (30m), 51% (1h); DeepSeek 48%, 55%, 63%. SL trades whose best price came within 2 bars: 62% / 63% / 77% (core). Median bars to SL: 5.9 (15m), 5.9 (30m), 5.0 (1h); dead SL trades 3.7 / 4.1 / 3.7 bars. Median bars to +0.3R about 1.3-1.5; to +0.5R about 2.6-3.3; reach +1R: 23% (core 15m), 8% (core 30m). Median MAE before +0.5R: -0.26R. rule_tradeoff.csv CUT05 on core 15m: helped 550 trades (+0.49R each), hurt 197 (-1.43R each); break-even precision 74.6%, actual 73.6%. On 30m: 69.1% needed, 74.6% actual.
findings.implication: A 15m AI sees only 3-4 bar closes before a dead trade stops out, and price state alone does not separate dead trades from recovering ones there. At 30m the cut works slightly, because hurt trades lose less (-1.08R vs -1.43R at 15m).

verification.recomputed: v3more.py: share of losers whose MFE never reached +0.2R: core 45/45/51%, DeepSeek 48/55/63% (15m/30m/1h), as claimed. CUT05 at 15m: core -0.006, DeepSeek -0.021 (break-even or worse), at 30m +0.045.
verification.note: Bar-timing medians (bars to SL, bars to +0.3R) and the rule_tradeoff precision figures were not recomputed. The shares that were checked match.

findings.claim: AI exit headroom is a property of the timeframe and of how bad the entries were in that run. It is not a stable property of a strategy. A per-strategy headroom ranking does not replicate.
findings.evidence: headroom_stability.csv, core cells with >= 10 signals in both runs. Spearman of hindsight headroom, v3b vs v4: 15m -0.07 (13 cells), 30m +0.24 (9). v3a trades vs v4 signals: -0.31 (17), -0.52 (9). Per-cell base mean R, v3b vs v4: -0.10 (15m), +0.07 (30m). CUT05 cell gains, v3b vs v4: -0.39 / -0.28. Across cells (headroom_rank.csv), the rule gain is strongly negatively correlated with the cell's base R: CUT05 -0.82 (15m), -0.73 (30m), -0.52 (1h); BE05 -0.87 (15m). Headroom vs base R: -0.60 / -0.42 / -0.86. The core cells with base >= 0 in both runs (N10_HA_PSAR@15m, N17_KC_RSI@15m, N20_EMA9_CHOP@30m, N24_DMI@30m) have headroom 0.08-0.27 and no rule gain in both runs.
findings.implication: Rank AI potential by timeframe, not by strategy. Cells graded H1 ('headroom, rule-consistent') are mostly bad entries being trimmed. Choose AI strategies on entry evidence (5-year results, the side-flip test; other lenses), and treat 'more room for AI exits' as a symptom of bad entries.

verification.recomputed: v3more.py, core cells with >= 10 signals in both runs: Spearman headroom v3b vs v4 15m -0.03 (13 cells), 30m +0.26 (9); base R -0.10 / +0.07; CUT05 gain -0.37 / -0.52. Across cells, CUT05 gain vs base R: -0.85 (15m, 22 cells), -0.56 (30m, 17).
verification.note: Same conclusion. With 9-13 cells these correlations carry about +-0.6 uncertainty, so 'does not replicate' should read 'no evidence that it replicates'. The negative gain-vs-base link is partly mechanical: low-base cells have the deep stop-outs that a cut trims.

findings.claim: Switching to a new signal while in position lost money under every pre-declared policy, in both runs. The loss per switch is about the cost of the extra round trip (about $63 at 30x with margin = 30% of equity), so the replacement signal was no better than the remainder of the held trade.
findings.evidence: switch_sim.py, account-level re-simulation of each account's own signal stream. The base reproduces all 366 accounts' trade counts and closed pnl (max diff $1.2e-10). switch_summary.csv, switch-on-every-new-signal policy: core -$54/switch at 15m (590 switches), -$73 at 30m (257), -$102 at 1h (140); v3b -$50, v4 -$71; 49% of accounts worse vs 16% better. DeepSeek -$28 / -$48 / -$67. Switch only when under water: core -$77/switch (674). Reversal on own opposite signal: core -$210 (26), DeepSeek -$98 (58). Switch only stale trades: core -$72 (114; v3b +$69 on 17 switches), DeepSeek +$3 (122). Signal level (skipped_vs_held.csv): switching to the skipped signal changed equity by -2.07% per instance (core n=1,296, CI -2.69..-1.45; v3b -1.31%, v4 -2.31%), -2.68% when the held trade was under water (n=691), DeepSeek -0.67% (n=1,219). v3a nightly skipped shadows: in-position skips averaged ROE -0.079 vs entered trades -0.037 (15m).
findings.implication: Make 'hold' the default and gate any switch in code. A switch must clear an expected gain greater than one round trip, about 0.22R at 15m and 1.26% of equity at 30x. Do not count switching as an AI upside.

verification.recomputed: Own account-level re-simulation v3acct.py (each account's own signal stream through one engine; parity 366/366 accounts on trade count, closed pnl max diff $1.2e-10). Switch on every new signal: core -$54 / -$73 / -$102 per switch at 15m/30m/1h (590/257/140 switches); v3b -$50, v4 -$71; DeepSeek -$28 / -$49 / -$66. Switch only under water: core -$78 per switch over 550 switches (lens: -$77 over 674). Selection check (v3ev.py, v3x.py): signals SKIPPED 'in position' vs signals ENTERED, each run alone: core 15m -0.066 vs -0.218 (diff +0.151, cluster CI +0.001..+0.296; v3b skipped -0.44, v4 +0.07); DeepSeek 15m 0.000 vs -0.293 (+0.293, CI +0.087..+0.484, v4 only); 30m/1h about equal or worse.
verification.note: The dollar results reproduce. But (1) only switching to another signal of the same strategy and timeframe was tested. The planned trader spans timeframes, and lens2_multi_tf (MT6, 5 years) finds switching only to a HIGHER timeframe the best rule (+0.015R vs first-come, 29/35 strategies). 'Do not count switching as an AI upside' overreaches; the supported statement is 'same-tf switch-on-any-signal loses about one round trip'. (2) 'The replacement signal was no better' does not hold at 15m: the in-position skipped signals were BETTER than the signals the accounts entered. The switching loss comes from cutting held trades whose remainders were good, plus the extra round trip, not from bad new signals. (3) The signal-level -2.07% per instance counts several skipped instances per held trade (not independent); not recomputed.

findings.claim: Entering a missed signal 1-4 bars late performs about like entering on time, slightly worse at 15m/30m. Recycling missed signals adds trades at the same (negative) base value, each paying full costs.
findings.evidence: late_lev_summary.csv, same signal re-entered k bars of its timeframe later with a fresh 2 ATR stop (paired). Core 15m: 1 bar late -0.026R (v3b +0.047, v4 -0.059; CI -0.106..+0.058), 4 bars -0.115. Core 30m: -0.045 / -0.086 / -0.065. Core 1h: +0.043 / +0.063 / +0.066 (CIs include 0). DeepSeek 15m: 1 bar late -0.082 (CI -0.159..-0.008), 4 bars -0.151.
findings.implication: Design D12's near-signal and missed-signal entries are unlikely to add edge. If allowed, cap them and score them separately, as the design already plans. They should not be counted as AI headroom.

verification.recomputed: v3rep.py late entry (k bars later, fresh 2 ATR stop from that 1m open), v3more.py: core 15m 1 bar -0.026 (CI -0.110..+0.058; v3b +0.047, v4 -0.059), 4 bars -0.115; core 30m -0.045 / -0.065; core 1h +0.043 / +0.066 (CIs span 0); DeepSeek 15m -0.082 (CI -0.158..-0.013) / -0.151.
verification.note: Exact match. At 1h, late entries are not worse (point estimates positive, not significant).

findings.claim: Leverage changes the exits, because the ladder locks a fixed ROE. On the same signals, higher leverage gave lower R. Above 30x most 15m/30m signals cannot be sized at all under the 2 ATR stop and the 15% max-loss cap.
findings.evidence: lev_pairs.csv, paired fixed leverage with margin = leverage%. 30x vs 20x: -0.026R (core 15m, n=1,252), -0.045 (30m), -0.046 (1h). 40x vs 30x: -0.104 (core 15m, n=976), -0.109 (DeepSeek 15m, CI -0.229..-0.005), -0.135 (DeepSeek 30m, CI -0.282..-0.024). 40x rejected 276 of 1,252 core 15m signals that 30x took; 50x was possible for only 179; at 30m/1h, 40x+ is almost never possible. ladder_geometry.csv: the first lock arms at 1.18 / 0.86 / 0.70 / 0.61R at 20 / 30 / 40 / 50x on 15m (median stop 0.63%), and at 0.84 / 0.61 / 0.50 / 0.43R on 30m. Loss at the stop with margin = lev%: 15m 6.9% of equity at 30x, 19.1% at 50x.
findings.implication: '20-50x by AI confidence' is mostly infeasible above 30x on 15m/30m, and where feasible it quietly tightens the exits. Define the code exits in R (price), not ROE, so a leverage choice does not change the exit. Check whether confidence predicts outcomes (twin accounts) before letting it scale exposure, which grows about 6x from 20x to 50x at margin = lev%.

verification.recomputed: v3rep.py fixed leverage (tiers set to L with margin L%), v3more.py: 30x-20x core -0.026 / -0.045 / -0.046 (15m/30m/1h, p 0.76/0.38/0.29; core 15m v3b +0.013); 40x-30x core 15m -0.104 (p 0.12), DeepSeek 15m -0.109 (p 0.078), DeepSeek 30m -0.135 (p 0.036). Sizable at 20/30/40x: core 15m 1252/1252/976; core 30m 639/630/212; core 1h 406/320/9; DeepSeek 30m 620/618/250.
verification.note: The paired values reproduce, but the core differences are not significant. '40x+ almost never possible at 30m' is wrong: 40x sizes 33% of core and 40% of DeepSeek 30m signals. At 1h, 40x is about 2% (9/406) and even 30x only 79%. So the 1h AI cannot scale leverage by confidence beyond 20-30x. 50x was not rechecked.

findings.claim: At 15m, the open trade's P&L state carries no stable exit signal. Whether exiting early would have helped is set by the run's market regime, not by a repeatable state rule.
findings.evidence: exit_now_by_state.csv, hold value minus exit-now value at 1, 2 and 4 bars by unrealized-R bin, with cluster bootstrap: no state cell is BH-significant (min q 0.32). Core 15m, all open trades at 2 bars: v3b -0.17R, v4 +0.22R (opposite signs). Per-cell CIs typically span +-0.3R.
findings.implication: An AI watching only the 15m price path is unlikely to beat code exits. Any 15m exit edge must come from other information (news, order flow, higher-tf context), and must be shown with paired twin accounts, not assumed.

verification.recomputed: v3more.py: core 15m, all trades open at 2 bars, hold minus exit-now: v3b -0.174, v4 +0.223, pooled +0.105 (CI -0.045..+0.276, 53 clusters).
verification.note: Opposite signs by run, as claimed. The full state-cell scan with BH was not redone.

findings.claim: Events and big moves: the window held only one scheduled macro event (NFP 10/02 21:30 KST, v3a), and it did no harm. Entries in or just after the biggest-move hours did better, not worse. Holding against a big move looked costly, but the cluster counts are tiny.
findings.evidence: events_macro.csv: data/macro_events.csv has only NFP 2026-10-02 12:30Z inside the runs. v3a trades entered within 2h: -0.091R (n=163, incl. 5m); trades held through the release +0.48R (n=37); other v3a trades -0.45R. events_bighours.csv, top-decile hours of the 6-coin 1h return (v4: 10/07 00:00, 10:00, 11:00 down, 14:00 up). v4 core signals entered in a big-move hour +0.31R (n=253), the hour after +0.19 (n=241), others -0.14 (n=1,226). v3b: -0.23 / -0.41 / -0.33. events_bighour_hold_vs_exit.csv, positions open at a big hour's end: against the move, hold minus exit -0.13 to -0.36R (core 30m/1h, DeepSeek); with the move +0.15 to +0.78R. Only 3-5 hour-clusters.
findings.implication: Do not build 'avoid volatile hours' logic. A 'cut positions against a big move, keep those with it' reaction is plausible; log it as a code shadow and judge it after many more events (CPI 10/14, FOMC 10/28, PCE 10/29).

verification.recomputed: data/macro_events.csv has 4 rows only (NFP 10/02, CPI 10/14, FOMC 10/28, PCE 10/29): one inside the runs. v3x.py, v3a trades around NFP 12:30Z (entries in [12:30, 14:30)Z): n 119, R -0.252 (lens n 163, -0.091); held through: n 39, +0.385 (lens 37, +0.48); others -0.448. Big hours (v3ev.py, top decile of 6-coin mean |1h return|): v4 4 hours, v3b 2. v4 core entries in a big hour +0.314 (n 253), hour after +0.114 (n 146; lens +0.19, n 241), others -0.140; v3b -0.229 / -0.406 / -0.334.
verification.note: 'Only one scheduled macro event' is true only of the repo list, which covers just NFP/CPI/FOMC/PCE. Second-tier US releases (e.g. ISM Services PMI, normally Mon 10/05 14:00Z inside v3b; JOLTS) and crypto-specific news were not checked (not verifiable here). NFP is one event, one cluster, in v3a, which has no live_bars for a replay. The big hours are picked after the fact (look-ahead), with 2-4 clusters. These data cannot say anything about event reactions either way; the implication (log it as a shadow and judge later) is right.

findings.claim: Skipping signals because other strategies disagree shows no reliable effect once look-ahead is removed. The naive version, which counts signals up to 15 min after entry, exaggerates the effect.
findings.evidence: agreement.csv, AI-visible window (signals in the 15 min before entry). Conflict minus agree: core 15m -0.019R (CI -0.31..+0.24), 30m -0.152 (CI -0.38..+0.07), 1h +0.049; DeepSeek 15m -0.161 (CI -0.52..+0.17). In v3b, conflict was not worse (15m -0.33 vs -0.41 for agree). agreement_leaky.csv (+-15 min window): core 15m conflict -0.217 vs agree -0.090.
findings.implication: No demonstrated skip rule from cross-strategy agreement. Any replay or evaluation of AI decisions must make sure the AI never sees bars after its decision; the leaky version shows how easily a fake skip edge appears.

verification.recomputed: v3ev.py, AI-visible window [bar close - 15 min, bar close], other accounts' SUBMITTED signals on the same coin; conflict minus agree: core 15m +0.034 (CI -0.19..+0.26; v3b +0.078, v4 -0.021), 30m -0.094 (CI -0.32..+0.12), 1h +0.049 (v3b +0.34, v4 -0.08), DeepSeek 15m -0.188 (CI -0.51..+0.12).
verification.note: Values differ a little from the lens (core 15m -0.019, 30m -0.152; probably different counting), but every CI spans 0 and signs change by run, so the conclusion of no reliable skip rule stands. The leaky window was not recomputed.

findings.claim: Exiting on the strategy's own opposite signal, at the same or a higher timeframe, lowered R at 15m in pooled data (driven by v4). Using reversals as exit or switch triggers is not supported.
findings.evidence: rules_stats.csv, all non-coin-flip kinds, 15m, n=2,424: exit on same-tf opposite signal -0.025R (CI -0.045..-0.009, p 0.004); same-or-higher tf -0.041R (CI -0.074..-0.013, p 0.004). v3b about 0 (-0.001 / +0.014), v4 -0.030 / -0.051. DeepSeek 15m same-or-higher tf -0.061R, BH q 0.029 (the only BH-significant cell in the family). The reversal switch policy lost $98-210 per switch (AIH-7).
findings.implication: Tell the AI not to treat the strategy's own opposite signal as a reason to exit or reverse at 15m/30m.

verification.note: The pooled result comes from DeepSeek 15m in v4 (single run). For the core 36 it is not significant and has mixed sign by run at 15m. At 30m it is slightly POSITIVE in both runs. 'Do not use the opposite signal at 15m/30m' is supported only for DeepSeek 15m. For core it is simply unproven either way.

findings.claim: Ranking by AI headroom: 30m is the only timeframe with a consistent, small exit improvement (about +0.03-0.05R per signal). 1h is similar but is planned as a rule account. 15m has the most theoretical room but nothing that captures it, and the worst costs (about 0.22R round trip). 4h has too few signals.
findings.evidence: Per signal: core 30m CUT05 +0.043, NP4 +0.032, deep-loser cut about +0.22R on about 12% of trades. Core 15m: no rule positive in both runs except NP4 (about 0.000). Trades per account-day (trades_per_account_day.csv): about 4-6 at 15m, 2.3-3.8 at 30m, 1.3-2.9 at 1h. So at 30m the plausible exit gain is about +0.1-0.16R per account-day against a base of about -0.37 to -0.55R per day. Grade counts (headroom_rank.csv), with N meaning too few signals: core 15m H1 3 / H2 12 / L 6 / N 11; core 30m H1 1 / H2 1 / L 12 / N 18; DeepSeek 15m H1 10 (v4 only) / H2 15 / L 1 / N 18; DeepSeek 30m H1 2 / H2 7 / L 9 / N 23.
findings.implication: For the AI budget: if AI traders run at 15m/30m, their value must come from entries and skips (not shown here; see other lenses). Exits should stay code (ladder plus possibly a 30m/1h loss-cut). Prefer 30m over 15m for AI traders. Measure the AI's realized contribution against paired twin code accounts, because the headroom figures are hindsight upper bounds, not expected values.

verification.recomputed: From v3rules.csv and v3more.py: the 30m 'consistent improvement' is CUT05 (a resting 1m hard stop, p 0.13, q 0.77) and core NP4 (+0.032). DeepSeek 30m NP4 is -0.004 (v4 only). The AI-visible bar-close cut gives +0.012 (core 30m) and +0.001 (DeepSeek 30m). The state cut is +0.014/signal at 30m and +0.021 at 1h (robust to the threshold only at 1h).
verification.note: The '+0.1-0.16R per account-day' multiplies non-significant point estimates by trades per day. It is an optimistic ceiling, not an expected gain. The only cut that held up beyond its cutoff is at 1h, which the 10/7 update now puts in scope for AI entries. 'Prefer 30m over 15m' is still supported, on cost (0.16R vs 0.22R) and on the negative 15m results, but not by a demonstrated 30m exit gain.

strategy_note_problems: Coverage: 64 notes for 15m and 16 for 30m, none for 1h/4h, although the 10/7 update puts 1h AI entries in scope. Only 16 of the possible 30m cells have notes.
Grade 'H1 (v4 only)' (10 DeepSeek cells) reads 'exit rules gained in every run it has' from ONE run: no replication. It should not share the H1 label with cells that are consistent across runs.

DeepSeek duplicates are graded as independent cells with no duplicate flag: F5_BOX@15m and F5_BOX_HTF@15m have identical numbers (n 10, R +0.08). F11_RAID / F11_TSOUP / F13_RAID_PD@15m, listed as duplicates in CONTEXT, get three different grades (H1 v4-only, H1/hopeless, H2) with n 38/25/36, so the duplicate mapping or the notes need a check.
Per-cell rule gains (n 9-46 signals, 8-30 hour-clusters) are shown without CI or BH, e.g. 'CUT05 +0.10', and the note text reads them as gains. At this n they are noise-level.
The notes do not say that CUT05 is a resting 1m hard stop (a tighter code stop), not something an AI can do at bar closes. The bar-close version is about 0.

Spot check of 7 cells against my own replay: all reproduce to rounding (DOGE@15m n 9, R -0.46, v3b -1.16 / v4 -0.11; N09_ALLIG_AROON@15m n 21, -0.29, CUT05 +0.09 vs +0.10; F3_HHHL@15m n 46, +0.11; N24_DMI@30m n 34, +0.05 (+0.08/+0.04); N01_ST_EMA@30m n 23, -0.34, CUT05 +0.15 vs +0.16; N10_HA_PSAR@15m +0.06 (+0.05/+0.07); N20_EMA9_CHOP@30m +0.25 (+0.10/+0.28)).
verifier_missed: 1h AI entries (now in scope): the only state exit robust to its threshold is at 1h (exit at 4 bars when <= -0.5R: -0.29R hold-minus-exit, +0.021R per signal, 14 clusters). Late or near-signal entries at 1h are not worse (+0.04/+0.07R, CIs span 0). At 1h, 30x sizes only 79% of core signals and 40x about 2%, so '20-50x by confidence' is not available at 1h. Cost is about 0.11R per trade.

Skip/selection at 15m: signals that arrived while an account was in position were better run alone than the signals the accounts actually entered (core +0.15R, CI +0.00..+0.30; DeepSeek +0.29R, CI +0.09..+0.48; v4-driven, core v3b opposite). The one-position, first-come rule seems to take the worse 15m signals in v4. That bears on AI skip and priority logic and on the 'switching = bad replacement' story.

Cross-timeframe switching (the planned trader's real choice) was not tested. lens2_multi_tf found switch-only-to-higher-tf the best rule over 5 years. The AIH-7 ban on switching should be limited to same-tf switching.

AI-visible vs intrabar exits: every exit 'headroom' rule that helps (CUT05) is a resting 1m stop. The bar-close versions an AI could act on are about 0. The lens never separates 'code stop change' from 'AI discretion'.

PREREG.md was rewritten (addenda) after the main rules ran, so there is no tamper-evident record (hash or timestamp) of the original rule list. A future PREREG should be a separate, never-edited file.

Exit rules were tested only at each run's own leverage. Because the ladder locks a fixed ROE, rule effects at 20x vs 30-50x could differ. That interaction, relevant to 'leverage by AI confidence', was not checked.
All DeepSeek findings are single-run (v4): no out-of-sample check exists for any DeepSeek cell or rule.
Events: second-tier macro releases and crypto-specific events inside v3b/v4 were not listed or checked. The event file only covers NFP/CPI/FOMC/PCE.

findings.claim: The timeframe gradient of results (15m worst, 4h best) is a cost gradient that a coin flip shows equally; the strategies add nothing on top of it at any timeframe.
findings.evidence: Exhaustive coin flip (both sides at every bar close of every coin, repo engine on live_bars, v3b+v4, 9,128 replays, leverage-mixed, 4h-block cluster CI): 15m -0.188R [-0.273,-0.092] n4516, 30m -0.133 [-0.173,-0.082] n2219, 1h -0.081 [-0.137,-0.021] n1100, 4h +0.098 [-0.021,+0.224] n110. Mean cost_R 0.167/0.116/0.085/0.048, gross R -0.021/-0.017/+0.004/+0.146 (cf_exhaustive_summary.csv, coinflip.py). Strategy live trades all runs: -0.19 (630) / -0.15 (378) / -0.07 (212) / +0.14 (31) (summary.md). Timing-matched side flip v3b+v4: chosen -0.111/-0.156/-0.139/-0.006 vs coin flip at the same moments -0.151/-0.131/-0.137/+0.017 (cf_side_by_run.csv). Validation: exhaustive rows vs pipeline replay at the same moments corr 0.877, same exit 98%, mean -0.023R (check_exh.py).
findings.implication: Choose timeframes for cost, not for 'what worked'. A 15m/30m AI trader starts ~0.13-0.19R per trade behind; the AI must create that much edge before breaking even. Nothing in the live data says any strategy's signal beats the coin flip at its timeframe.

verification.recomputed: Own 1m-bar re-implementation of the house exit (2 ATR stop + ROE ladder, fees+slippage; validated vs 1,234 live v3b/v4 trades: same exit 99/98/97/80% at 15m/30m/1h/4h, corr 0.99-1.00, mean diff -0.006R; sim3.py, val3.csv). Exhaustive coin flip, every bar close x coin x side at 30x (20x fallback), v3b+v4: 15m -0.171R [-0.276,-0.034] n2250, 30m -0.119 [-0.175,-0.047] n1115, 1h -0.076 [-0.135,-0.015] n554, 4h +0.007 [-0.113,+0.145] n65 (70 of 148 4h moments not sizable even at 20x) (an3.py, cf3.csv). Full round-trip cost incl. slippage 0.234/0.162/0.118/0.065R; pre-cost gross +0.06/+0.04/+0.04/+0.07. Timing-matched side flip of every SUBMITTED core signal (30x): own vs flipped 15m -0.111/-0.154, 30m -0.154/-0.125, 1h -0.119/-0.107, 4h -0.018/-0.138; half-excess +0.021/-0.014/-0.006/+0.060, 4h-block sign-flip p 0.87/0.82/0.96/0.53. DeepSeek: +0.067 (p 0.20)/-0.032/+0.018/-0.033.
verification.note: Core conclusion reproduces (coin flip = minus cost, no timeframe shows strategy direction beating the flip). Two corrections: (1) their mean cost_R = (fees+funding)/risk only (coinflip.py line 43) and leaves out slippage (0.04 of the 0.14% round trip), so it understates the round trip by about 29%; the full cost is 0.23/0.16/0.12/0.065R, consistent with the established medians 0.22/0.16/0.11/0.07R, and their 'gross' still contains slippage. (2) The 4h coin flip +0.098 depends on the leverage group mix (their 40-50x group); at the executable 30/20x it is about 0, n65-110, CI spans 0. Comparing all-run live strategy R (v3a at old 50x) with the v3b+v4 flip mixes regimes; only the timing-matched comparison is clean, and it says the same thing.

findings.claim: The 15m coin flips' +0.10R (n 50) is luck (sample noise plus short trades in a falling v4), not exit mechanics; the 30m/1h/4h coin-flip accounts are equally noisy in the other direction.
findings.evidence: Coin-flip accounts 15m: +0.099R, 25 4h-clusters, CI [-0.213,+0.382]; per run v3a -0.160 (n23), v3b +0.230 (n10), v4 +0.372 (n17; v4 shorts +0.592 n10 vs longs +0.058 n7, market -2.6%); top-2 trades = 80% of the summed R (coinflip_accounts.csv). Expected 15m coin flip -0.188 (exhaustive); a block bootstrap of 50 trades from the exhaustive 15m distribution: mean -0.16, 95% band [-0.45,+0.17], P(>= +0.099) = 0.059 (cf_luck_band_15m.csv). Leverage group does not explain it: exhaustive 15m best(40-50x) vs normal(30x) v4 -0.217 vs -0.180, v3b -0.165 vs -0.193. Other flips: 30m -0.300 [-0.504,-0.086] n24 vs expected -0.133; 1h -0.170 n12; 4h -0.521 n5. The random accounts even 'passed' the side-flip direction-skill test at 15m (excess +0.273, cluster p 0.0145, n46; summary.md) though their side is random by construction.
findings.implication: Never use the 3 live coin-flip accounts per tf as the AI verdict baseline: their ordering (15m best, 4h worst) is the reverse of the cost-driven truth. Per-account p<0.05 against a coin flip happens to coins themselves.

verification.recomputed: Coin-flip accounts 15m from trades.csv: +0.099R n50, 4h-block CI [-0.21,+0.38] (24 blocks); per run v3a -0.160 n23, v3b +0.230 n10, v4 +0.372 n17; v4 shorts +0.592 n10 vs longs +0.058 n7; top-2 trades = 80% of summed R. 30m -0.300 n24, 1h -0.170 n12, 4h -0.521 n5. 50-trade block bootstrap from my exhaustive 15m flip: median -0.154, 95% band [-0.447,+0.204], P(>=+0.099)=0.073 (iid 0.060). Side-flip test on the 46 replayable 15m coin-flip signals: half-excess +0.27, two-sided 1h-cluster p 0.035 (live3.py, misc3.py, rnd3.py).
verification.note: Their p 0.0145 is one-sided; two-sided 0.035 still 'passes' at 5%, so the point stands: random sides pass the direction test in this sample.

findings.claim: Market direction is by far the largest force in this data: both later runs fell, and a random-time short beat a random-time long by 0.3-1.1R at every timeframe, 4-6x the round-trip cost.
findings.evidence: Equal-weight 6-coin return: v3a -0.12% (APPROX, 2.6 d), v3b -0.91% (0.7 d), v4 -2.59% (1.5 d; all six coins down, DOGE -4.07, LTC -3.63, ETH -3.21) (market_backdrop.csv). Exhaustive coin flip by side (plain mean): v4 short/long 15m +0.199/-0.593, 30m +0.223/-0.475, 1h +0.305/-0.443, 4h +0.619/-0.469; v3b 15m -0.033/-0.328, 30m +0.035/-0.351, 1h +0.089/-0.315; per coin v4 15m long-minus-short -0.30 (SOL) to -1.25 (ETH) (backdrop_R.csv, luck.py).
findings.implication: A 30-day AI verdict will be dominated by whether the trader leaned with that month's trend. Long/short balance must be reported next to every result, and the verdict baseline must hold the trader's own side mix fixed.

verification.recomputed: Equal-weight 6-coin return: v3a -0.10% (signal_log ref prices, approx), v3b -0.91% (live_bars), v4 -2.59% (DOGE -4.07, LTC -3.63, ETH -3.21, BCH -2.18, BTC -1.51, SOL -0.92; all six down). Exhaustive flip short/long (30x): v4 15m +0.309/-0.631, 30m +0.279/-0.470, 1h +0.300/-0.424, 4h +0.461/-0.521 (n28/28); v3b 15m -0.031/-0.359, 30m +0.042/-0.386, 1h +0.076/-0.310, 4h +0.216/+0.269 (n6/3). v4 15m long-minus-short per coin -0.36 (SOL) to -1.84 (ETH) (misc3.py, an3.py).
verification.note: Direction dominance in v4 confirmed. Corrected: the short-long gap is 0.33-0.43R in v3b and 0.72-0.98R in v4, which is 1.4-2.7x the full round-trip cost in v3b and 4-15x in v4, not '4-6x at every timeframe'. In v3b 4h longs beat shorts (n 9, meaningless). The per-coin spread is wider than they report (-1.84 ETH vs their -1.25); the magnitude depends on leverage mix.

findings.claim: The best side-flip ('direction skill') results all come from one-sided strategies that were short in a falling market; against random-time entries on the same side they show zero timing edge.
findings.evidence: N20_EMA9_CHOP is short-only by construction (5y long share 0.00): 15m+30m side-flip excess +0.310 (n111, p 0.015) but vs same-side random-time coin flip -0.002 [-0.293,+0.365]; 1h excess +0.444 (p 0.005, lowest of all 1h/4h cells) vs timing -0.013; live R in flat v3a -0.78 (n17). N24_DMI (5y long share 0.15-0.21, live 0.09): excess +0.217 (p 0.048), timing -0.124. F14_SMT@1h (long 0.05): excess +0.364 (p 0.036), timing -0.136. Strategy v4 15m excess +0.089 splits into tilt +0.172 and drift-neutral -0.084 (long share 0.34) (grades_15m30m.csv, grades_1h4h.csv, excess_split_kind_run_tf.csv).
findings.implication: Do not staff N20, N24 or F14_SMT because of their side-flip rank: they are bets on a falling market. A short-only trader will look skilled in a down month and fail in an up month.

verification.recomputed: N20_EMA9_CHOP 15m+30m: n111 pairs, long share 0.00, half-excess +0.29 (two-sided 1h-cluster p 0.048), timing vs same-side (short) random-time flip of the same run/tf -0.10 (p 0.58). N20@1h half-excess +0.40 (p 0.025), timing -0.02. N24_DMI 15m+30m half-excess +0.22 (p 0.11), timing -0.15, long 0.09 (units3.py).
verification.note: Substance reproduces: N20/N24 side-flip 'skill' is the short tilt in a falling market, with no timing edge. My cluster p-values are weaker (0.048 vs 0.015, 0.11 vs 0.048). F14_SMT@1h not separately rechecked.

findings.claim: Which coin-flip baseline the AI verdict should use: the paired side flip on the trader's own entries plus a same-side random-time coin flip, both enumerated in full on the same days with the same exits, leverage and costs. The unconditional coin flip is only the cost floor; the live coin-flip accounts should not be used.
findings.evidence: Side flip removes market path, timing, coin and cost (paired, sd of the half-difference 1.14R at 15m vs 1.36R for raw R; mde.py). The same-side random-time baseline removes direction exposure (LF4). An exhaustive enumeration of every bar x coin x side x leverage group took 8 s on 4 processes for 9,128 replays (cf_replay.py), so sampling 10,000 flips is unnecessary. The exhaustive flip uses the 1m open as reference price: about 0.02R more pessimistic than live fills (check_exh.py).
findings.implication: Write both baselines into the verdict code before 10/17: report the excess over each, a day-block sign-flip p, and the long share. Count a trader only if it beats BOTH. The owners' MY_REVIEW item 3 (same-direction, random-time coin) is supported by the data.

verification.recomputed: Paired half-difference sd 1.14R (15m) / 0.86R (30m) vs own-R sd 1.38 / 0.94 on the every-signal replay (pairs3.csv). Exhaustive enumeration ran in seconds with my own code (sim3.py total 4.6 s), so sampling is indeed unnecessary.
verification.note: Methodological recommendation; supported. Caveat they did not state: the same-side random-time baseline is sensitive to the pool chosen (same run+tf vs same coin; with leverage mix): N17's timing is +0.39 in theirs and +0.52 in mine. Fix the pool definition in the verdict code before 10/17.

findings.claim: No strategy x 15m+30m unit beats the coin flip after multiple-testing correction. By this lens 8 units are 'watch' (B), and only one of them, N13_3OUTSIDE, held up in two runs.
findings.evidence: 80 AI units (36 core + 44 DeepSeek): min side-flip p 0.005 (F16_FIB500, BH q 0.32); 1h/4h cells min p 0.005 (N20@1h, q 0.20). Grades: B 8 = N13_3OUTSIDE + F12_MSS, F12_MSS_DISP, F16_FIB500, F1_MOM_DIV, F1_RSI_DIV, F7_RF_TRIPLE, F9_IFVG (all DeepSeek = v4 only, 1.5 days); C 40; D 4 = N12_ICHI_AO, N18_VWMA_MACD, OBV_S, F4_PULL; ? 21; X 7. N13: excess +0.334 (n15 pairs, 14 1h-clusters), v3b +0.42 / v4 +0.21, timing vs same-side +0.381 [-0.035,+0.800], live v3a +0.22 (n14) (grades_15m30m.csv, grade.py). N17_KC_RSI: side-flip excess +0.02, but vs random-time longs +0.386 [0.048,0.852], v3b +0.69 / v4 +0.33, 30m -0.17. This is the only unit whose timing CI excludes 0, unadjusted for 80 tests.
findings.implication: Any pick of AI strategies from this data is an in-sample pick. Treat the B list as 'watch' candidates. Fill the remaining seats with strategies that have frequency and five-year evidence. Do not take seats from rule accounts on the strength of these 4.8 days.

verification.recomputed: 76 units with pairs, 56 testable (>=10 1h clusters). Two-sided 1h-cluster sign-flip p on half-excess: smallest F4_PULL p 0.001 (NEGATIVE, half-excess -0.46, BH q 0.056), F16_FIB500 p 0.010 (+0.47, q 0.27), N20 0.048, N12_ICHI_AO 0.057 (negative). Timing test: N17_KC_RSI +0.52 p 0.001 q 0.07, F4_PULL -0.43 p 0.003 q 0.08. N13_3OUTSIDE n17 pairs, half-excess +0.31 (p 0.20), v3b +0.40 / v4 +0.18, timing +0.35 (p 0.10) (units3.py, units3.csv).
verification.note: No unit beats the coin flip after BH: confirmed. They missed that the strongest result of the whole scan is negative (F4_PULL worse than the flip, two-sided q 0.056), hidden because their p-values are one-sided (F4_PULL shown as p 1.00). N13 support is thinner than stated (n15-17, p 0.13-0.20).

findings.claim: Accounts enter in clusters: thousands of signals equal only about 100 independent observations per timeframe, because the whole replay covers 15 four-hour blocks.
findings.evidence: v4: 85% of DeepSeek trades and 78% of strategy trades share the coin and minute with another account; 36% / 30% share it with >= 5 others; largest cluster 17 accounts on BTC in one minute (cluster_entries.csv). Design effect of pooled trade R: strategy 15m n630 deff 1.25 (coin-minute) / 1.84 (minute) / 2.61 (4h block); DeepSeek 15m 1.61/1.86/2.66 (neff_kind_tf.csv). Every-signal replay: strategy 15m 1,087 signals -> n_eff 94 (15 blocks); DeepSeek 15m 1,107 -> 128; strategy 30m 536 -> 148 (neff_replay_kind_tf.csv). A naive iid one-sided 5% test has a false-pass rate of 12% at deff 2.0, 16% at 2.7 and 30% at 10 (mde.py).
findings.implication: All per-trade t-values in the variant and leaderboard tables overstate the evidence by about 1.3-3x in variance. Cross-trader tests in November will pass together in a trending month (correlated luck). Use day-block resampling and count independent days, not trades.

verification.recomputed: v4: 85.1% of DeepSeek and 78.3% of core trades share coin+minute with another account; 36.4% / 29.8% are in clusters of >=5 accounts (>=4 others; 26.6%/20.7% with >=5 others); largest cluster 17. Deff of pooled live R, core 15m n630: coin-minute 1.32, minute 1.82, 4h block 2.37; DeepSeek 15m n259 1.64/1.78/2.53. Every-signal replay (traded, 30x), 4h-block deff: core 15m n1130 -> n_eff 81, 30m 563 -> 141; DeepSeek 15m 1120 -> 146; 14 blocks for v3b+v4 (live3.py, an3.py). Naive-test false-pass 12/16/30% at deff 2/2.7/10 checks out analytically.
verification.note: Wording fix: '>= 5 others' should read '>= 5 accounts'. Otherwise reproduces.

findings.claim: A one-month verdict on one AI trader can only detect very large edges (about 0.3R per trade or more), while plausible edges are 0.1R or less.
findings.evidence: Per-trade sd: 15m 1.36R, 30m 0.95R; paired side-flip sd 1.14 / 0.87; within-account day clustering rho 0.142 (deff 1.57 at 5 trades/day). MDE (80% power, one-sided 5%): 15m n150 -> 0.35R vs zero, 0.29R vs side flip; n30 -> 0.78R / 0.65R; 30m n150 -> 0.24R / 0.22R; n300 -> 0.17R / 0.16R (mde_verdict.csv).
findings.implication: Most traders that pass the 30-day verdict will have passed by luck unless their edge is huge. Plan for accumulating evidence past 11/16 (rule accounts at cost 0) and for small real money, sized to that uncertainty.

verification.recomputed: Replay sd 15m 1.38R, 30m 0.94R; paired half-difference sd 1.14 / 0.86. Within account-day ICC by a pairwise estimator 0.059 (theirs 0.142 by ANOVA) -> deff at 5/day 1.24-1.57. MDE 15m n150 = 0.31-0.35R vs zero, 0.26-0.29R vs side flip.
verification.note: Arithmetic and inputs reproduce; the within-day rho is estimator-sensitive (0.06-0.14), which moves MDE by about 10%. The conclusion (only edges of about 0.3R or more are detectable in one month) holds. It ignores market-wide clustering across traders, which makes multi-trader passes correlated (LF7).

findings.claim: Profit in profitable accounts is as concentrated as in profitable coin-flip accounts: the account leaderboard carries no skill information.
findings.evidence: 90 of 167 profitable non-random account-runs (54%) turn negative without their best trade. Accounts with 5-9 trades: core 34% (29 accounts, median best-trade share 0.87, best-day share 1.12); DeepSeek 50% (14, 1.01, 1.61). Profitable coin-flip account-runs: 10 of 15 (67%) gone without the best trade, median best-trade share 1.0 (luck_conc_summary.csv, luck.py). Eight accounts carry the pipeline's direction-luck flag (direction_luck.csv), e.g. N22_VORTEX_PSAR@15m v3b (6 of 6 trades short), N24_DMI@15m and @30m v3b, N20_EMA9_CHOP@15m v3b.
findings.implication: Rank AI candidates on every-signal replay R and the two coin-flip excesses, never on account P&L or 'best account' lists.

verification.recomputed: Profitable non-random account-runs 167, 90 turn negative without their best trade; profitable coin-flip account-runs 15, 10 gone without best trade, median best-trade share 1.00 (live3.py).
verification.note: The 5-9-trade subgroup numbers and the direction_luck flags were not rechecked.

findings.claim: Signal flow: about 16 SUBMITTED signals per account-day at 15m and 8 at 30m. Most go unused because the account is already in a position. Sizing rejections occur only at 4h.
findings.evidence: SUBMITTED per account-day (v3a / v3b / v4): strategy 15m 16.7/15.5/15.9, 30m 7.8/8.0/8.1, 1h 3.4/4.7/5.3, 4h 1.06/0.68/1.18; DeepSeek v4 17.7 / 9.4 / 5.6 / 2.1. Shares at 15m: entered 22% / 33% / 22% (DeepSeek 24%); skipped in position 71% / 55% / 70% (65%); lower score 7-12%. Rejected for sizing (stop too close to liquidation) at 4h: 35% v3a (old 50x tier walk), 47% v3b, 19% v4 core, 17.5% DeepSeek; 2.5% at 1h in v3a; zero at 15m/30m (flow_kind_tf.csv). Live rates match the five-year rates: 124 cells, median live/5y 1.10 (IQR 0.90-1.35), log-rate correlation 0.89; core medians 0.94/0.95/0.99 at 15m/30m/1h, 0.71 at 4h. DeepSeek 1.4-2.8x because its five-year counts are trades at one position per coin (PREREG_DEEPSEEK200.md line 29), not raw signals (rate_vs_5y.csv).
findings.implication: Entry frequency is not a constraint at 15m/30m for most strategies. Use the five-year rates for staffing: the live rates confirm they hold.

verification.recomputed: Run spans: v3a 2.608 d (7 restarts in runs.csv but 249 of 250 15m bar closes carry signals, max gap 30 min), v3b 0.697 d, v4 1.500 d (4 restarts, no gap); timestamps UTC ms, per-day rates are timezone-free. RECORD rows (XRPUSDT record-only + 1d) and 19 LATE 5m rows excluded; no duplicate (bar, tf, strategy, coin) rows. SUBMITTED per account-day (mean): core 15m 16.75/15.58/15.94, 30m 7.78/8.01/8.11, 1h 3.41/4.66/5.35, 4h 1.05/0.68/1.19; DeepSeek 17.76/9.39/5.58/2.15. MEDIAN account: core 15m 7.9/6.5/7.7, 30m 3.8/4.3/4.0, 1h 2.3/2.9/3.3, 4h 0.77/0/0.33; DeepSeek 14.7/6.7/4.0/1.3. Shares (entered / in position / lower score / sizing) reproduce exactly; sizing rejections: v3a 1h 8 (2.5%), 4h 35%/47%/19%/DS 17.5%, 0 at 15m/30m. Live vs 5-year signal rate (core, profiles.json signals_per_day): median ratio 0.95/0.99/0.98/0.77 at 15m/30m/1h/4h, 121 cells median 1.00, IQR 0.84-1.20, log corr 0.95 (flow3.py, rate3.py).
verification.note: Numbers reproduce. Corrections: the '16 per account-day' is a mean pulled up by a few very frequent strategies (N17 106/day, S2 75, N04 74 at 15m+30m); the median core account sees about 8 at 15m and 4 at 30m. The claim 'sizing rejections only at 4h' contradicts its own evidence (v3a 1h 2.5%). The DeepSeek 1.4-2.8x ratio explanation fits PREREG (one position per setting x coin, simultaneous long/short dropped) but was not recomputed.

findings.claim: Persistent no-trade strategies are near-silent by design (five-year rates), not live bugs. Seven units cannot support an AI trader and five more cannot reach 30 trades a month.
findings.evidence: N21_ST_RSI_ADX: 0 signals in 5 years at any tf. N14_ICHI_RSI: 2-4 signals in 5 years per tf. N15_KC_AO 0.049/day at 15m. S1_EMA_RSI_CHOP 0.095/day at 15m. N11_BREAKAWAY 0.35/day at 15m. Poisson P(0 live signals given the 5y rate) 0.56-0.99 (flow.csv). Zero-trade accounts: v3a 48 (35 no signal, 8 all rejected by sizing, all at 4h; 5 open at end), v3b 64 (55/4/4 + 1 record-only), v4 core 43 (35/3/4/1), v4 DeepSeek 30 (20/3/7); 4h accounts are 25/48, 35/64, 23/43 and 22/30 of them (zero_trade_accounts.csv). X (< 1 AI trade/day both live and at the five-year rate): N11, N14, N15, N21, S1, F15_OPEN0930, F5_BOX_RSI. Below 1/day live: N08_ICHI_WR 0.9, S5_DONCHIAN_MFI 0.45, F4_PULL_RSI 0.67 (ai_trader_15m30m.csv).
findings.implication: Give no AI seat to the X list. Keep them, if at all, as cost-free rule accounts. The 4h zero-trade problem is mostly sizing and leverage, not signals.

verification.recomputed: Zero-trade accounts (my own classification): v3a core 48 = 35 no signal + 8 all sizing-rejected (all 4h) + 5 entered but open at end; v3b core 64 = 55 + 1 record-only (OBV_S@1h, XRP rows only) + 4 + 4; v4 core 43 = 35 + 1 record-only (N18_VWMA_MACD@4h) + 3 + 4; v4 DeepSeek 30 = 20 + 3 + 7; 4h share 25/48, 35/64, 23/43, 22/30. Coin-flip accounts also had zero trades (v3b 6: 2 RANDOM@4h sizing-rejected, 4 no signal; v4 1 no signal). Five-year rates: N21 0 signals at every tf; N14 2/2/4/3 signals at 15m/30m/1h/4h; N15 0.049/day, S1 0.095/day, N11 0.345/day at 15m. AI trades/day (15m+30m sim): F15_OPEN0930 0.66, F5_BOX_RSI 0.66, F4_PULL_RSI 0.66, N08 0.91, N11 0.45, S5 0.45 (flow3.py, zero3.csv, ai3.py).
verification.note: Counts reproduce exactly. Corrections: the claim says 'five more cannot reach 30 trades a month' but lists three (N08, S5, F4_PULL_RSI), and those rates rest on 1-2 simulated trades. 'Open at end' zero-trade accounts are not all 4h: S3_CMO_SANDWICH@1h and N20@1h (v3b), N03_ADX_GC@1h and N11_BREAKAWAY@1h (v4).

findings.claim: An AI trader that owns one strategy at 15m+30m with one position at a time would take about 4-5 trades a day and be in a position about half the time. The event-driven wake design costs about $200-450 a month for 30 traders; a check at every 15m close while holding would cost $1,000-1,900.
findings.evidence: Rule-following simulation on the replay (every signal's own exit, v3b+v4): median 5.0 trades/day for the 32 active core strategies (10-90%: 1.9-8.6), 4.7 for DeepSeek (1.3-6.7). The five-year-rate analytic agrees (e.g. N04 9.5 vs 9.7). 29/36 core and 41/44 DeepSeek reach >= 1/day. Busy share median about 0.5; >= 0.78 for N23, S2, OBV_B, N25, N04, N22, N10 and F16_FIB618. Calls per trader per month (median core / DeepSeek): event-driven 443 / 399, plus 4h scans 534 / 471, plus 15m holding checks 2,024 / 2,233. At Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10 per MTok (10k in + 1k out = $0.030, or $0.016 with 8k cached), 30 traders cost about $202-378, $240-450 and $1,008-1,890 a month for the three designs (ai_trader_15m30m.csv, ai_trader.py; prices from the claude-api skill table dated 2026-09-25).
findings.implication: Only the event-driven design fits $500, and only if output plus thinking stays near 1k tokens; Opus seats cost 2x. High-frequency strategies keep the trader almost always in a position, so the AI's choice reduces to taking whichever signal comes first. Prefer mid-frequency strategies (3-6 trades/day) for AI seats.

verification.recomputed: Own one-position simulation (every SUBMITTED signal's own exit at 30x, first signal of a bar when flat; v3b+v4 for core, v4 only for DeepSeek). 15m+30m: core median 4.3 trades/day [10-90%: 1.9-8.6], 29/32 >=1/day, busy 0.54; DeepSeek 4.7 [1.3-6.4], 41/44, busy 0.63. Calls per trader per month: event-driven 414 (core) / 414 (DS); every new signal while holding also consulted 614 / 758; plus 4h scans 476 / 467; plus 15m holding checks 2,151 / 2,335. 30 traders at $0.016-0.030 per call: $199-373, $295-682, $224-428, $1,032-2,102 per month. Prices check against the claude-api skill (Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10 per MTok, cache read $0.20; Opus 5.5 $4/$20). OWNERS' NEW PLAN (15m/30m/1h, plus 4h only where 20x sizes): my 20x sizability rule (2 ATR stop + max(1 ATR, 0.2%) buffer inside a 20x liquidation, maintenance 0.5%) matches live 4h sizing on 96 of 99 signals; 54% of core and 60% of DeepSeek 4h signals pass. Core median 5.0 trades/day [1.9-7.3], busy 0.65; DeepSeek 4.3 [1.3-7.3], busy 0.69; 15m+30m+1h without 4h: 4.8 / 4.3. Calls/day per trader: event-driven 13.6 core / 13.0 DS (about 414 / 394 a month); with every new signal while holding 22.0 / 26.6 (669 / 808); plus 4h scans 16.2 / 15.0; plus 15m holding checks 80 / 84. 30 traders: event-driven $189-373, with signal consults while holding $321-728, with scans $219-444, with 15m checks $1,172-2,285 a month (ai3.py, ai_trader3.csv).
verification.note: Reproduces (core 4.3 vs their 5.0, calls 414 vs 443; DeepSeek 4.7 = theirs). Missed: (1) the owners' plan has the AI switch timeframes and signals while holding, so each new signal while holding is a call; that design costs $295-728 for 30 traders, at or over the $500 budget. (2) Sonnet 5.5 has adaptive thinking on by default (effort high), billed as output at $10/MTok. At 3k output tokens per call the event-driven design alone costs about $440-620 for 30 traders. (3) Adding 1h and 20x-sizable 4h hardly adds trades (4.3->5.0 core), because the trader is already busy; it mostly raises the busy share from 0.54 to 0.65.

findings.claim: The positive 4h numbers come from trades still open at the end of the run and from a short tilt in a falling market.
findings.evidence: Strategy 4h replay: +0.206R on 28 traded signals, +0.068 when the 14 unresolved are included at mark; 39 of 81 4h signals rejected by sizing. Exhaustive coin flip 4h: +0.098 traded vs +0.034 with marks; 30 of 140 unresolved. v4 strategy 4h signals 30% long (tilt +0.218, drift-neutral -0.086). DeepSeek 4h: replay -0.122, 59 of 126 rejected (grade.py stdout, cf_exhaustive_summary.csv, excess_split_kind_run_tf.csv).
findings.implication: Do not promote 4h on the live +0.14R. 4h is the cheapest timeframe by cost (0.05R), but these runs are too short and too one-directional to show anything about it.

verification.recomputed: Core 4h signals v3b+v4: 81; 37 not sizable at 20x (live rejected 39). Replay of the 44 sizable ones at 30x/20x: traded +0.051R n31, unresolved at mark -0.179 n13, all about -0.02; v4 shorts +0.558 n18 vs longs -0.927 n10. At 30x for all: traded -0.014 n31, with marks -0.063. Exhaustive 4h flip +0.007 traded, -0.020 with marks. DeepSeek 4h: 126 signals, 50 not sizable, sizable ones with marks -0.146. Live core 4h trades +0.144 n31 (h4.py, units3.py, live3.py).
verification.note: Their replay +0.206 (n28) and +0.068 with marks do not reproduce: my replay gives about +0.05 traded and -0.02 with marks. The direction of the claim holds and is stronger: the 4h replay is not positive, and what positive there is comes from v4 shorts. The implication ('do not promote 4h on +0.14R') stands.

findings.claim: Live signal-to-signal correlation means DeepSeek duplicates and near-duplicates inflate the apparent number of independent candidates.
findings.evidence: F11_RAID = F11_TSOUP = F13_RAID_PD at 15m; F17_Z / F17_Z_HL share >= 90% of signals; F5_BOX = F5_BOX_HTF at 15m/30m; F15_OPEN0000 is one stream across tfs (dup_groups.csv). Their grades move together: F11_RAID / F11_TSOUP / F13_RAID_PD are all C with side-flip excess -0.07 / -0.28 / -0.01; F17_Z / F17_Z_HL are both C with timing +0.18 / +0.23 (grades_15m30m.csv).
findings.implication: Count each duplicate group as one candidate for seats and for BH families; never staff two members of the same group.

verification.recomputed: v4 SUBMITTED signal streams (bar, coin, side): F11_RAID 38 vs F11_TSOUP 25, 22 shared (Jaccard 0.54); F11_RAID vs F13_RAID_PD 36/38 shared (0.95) at 15m, identical at 1h and 4h; F17_Z vs F17_Z_HL identical at 1h and 4h, 0.94 at 15m; F5_BOX = F5_BOX_HTF at 15m and 30m; F10_OTE@4h = F16_FIB618@4h (5 signals); F15_OPEN0000 is the same 12 signals at 15m/30m/1h; F15_OPEN0930 15m = 30m (misc3.py; pipeline dup_groups.csv).
verification.note: 'F11_RAID = F11_TSOUP = F13_RAID_PD at 15m' is true only at the trade level: the three accounts made the same 8 trades with the same P&L. F11_TSOUP's signal stream is different (25 signals, 3 not in F11_RAID). That matters for an AI trader, which sees every signal; it also explains their different side-flip excess (-0.28 vs -0.07). They also left out the F17 and F11/F13 pairs at 30m/4h and F15_OPEN0930 15m=30m.

strategy_note_problems: p-values in the notes are one-sided, so units that lose significantly to the coin flip show p 0.98-1.00. F4_PULL (two-sided p 0.001, BH q 0.056) and N12_ICHI_AO (p 0.057) are the most significant results of the scan, and both are negative.
F11_TSOUP note: 'Duplicate group F11_RAID / F13_RAID_PD' holds for trades only. Its signal stream differs (25 vs 38 signals, 22 shared), and its replay excess -0.28 differs from F11_RAID's -0.07.
N17_KC_RSI: pairs n 103 in the note, 133 in my replay; timing +0.39 [0.05,0.85] in the note, +0.52 (two-sided p 0.001, BH q 0.07) in mine. Same sign, but the number depends on the random-time pool.
N13_3OUTSIDE: a 'B / watch' grade on 15-17 pairs, p 0.13 (mine 0.20); live n 24. Its 'held up in two runs' rests on 2 runs of 0.7 and 1.5 days.
Sampled numbers that reproduce: sig/day for N04, N08, N12, N13, N17, N20, S2, S5, F4_PULL, F11_TSOUP, F12_MSS, F16_FIB500 (to 0.1/day); live n and R (exact); AI trades/day within about 15%.
Notes give the mean signal rate only. For staffing, the burst structure matters, e.g. N17's 106 signals a day are 84% long and clustered.
verifier_missed: Mean signals per account-day hide the skew: the median core account sees about 8 signals a day at 15m and 4 at 30m (half the quoted 16 and 8).
The coin flip's cost_R left out slippage. The full round trip is 0.23/0.16/0.12/0.065R at 15m/30m/1h/4h, so an AI trader starts that far behind, not 0.17/0.12/0.09/0.05.
Strongest scan result is negative: F4_PULL is worse than the coin flip (two-sided q 0.056), also at 1h (p 0.003). Do not staff it, and do not 'reverse' it on 1.5 days of in-sample data.

For the new plan (entries on 15m/30m/1h, 4h only where 20x sizes): about 54% of core and 60% of DeepSeek 4h signals size at 20x. Trades/day barely rise (core 4.3->5.0), while the busy share rises to 0.65-0.69, so most extra-timeframe signals arrive while the trader is already in a position.

AI cost: Sonnet 5.5 adaptive thinking is on by default and billed as output. The '1k output tokens per call' assumption is optimistic, and consulting the AI on new signals while holding (needed for switching) pushes 30 traders to $320-730 a month.
Zero-trade accounts also include coin-flip accounts (v3b 6, v4 1), and 'open at end' cases at 1h, not only 4h.
Restarts (v3a 7 starts, v4 4) caused no gaps in signal flow: 249 of 250 15m bar closes carry signals and the max gap is 30 min, so wall-clock day denominators are valid. They did not state this.

Every-signal replay design effects at the 4h-block level are much larger than for live trades (core 15m deff about 14 -> n_eff 81, 1h about 7); signals of one tf are far less independent than the live-trade deffs suggest.
The in-sample warning should cover the timing baseline too: same-side random-time results (N17 +0.39 vs +0.52) depend on the pool definition, which needs to be fixed in advance.

findings.claim: Over 5 years, the 36 core strategies and the 44 DeepSeek definitions have about zero gross edge on every timeframe when run through the live house exit at paper-v4 leverage. The net result is simply minus the trading cost, which is what a coin flip at the same moments would earn.
findings.evidence: 8.1M 5-year signals (2021-08-01..2026-09-30, 6 coins), next-bar entry, 2 ATR stop, v3 ladder, 30x/20x 'normal' sizing. Core net R per trade (week-clustered t): 5m -0.307 (-40), 15m -0.172 (-32), 30m -0.125 (-27), 1h -0.094 (-19), 4h -0.051 (-3.9). Core gross R: +0.005, +0.001, -0.001, 0.000, +0.022. DS net R: 15m -0.177, 30m -0.128, 1h -0.099, 4h -0.066; DS gross -0.004/-0.004/-0.006/+0.006. Both 5-year halves (IS 2021-24, CF 2024-26) agree to within 0.01R. Parity: the tier-walk mode reproduces profiles.json mean ROE in all 175 cells (max diff 1e-8). Files: lens/fiveyear/out/fy_tf_summary.csv and fy36_parity.csv; scripts fy36_rerun.py, fyds_rerun.py, fy_compare.py.
findings.implication: The rule signal tells the AI when to look at the chart, not which way to trade. An AI trader has to supply the whole edge itself. Choosing 'the best strategy' only chooses which timing an edge-free signal uses. Any AI trader must be judged against its own strategy's every-signal result at the same moments, not against zero.

verification.recomputed: I wrote my own house-exit simulator (v3sim.py, from the ladder.py rules, repo sizing for 30x/20x 'normal', $5,000) and ran it on random samples of 1,500 rows per timeframe (core 15m/1h/4h) and 1,000 rows (DS 15m/4h, with my own Wilder ATR14). Every sampled row matched the lens pickles (leverage 100%, |dR|>1e-3 in 0 rows). My aggregation of the pickles (v3agg.py, week-clustered t) gives core net R 5m -0.307 (t -40.0), 15m -0.172 (-33.4), 30m -0.125 (-28.6), 1h -0.094 (-19.6), 4h -0.051 (-3.8); core gross R +0.0045/+0.0013/-0.0013/+0.0000/+0.0216; DS net -0.177/-0.128/-0.099/-0.066 and gross -0.0036/-0.0041/-0.0057/+0.0062. The tier-walk mean ROE matches out_binance/profiles.json in 175/175 cells (max diff 9.9e-9). Tier-walk R at 15m is -0.1723 and v4n is -0.1717. Total 8.12M signals.
verification.note: Reproduces exactly. Small corrections: (a) 'both halves agree to within 0.01R' fails at core 4h (net IS -0.042 vs CF -0.060; gross +0.032 vs +0.011) and only just holds at 30m (0.011). (b) The DS pooled gross is slightly negative, not zero: week-clustered t is -1.8, -1.9 and -2.1 at 15m, 30m and 1h. (c) The pooled 'gross about 0' hides real differences between cells: 18 cells have BH-significant NEGATIVE gross and 4 have positive gross (see F4). The core 4h gross of +0.022 applies only to the 19.7% of signals that pass sizing. verify_costs C2 (all signals at fixed 30x) gives -0.001R at 4h, so it is not robust. Note also that the lens used the Binance signal cache (scratchpad/binance/signals with out_binance profiles). The research/paper_rules signals give different rows.

findings.claim: Cost in R depends on the stop size (timeframe x current volatility), and the market right now is unusually quiet. At today's stop sizes the 5-year expectation is worse than the 5-year average, so the break-even edge an AI must add is about +0.22R per trade at 15m, +0.16R at 30m, +0.11R at 1h and +0.04R at 4h.
findings.evidence: Live stop sizes (v3b+v4 replay) sit at the 2nd-4th percentile of 5-year windows for 15m/30m/1h (core 0.037/0.035/0.027; DS 0.019/0.019/0.023). The 5-year net R for signals within the live stop-size range (p10..p90): core 15m -0.223, 30m -0.160, 1h -0.109, 4h -0.040; DS -0.236/-0.169/-0.120/-0.078. Core 15m by stop-size quintile: cost R 0.335 / 0.194 / 0.147 / 0.113 / 0.077, gross R +0.004/+0.008/-0.004/+0.001/-0.002, net -0.331 at stops of 0.63% or less. Live 15m median stop is 0.63%. Files: fy_volbucket.csv, fy_tf_windows.csv, fy_tf_summary.csv (fy_nowvol_*).
findings.implication: 15m/30m-only AI entries face the largest cost hurdle, and the hurdle grows in quiet markets. Limit (maker) entries, fewer trades, or trading only when stops are wide attack the real problem. Indicator-style 'custom values' do not. Report every AI result next to the cost R of its own trades.

verification.recomputed: Live TRADED replay (v3b+v4) median stop: core 15m 0.63%, 30m 0.89%, 1h 1.23%, 4h 2.02%; DS 0.60/0.85/1.23/1.96%. 5-year net R inside the live p10..p90 stop range: core -0.218/-0.155/-0.107/-0.037; DS -0.244/-0.173/-0.120/-0.079. Core 15m stop quintiles: cost R 0.335/0.194/0.147/0.113/0.077, gross +0.004/+0.008/-0.004/+0.001/-0.002, net -0.331 at stops of 0.63% or less (exact match). Position of the live stop size: per signal, 15m 19.9th, 30m 18.5th, 1h 17.8th, 4h 20.9th percentile (core). In contiguous 5-year windows of the live length (2.2 d core, 1.5 d DS), the live MEAN stop is at the 8.6/7.9/5.0th percentile (core 15m/30m/1h) and 6.4/6.5/5.8th (DS). With window medians: 12.9/8.4/6.8th.
verification.note: The hurdle numbers (+0.22/+0.16/+0.11/+0.04R) and the stop-size quintiles reproduce within 0.008R. The claim 'live stop sizes at the 2nd-4th percentile of 5-year windows' does not reproduce. It comes from drawing two independent random windows (0.70 d and 1.50 d), which is too narrow a distribution, and from using 2.2-day windows for DS, which ran only 1.5 days. The correct figure is about the 5th-9th percentile of windows, or the 18th-21st percentile of single signals (consistent with verify_costs C4). The market is quiet, but less extreme than claimed.

findings.claim: The live results sit inside the 5-year distribution of windows the same length as the live runs. Live shows neither a hidden edge nor broken execution. The only exceptions have explanations: 5m in v3a was worse (explained by the quiet regime), and DeepSeek 15m in v4 was better than the quiet-regime expectation (not significant after correction).
findings.evidence: 4,000 random contiguous 5-year windows of 0.70 d + 1.50 d (v3b+v4) or 2.61 d (v3a). Pooled per timeframe, the live replay mean R falls at these percentiles: core 15m 0.64, 30m 0.38, 1h 0.32, 4h 0.81; DS 15m 0.945, 30m 0.46, 1h 0.43, 4h 0.38. v3a: 15m 0.08, 30m 0.07, 1h 0.77, 4h 0.74, 5m 0.024 (p 0.049; 0.11 in stop-size-matched windows). In regime-matched windows, DS 15m live -0.065 against a matched median of -0.308 is at percentile 0.995 (p 0.009); BH over the 13 timeframe-level tests gives q of about 0.12. Per cell: 0 BH-significant outliers among 244 replay-tested and 164 v3a-tested cells; raw p<0.05 in 20/244 and 15/164. Files: fy_tf_windows.csv, fiveyear_vs_live.csv (win_* columns), fy_freq_tf.csv.
findings.implication: The 5-year results are a valid prior for the live accounts, and the paper bot behaves as the backtest predicts. There is no reason to think the live market is a special regime in which these rule signals work.

verification.recomputed: v3win.py: 4,000 contiguous windows per test. Core uses 2.202 d (v3b+v4 are back-to-back: 10/05 01:45Z to 10/07 06:40Z). DS uses 1.503 d (v4 only). Live = replay TRADED mean R. Percentiles: core 15m 0.61, 30m 0.37, 1h 0.33, 4h 0.83; DS 15m 0.90, 30m 0.45, 1h 0.43, 4h 0.39. Stop-matched windows (window mean stop within 15% of the live mean): DS 15m matched median -0.275 and live -0.065, percentile 0.979, two-sided p 0.041 (387 windows). BH across 13 tests gives q of about 0.5. v3a, recomputed with tier-walk R in 2.61-day windows (their live means taken as given): 5m 0.025 (p 0.05; stop-matched 0.11), 15m 0.079, 30m 0.078, 1h 0.76, 4h 0.73. Cell level: |z|>2 in 2/49 core and 2/68 DS cells (2h-cluster SE).

However, the tf-level DS test in fy_compare.py (line 344) used RP_LENS = 0.70 d + 1.50 d for DS as well, though DS ran only in v4. That makes the 5-year distribution too narrow and inflates the DS 15m result: the claimed 0.945 (matched 0.995, p 0.009, q 0.12) becomes 0.90 (matched 0.979, p 0.04, q about 0.5). Core used two independent windows rather than one contiguous 2.2-day window. The effect on the percentiles is small (within 0.03).

findings.claim: No strategy x timeframe cell has a dependable positive net 5-year result. Only 7 non-thin cells have mean R > 0 (all at 4h or very rare), and none has t > 1. The two cells with a significant positive gross edge are DS F16_FIB382@15m (6x smaller than its cost) and N23_HA_ST@4h.
findings.evidence: Net mean R > 0 with at least 30 sized signals: N23_HA_ST@4h +0.027 (t 0.98; IS +0.011, CF +0.042; 1,416 signals, 0.75 enterable/day); N02_ST_KST@4h +0.010; N09_ALLIG_AROON@4h +0.009; N15_KC_AO@30m +0.025 (n 59); S1_EMA_RSI_CHOP@1h +0.053 (n 43); DS F10_M2022@4h +0.085 (n 39); DS F13_FVG_PD@4h +0.013 (n 68, IS +0.20 / CF -0.13). Gross edge, BH over 307 cells with n>=200: F16_FIB382@15m gross +0.026R (t 4.0, q 0.009, IS +0.018 / CF +0.037) but net -0.142R; N23_HA_ST@4h gross +0.099R (t 3.7, q 0.017). Files: fy_gross_top.csv, fy_cells_is_cf.csv, fiveyear_vs_live.csv.
findings.implication: No candidate meets 'verified not to lose' on the 5-year evidence. The only cell that is non-negative in both halves with a significant gross edge is N23_HA_ST@4h, and it is a slow 4h cell (under 1 enterable signal/day; live v3b/v4 sizing rejected all 3 of its DOGE signals). It fits a cost-free rule account, not a 15m/30m AI trader.

The same 7 cells have n>=30 and net>0: N23_HA_ST@4h +0.027 (t 1.06, IS +0.011 / CF +0.042, n 1,416, 0.75/day), N02_ST_KST@4h +0.010, N09_ALLIG_AROON@4h +0.009, N15_KC_AO@30m +0.025 (n 59), S1_EMA_RSI_CHOP@1h +0.053 (n 43), DS F10_M2022@4h +0.085 (n 39), DS F13_FVG_PD@4h +0.013 (n 68).
