Gross test, BH over 307 cells with n>=200: q<0.05 in 4 POSITIVE cells, N23_HA_ST@4h +0.099 (t 3.95, q 0.006), F16_FIB382@15m +0.026 (t 3.89, q 0.006, net -0.142), F16_FIB500@15m +0.022 (t 3.31, q 0.020, IS +0.019 / CF +0.026) and N20_EMA9_CHOP@5m +0.029 (t 3.24, q 0.021, net -0.315); and in 18 NEGATIVE cells.

N23 has week-clustered t 1.06 (borderline on 'none has t>1'). The finding also leaves out that significant negative gross is 4.5 times as common as positive (18 vs 4). See 'missed'.

findings.claim: The best live cells are bad over 5 years, and they flip sign between live runs. Choosing AI strategies from live P&L would select noise.
findings.evidence: Live v3b+v4 every-signal R against v3a every-signal R and the 5-year result: S4_BB_BBP@15m +0.42 (n 39) vs v3a -0.25 (n 56), 5y -0.20 (gross -0.013). N17_KC_RSI@15m +0.11 (n 109) vs v3a -0.55 (n 161), 5y -0.16 with negative gross (t -3.4). N20_EMA9_CHOP@30m +0.26 (42) vs v3a -0.42 (14), 5y -0.15. N20_EMA9_CHOP@1h +0.29 +/-0.10 (17) vs v3a -0.82 (5), 5y -0.097. N01_ST_EMA@15m +0.16 (30) vs v3a -0.47 (42). DS F1_RSI_DIV@15m +0.45 (18) vs 5y -0.18. Rank agreement for cells with live n>=10: Spearman 5y vs live, core -0.10 (49 cells, permutation p 0.52), DS -0.11 (68, p 0.38); live v3a vs v3b+v4, -0.11 (41, p 0.48). Files: fy_top_lists.csv, fy_rank_agreement.csv, live_cells.csv.
findings.implication: Do not use live leaderboards (or the November 'promotion' if it is based on P&L) to choose AI traders or their custom values. Each live run disagrees with the next one.

verification.recomputed: v3cells.py, live = replay TRADED v3b+v4, 2h-cluster SE: S4_BB_BBP@15m +0.42 (n 39) vs 5y -0.202 (gross -0.013); N17_KC_RSI@15m +0.11 (n 109) vs -0.160 (gross t -3.35); N20_EMA9_CHOP@30m +0.26 (42) vs -0.150; N20_EMA9_CHOP@1h +0.29 +/-0.10 (17) vs -0.097; N01_ST_EMA@15m +0.16 (30) vs -0.173; DS F1_RSI_DIV@15m +0.45 (18) vs -0.183. A rank correlation near zero was therefore guaranteed whatever the truth, so this test only shows that live cannot rank cells. It says nothing about whether the 5-year ranks are real.

findings.claim: The number of live positive cells is about what noise around the 5-year expectation predicts, so the positive live cells are not evidence of skill.
findings.evidence: Cells with live n>=10 and a cluster SE. Core: 11 observed live-positive vs 10.4 expected if the true mean were the 5-year mean at today's stop size (12.5 if it were the 5-year average). DS: 26 observed vs 16.2 expected, an excess concentrated at 15m in a good 1.5-day stretch. z = (live - 5y)/live SE has sd 1.23 (core) and 1.29 (DS); |z|>2 in 3/49 and 4/68. Script: fy_compare.py and the check run inline on fiveyear_vs_live.csv.
findings.implication: With per-cell live n of 10-110 and an R sd of about 0.8-1.3, a cell needs about 100-280 independent signals before it can separate +0.2R from the 5-year expectation. Four days of paper trading cannot rank strategies.

verification.recomputed: Cells with live n>=10: core 11 positive observed vs 12.9 expected at the 5-year average mean (theirs 12.5); DS 26 vs 19.9. z=(live-5y)/SE has sd 1.23 (core) and 1.29 (DS), an exact match. |z|>2 in 2/49 and 2/68 (theirs 3/49 and 4/68; the cluster definition differs).
verification.note: The expectation at today's stop size (10.4 / 16.2) was not recomputed. The cells share the same market moments, so the observed-vs-expected count has no simple binomial p-value. The DS excess fits the DS 15m stretch in F3.

findings.claim: Live signal frequency matches the 5-year definitions on every timeframe, so the live signal service reproduces the backtested strategies, including the DeepSeek port.
findings.evidence: Live/5y signals per day, summed per timeframe: core 5m 1.04, 15m 0.97, 30m 0.94, 1h 0.99, 4h 1.01; DS 15m 1.08, 30m 1.03, 1h 1.05, 4h 1.29. Across 274 cells with >=1 5-year signal/day, the correlation of log frequency is 0.91 and 92% of cells are within 0.5-2x. No count mismatch survives BH (raw p<0.05 in 7 of 311 window-count tests). The largest gaps are small-count noise, e.g. N17_KC_RSI@4h with 4 live signals vs 5.75/day over 5y, inside the 5-year 2.2-day count range 0-39. Files: fy_freq_tf.csv, fiveyear_vs_live.csv (win_rp_cnt_*).
findings.implication: An AI trader per strategy gets the 5-year rate of chances. 15m/30m strategies give 5-60 signals/day over the 6 coins, so the AI's selectivity, not signal supply, sets how many trades it takes. 4h gives only about 0.2-1.3 enterable signals/day per strategy under v4 sizing.

verification.recomputed: Live submitted signals (replay, v3b+v4) per day vs the 5-year rate: core 15m 0.94, 30m 0.96, 1h 1.21, 4h 0.99; DS 15m 1.08, 30m 1.03, 1h 1.05, 4h 1.29. Core 1h has 406 live signals vs a median of 335 in 2.2-day windows (96th percentile). Cells with >=1 signal/day over 5y (235, v3b+v4 only): log-frequency correlation 0.89, 88% within 0.5-2x. N17_KC_RSI@4h: 5-year 2.2-day window count p5/p50/p95 is 0/7/46, and 28% of windows have <=1 signal, so the live gap is small-count noise.
verification.note: The DS ratios match exactly. Their core 'every timeframe ~1' pooled v3a in. In v3b+v4 alone, core 1h runs 21% above the 5-year rate (the 96th percentile of windows, not significant after correction). The conclusion holds. Enterable 4h signals per strategy run up to 0.8/day (core) and 1.9/day (DS), not 1.3.

findings.claim: Leverage does not change the per-notional result but multiplies the loss to equity. 40-50x with 2 ATR stops adds liquidations, badly so at 1h/4h. With no proven edge, '20-50x by AI confidence' speeds up ruin.
findings.evidence: research/levstop (fixed leverage, 2 ATR, every 5-year signal) in out/fy_levstop_arms.csv. 15m return per notional at 10/20/30/40/50x: -0.141/-0.142/-0.142/-0.147/-0.159%; equity per trade -0.28/-0.57/-1.28/-2.36/-3.18%; liquidated share 0.004/0.08/0.48/1.8/4.8%; busted accounts 47/58/61/64/64 of 70. Liquidated share at 50x: 30m 11%, 1h 19%, 4h 34%. My rerun: tier walk (mostly 50x) R -0.1723 vs v4 normal 30x R -0.1717 at 15m. Zero-edge drain (fy_equity_drain.csv): at 15m, 30x/30% loses 1.28%/trade (equity halves in about 54 trades), 50x/50% loses 3.56%/trade (about 19 trades).
findings.implication: Cap AI traders at 20-30x and keep the existing sizing checks (15% loss cap, liquidation buffer) until an AI shows a positive paired edge. Allow 40-50x only after its confidence score is shown to be calibrated over at least 100 resolved shadow trades. Never use 50x with 2 ATR stops on 1h/4h.

verification.recomputed: research/levstop/out/levstop.json, arm k=2.0, pooled over cells by trades. 15m per notional at 10/20/30/40/50x: -0.141/-0.142/-0.142/-0.147/-0.159%; equity per trade -0.28/-0.57/-1.28/-2.36/-3.17%; liquidated share 0.00/0.08/0.48/1.82/4.76%; busts 47/58/61/64/64 of 70. Liquidated share at 50x: 30m 10.97%, 1h 19.16%, 4h 33.89%. Per notional at 50x worsens to -0.224% (1h) and -0.288% (4h).
verification.note: Exact. One small understatement: fy_equity_drain.csv applies the 30x per-notional figure (-0.142%) at 50x/50%. At the real 50x per-notional figure (-0.159%, which includes liquidations) the drain is about 3.97%/trade, so equity halves in about 17 trades, not 19.

findings.claim: Exit tuning does not rescue these signals. The 5-year studies show exit styles reshape results by at most about 0.06% of equity per trade, and the live 'lev10 +0.26R / lock30 +0.14R' what-ifs are not supported by 5-year per-notional results at 15m.
findings.evidence: research/exitstyle (5 years, 1.89M trades): ladder -1.415% equity/trade; fixed TP 1R/1.5R/2R/3R -1.422/-1.418/-1.389/-1.378%; ladder+2R cap -1.403%. No pre-registered rule passes. 10x vs 30x at 15m: -0.141% vs -0.142% per notional (levstop). Exit choice also leaves gross R unchanged by construction: the gross R of about 0 comes from the entries.
findings.implication: Weekly shadow tuning of custom values will mostly fit noise. Expect gains of 0.0-0.05R, against the 0.16-0.22R needed at 15m/30m. Spend AI effort on entry selection and skipping, measured against same-moment rule outcomes, not on exit parameters.

verification.recomputed: research/exitstyle/out/exitstyle.json (1,890,071 trades, primary 15m-4h, 2 ATR, tier leverage): equity per trade, ladder -1.415%, tp1R -1.422, tp1.5R -1.418, tp2R -1.389, tp3R -1.378, ladder+2R -1.403. Decision: no arm passes, keep the ladder.
verification.note: Exact. The largest pooled difference from the ladder is 0.037% of equity (they said 0.06). The finding misses that exitstyle has BH-significant per-cell gains for fixed TPs exactly in the candidate cells: tp1R at N01_ST_EMA@15m; tp1.5R/tp2R at N24_DMI@15m/30m and N20_EMA9_CHOP@15m/30m. These matter for those traders' custom values even though the pooled effect is about 0.

findings.claim: On 15m/30m vs 1h/4h, the 5-year ranking (4h least bad, then 1h, 30m, 15m) comes entirely from cost. 4h is the only timeframe with several near-zero cells, but it is rare under v4 sizing and has almost no live data.
findings.evidence: Core cost R 0.173 (15m), 0.124 (30m), 0.094 (1h), 0.072 (4h), with gross about 0 at all four. Cells with net mean > 0: core 4h 3 of 26 non-thin vs 0-1 at 15m-1h; 4h is mostly class Z+ (18 core, 18 DS) because n is small, not because of an edge. Only 19.7% of 4h 5-year signals pass v4 sizing; core 4h has 7.3 enterable signals/day across all 35 strategies. Live 4h replay: core +0.206R (n 28), which drops to +0.068 when the 14 still-open signals are counted at mark; DS -0.122 (n 51).
findings.implication: The owners' plan (AI enters on 15m/30m; 1h/4h stay cost-free rule accounts) puts the AI where the 5-year hurdle is highest. If budget allows, give at least one AI trader 1h entries for comparison. Keep 4h as rule accounts and judge them only on 5-year-sized samples, never on a few live trades.

verification.recomputed: Core cost R 0.173/0.124/0.094/0.072 with gross about 0 (4h +0.022, t 1.65). Core cells with n>=30 and net>0: 15m 0/34, 30m 1/34, 1h 1/33, 4h 3/27. Class Z+ at 4h: 18 core and 18 DS. Sized share at 4h 19.67%; core 4h enterable signals 7.31/day across 35 strategies. Live 4h replay: core +0.206 (n 28), and +0.068 with the unresolved signals at mark; DS -0.122 (n 51).
verification.note: Reproduces exactly.

findings.claim: DeepSeek: the house exits and the pre-registered exits (PREREG) lose about the same over 5 years. No DeepSeek definition is positive in both 5-year halves at 15m/30m/1h, and the two PREREG stage-1 passes (both 4h) failed stage 2.
findings.evidence: Mean net % per trade, house / X5_TRAIL2 / X2_SL15_TP3: 15m -0.149/-0.151/-0.142, 30m -0.152/-0.167/-0.147, 1h -0.160/-0.175/-0.159, 4h -0.189/-0.211/-0.172. Cross-cell rank agreement with the house exits at 15m: 0.47 (p 0.0008, X5) and 0.70 (p<0.001, X2). Stage-1 passes: F5_BOX@4h X2 and F13_FVG_PD@4h X5; both have negative CF. The PREREG gross per trade is negative on every timeframe (per_tf.csv). Files: fy_ds_prereg_vs_house.csv, research/deepseek200/out/results.csv.
findings.implication: The DeepSeek family is no better a source for AI traders than the core 36. Its live 15m outperformance over 1.5 days is a lucky stretch (F3/F6), not evidence of an edge. Duplicates (F11_RAID = F11_TSOUP = F13_RAID_PD @15m, etc.) should count as one strategy.

verification.recomputed: v3ds11.py: house net % per trade (cell average) 15m -0.1485, 30m -0.1523, 1h -0.1598, 4h -0.1886. PREREG (results.csv, IS+CF n-weighted) X5_TRAIL2 -0.152/-0.167/-0.177/-0.213; X2_SL15_TP3 -0.142/-0.148/-0.161/-0.170. Spearman house vs X5/X2: 15m 0.46/0.67, 30m 0.23/0.30, 1h 0.41/0.36, 4h 0.11/0.18. Stage 1 = 2 (F5_BOX@4h X2 CF -0.413%, F13_FVG_PD@4h X5 CF -0.532%), stage 2 = 0. per_tf.csv PREREG gross per trade: -0.045/-0.055/-0.060/-0.020% (IS) and negative in CF on every timeframe.
verification.note: The numbers reproduce within 0.003%. 'No DS definition positive in both halves at 15m/30m/1h' is true only for the house exits. Under PREREG X2_SL15_TP3, F5_BOX_RSI@1h has IS +0.008% (n 170) and CF +0.319% (n 123), not significant (p12 0.22, pre-period -1.34%). The units are consistent: house and PREREG are both unlevered net % per notional per trade, though the PREREG % is not normalized for risk (its stops differ).

findings.claim: Reel 5m behaves exactly as its 5-year study predicts, and the prediction is a steady loss.
findings.evidence: 5 years: 35,858 trades (19.0/day), net -0.125%/trade, gross before costs +0.011% (IS) / +0.007% (CF), r_net -0.55 per trade, 33% wins. Live: 18.0 signals/day; 13 trades R -0.458 (46% wins), mean -0.019%/trade; all 27 signals including 14 skipped shadows (ROE/30) average -0.156%/trade, at percentile 0.44 of 5-year 1.5-day windows (band p5..p95 -0.417%..+0.137%). Files: fy_reel.csv, research/reel5m/out/h1_trades.csv.gz.
findings.implication: Do not give the reel an AI trader. Keep it, if at all, as the documented 5m control.

verification.recomputed: research/reel5m/out/h1_trades.csv.gz, IS+CF: 35,858 trades (19.01/day), net -0.1247%/trade, gross_raw +0.0108% (IS) / +0.0072% (CF), r_net -0.549, wins 32.9%. Live reel: 13 trades, mean R -0.458, 46.2% wins, -0.019%/trade. In 1.5-day 5-year windows (p5/p50/p95 -0.43/-0.14/+0.135%), -0.156% sits at the 0.45 percentile.
verification.note: Exact (their 0.44). The 'gross' column in the trades file is negative (-0.022/-0.026%) because it already includes slippage. Their +0.011% is gross_raw, the same as h1.json.

findings.claim: Combined grades (5-year class x live class): no A; 3 B (all rare 1h/4h cells); 54 C, mostly low-power 4h cells plus 8 cost-killed 15m/30m/1h cells with live >= 0; 117 D; 158 F; 19 thin. The best 15m/30m combinations still lose 0.11-0.17R per trade over 5 years.
findings.evidence: fiveyear_vs_live.csv (351 rows). B: N23_HA_ST@4h, S1_EMA_RSI_CHOP@1h (0.02 enterable/day), DS F10_M2022@4h (0.02/day). Best at 15m/30m (all class N+ with live L+): core N01_ST_EMA@15m (5y -0.173, gross +0.011 in both halves, live +0.16+/-0.47 n30), N10_HA_PSAR@15m (-0.174, live +0.07+/-0.22 n44), N24_DMI@30m (-0.125, live +0.07+/-0.16 n33); DS F7_RF_TRIPLE@30m (-0.108, gross +0.012 in both halves, t 2.0, live +0.08+/-0.32 n40), F7_RF_TRIPLE@15m, F9_IFVG@15m (gross t 2.55), F6_VWAP_CROSS@15m, F12_MSS@30m. Highest 5-year gross: F16_FIB382@15m and F16_FIB500@15m (grade D; live -0.40 n18 and +0.29 n13). 1h/4h: N23_HA_ST@4h, N22_VORTEX_PSAR@4h (gross t 2.4), N02_ST_KST@4h, S2_ST_ROC@4h, N24_DMI@1h, N20_EMA9_CHOP@1h; DS F2_DEMARK@4h, F6_VWAP_CROSS@1h, F15_ORB@4h. Files: fy_candidates.csv, fy_grade.py.
findings.implication: If AI traders must be assigned, prefer the C-grade cells whose 5-year gross is >= 0 in both halves and that give >= 10 signals/day. Their direction content is at least not negative and they give the AI many chances to skip. Treat every assignment as an experiment whose null is the strategy's own every-signal R, which the 5-year data puts at -0.15 to -0.23R.

verification.recomputed: v3grade.py: their class and grade rules applied to my own 5-year cells and live (2h-cluster) table, 15m-4h. B 3 (N23_HA_ST@4h, S1_EMA_RSI_CHOP@1h, F10_M2022@4h), C 54, D 115, F 126, thin 17 (theirs B 3, C 54, D 114, F 127, thin 17). 97% of cells agree; the 9 differences sit at the t=-2 or mu+-2SE edges. The candidate lists reproduce: 15m/30m N01_ST_EMA@15m, N10_HA_PSAR@15m, N24_DMI@30m, F7_RF_TRIPLE@30m/15m, F9_IFVG@15m, F6_VWAP_CROSS@15m, F12_MSS@30m, plus 3 rare Z+ cells; 1h/4h list as in fy_candidates.csv.
verification.note: The counts are right, but the method is weak. (1) The grade relies on the live sign, which F5/F6 show is noise. As a result, the cells with the strongest 5-year direction evidence (F16_FIB382@15m and F16_FIB500@15m, both BH-significant and positive in both halves) get D because of 13-18 live trades. F9_FVG@15m (gross t 2.56, both halves) is left out. N10_HA_PSAR@15m and N24_DMI@30m are listed as 'best' although their IS gross is negative. (2) A 5-year class 'N+' with t <= -2 plus a positive live sign gets C, the same grade as an untested Z+ cell. (3) The 1h/4h C list consists mostly of low-power 4h cells (n 39-1,416), where t>-2 means a weak test rather than evidence. With 26-36 cells per kind, a few gross t of about 2 are expected by chance (e.g. F15_ORB@4h is +0.041 while F15_ORB@15m is -0.052, t -4.1).

findings.claim: Detecting a real AI edge before 12/31 is possible only with enough independent trades and a paired comparison.
findings.evidence: R sd per trade, live replay: 15m 1.34, 30m 0.94, 1h 0.77; 5-year 15m 0.90, 30m 0.80. Trades needed to detect +0.2R at 80% power (one-sided 5%): 15m 140-280, 30m about 110-140, 1h about 90, before clustering. Live signals arrive in clusters; the cluster SEs here imply effective n well below raw n.
findings.implication: Per AI trader, log every rule signal it saw with the AI's decision (take/skip/near-entry) and the same-moment rule replay. Judge it on the paired difference with cluster-robust SE, pre-register the decision rule, and do not promote any trader before about 150 resolved, de-clustered decisions.

verification.note: The 15m range starts at 125, not 140. Otherwise it holds. For a paired AI-vs-rule test, the relevant sd is that of the paired difference, which is not estimated here. Clustering raises all of these numbers.

strategy_note_problems: The strategy_notes in resume/lens_fiveyear.json cover only 61 of 80 strategies (136 of 351 cells). The full set exists in lens/fiveyear/out/strategy_notes_grouped.json but was not carried over. The 18 omitted include N17_KC_RSI (the busiest core strategy, about 68 sized signals/day at 15m, with BH-significant NEGATIVE gross at 15m/30m/1h, and one of the F5 'best live' cells), N04_ST_KLINGER (74/day at 15m/30m), DOGE, the F5_BOX/F5_BOX_HTF/F5_BOX_RSI duplicate family, F4_PULL (52/day), F9_OB, OBV_B/OBV_S, V45_AMB, S3_CMO_SANDWICH, S5_DONCHIAN_MFI, N13_3OUTSIDE, N14_ICHI_RSI (thin), N19_FIB_CHOP, F3_BOS_ZONE and F8_VWICK.

Spot check of all 136 cell entries (5-year net, gross, live n and mean, grade) against my tables: the numbers agree within rounding. The one grade difference is F16_FIB500@4h, F (NN) vs my D (Z-), at t of about -2.

The notes give the gross mean but not its t or BH q, except for F16_FIB382 and N23. Readers cannot tell 'about 0' from 'reliably wrong-way'. For example, the F11_RAID/F13_RAID_PD/F11_TSOUP, F17_Z/F17_Z_HL and F15_ORB/F15_ASIA_SWEEP notes do not say their direction is significantly negative.

The live part of each note (rp n, mean+-SE) feeds the grade, although the lens's own F5/F6 show it carries no information. Notes such as 'N+/L++' for N20_EMA9_CHOP@1h (live +0.29+/-0.10, n 17) read as a positive signal.

The F16_FIB382 note says 'best 5y gross edge of all 15m cells'. It does not say that F16_FIB500@15m is also BH-significant, or that the two share only 18% of their signals (3,842 identical of about 21.6k/22.8k), so they are close to independent confirmations of a Fibonacci-retracement edge before costs.
verifier_missed: Anti-edges. 18 cells have BH-significant negative gross (week-clustered, 307 cells with n>=200), against 4 positive. Examples: N17_KC_RSI at 15m (t -3.35), 30m (-2.97) and 1h (-3.90); DS F15_ORB@15m (-4.11); F11_RAID@15m (-4.01) and its duplicates F13_RAID_PD/F11_TSOUP@15m; F17_Z and F17_Z_HL at 15m/1h/4h; F15_ASIA_SWEEP at 15m/30m/1h; F11_PO3 at 30m/1h; F1_PVT_DIV@15m; S4_BB_BBP@5m. These definitions should be the last choice for an AI trader. Flipping them gives only +0.02-0.05R of gross, well below the 0.17R cost at 15m.
The DS family has a small but consistent negative direction content at 15m/30m/1h (pooled gross -0.004 to -0.006R, week-clustered t -1.8 to -2.1). Core is at about 0.

Candidate list without the live sign. Ranked on 5-year evidence alone (gross positive in both halves, BH, frequency), the 15m/30m shortlist would be F16_FIB382@15m (gross +0.026, q 0.006, 11.2/day), F16_FIB500@15m (+0.022, q 0.020, 11.8/day), F9_IFVG@15m (+0.016, t 2.6), F9_FVG@15m (+0.017, t 2.56, 18/day), F7_RF_TRIPLE@30m (+0.012, t 2.0, 30/day) and N01_ST_EMA@15m (+0.011, t 1.3, 17/day). Every one is still about -0.14 to -0.17R net. The lens's C list dropped the first two and F9_FVG because of 13-26 live trades.

The 4h numbers describe a stop-selected subset. v4 sizing admits only 19.7% of 4h signals (narrow stops). The core 4h gross of +0.022R (t 1.65) holds for that subset only; verify_costs C2 finds -0.001R for all 4h signals at fixed 30x. '4h only where 20x is executable' in PLAN_ATTACH matches this subset, but the edge is not significant.

The window-length error for DS in fy_compare.py (2.2-day windows for a 1.5-day run), plus the use of two independent windows, overstated both the DS 15m live outlier and the 'quiet regime' percentile (F2/F3).

The research/exitstyle per-cell BH-significant TP gains in candidate cells (N01_ST_EMA@15m tp1R; N24_DMI and N20_EMA9_CHOP at 15m/30m tp1.5R/tp2R) bear directly on those traders' custom values. The lens reported only the pooled result.
The levstop 'sig_pos_bh' cells (N14_ICHI_RSI@15m/1h/4h, N15_KC_AO@4h, DOGE@4h) rest on 1-2 trades. Anyone reading levstop.json should ignore them. The lens did not warn about this.

findings.claim: Walk-forward custom-value search (225 combinations per cell, trailing window, applied to the next 1 or 4 weeks) does not beat default values out of sample once results are measured in a stop-independent money unit.
findings.evidence: out_R2/wf_methods.csv, naive rows: pooled OOS delta -0.0040 to +0.0037 R2 per trade over 8 schemes (1,258,505 default trades, 36 cells, 268 OOS weeks), all 95% day-cluster CIs include 0 (e.g. monthly/26 wk -0.0009 [-0.0135, +0.0124]); 0 of 36 cells BH-significant in 7 of 8 schemes (1 in s4_w1); 12 to 17 of 36 cells positive (chance level).
findings.implication: Do not let the bot adopt searched custom values without a gate and shadow check; the owners' premise is not supported on 5-year data.

verification.recomputed: R2 naive, 8 schemes: -0.0040..+0.0037, all CIs include 0 (wf_methods). Own net % per notional bootstrap, 36 cells (verify/vnp.py): s4_w26 -0.0164 pp [-0.0405, +0.0056] against a default of -0.150 %/trade; s4_w13 -0.0160 [-0.0384, +0.0067]; s1_w1 -0.0249 [-0.0447, -0.0048]; the 8 schemes range -0.011 to -0.025 pp.
verification.note: The no-gain verdict holds and is stronger in money per notional: the search is worse in all 8 schemes (7-17% larger loss per trade), and significantly worse with the 1-week window. Small fixes: BH hits are 2 in s1_w4 and 1 in s4_w1 (0 in 6 of 8 schemes, not 7 of 8); there are 269 OOS weeks, not 268.

findings.claim: In the pre-registered stop-relative R the same search looks like a +0.02 to +0.025 R win, but this is an artefact of stop width.
findings.evidence: out/wf_methods.csv: pooled delta +0.0236..+0.0254 R (CI above 0 for 6 of 8 schemes; 24-32 of 36 cells positive), yet net return per trade in % moved -0.008 to -0.019 pct points; naive pick uses the 2.5 ATR stop in 78% of weeks (26 wk), static 2.5 ATR is -0.005 R2 in half A and -0.004 in half B (3 and 8 of 36 cells positive). out/pick_composition.csv.
findings.implication: Any custom-value search must score candidates in money (or R at the default stop), never in R of the candidate stop; otherwise it will always find "wider stops are better".

verification.recomputed: out/wf_methods naive (R): +0.0073 (s1_w1), +0.0123 (s4_w1), +0.0195 (s4_w4), +0.0232..+0.0254 (others). CI above 0 in 7 of 8 schemes, cells positive 18-32, PREREG rule passes 6 of 8. Net% -0.008..-0.019 pp. 2.5 ATR stop share 0.78 (26 wk).
verification.note: The mechanism (R rewards wide stops) is confirmed by my own walk-forward. The stated evidence range (+0.0236..+0.0254, CI>0 in 6 of 8, 24-32 cells) is wrong; the correct figures are in recomputed.

findings.claim: The in-sample gain of the picked combination vanishes out of sample.
findings.evidence: mean training improvement of the pick over default 0.137 R (26 wk) to 0.491 R (1 wk) per trade (out_R2/wf_methods.csv); out-of-sample about 0; half-A top-10 combos +0.042 R in A and +0.006 R in B (out_R2/persistence.csv, 36 cells; positive in B in 22 of 36 cells; mean Spearman A vs B +0.24). Picks that lose to default in the applied period: 43-52% of switches.
findings.implication: Show the owners the training-vs-next-period gap; a weekly "best value found" report is a noise report.

verification.recomputed: Mean training improvement of the pick 0.137 (26 wk) to 0.491 (1 wk). Top-10 half A +0.042 -> half B +0.0057, positive in B in 22 of 36 cells, mean Spearman +0.238. Noise rate 0.505-0.524 (R2 naive), 0.428-0.511 (R naive).
verification.note: Reproduced from the tables. My 4-cell walk-forward gives the same OOS collapse.

findings.claim: Short windows are worse; at 13 to 26 weeks the search is stable but still at zero. Weekly versus monthly re-tuning does not matter at long windows.
findings.implication: If a search runs: monthly, trailing 26 weeks; never a 1-week window.

verification.note: 'Short windows are worse' holds only for the weekly re-tune with a 1-week window, and only clearly in net %. In R2, the monthly re-tune with a 1-week window (s4_w1) has one of the highest deltas of the 8 schemes. No window difference is established. Advising against the 1-week window plus weekly re-tune is fine; 'monthly, 26 weeks' is not shown to be better than the other windows.

findings.claim: Of the kinds of custom values, only context filters (and a tighter stop) show small, stable out-of-sample value; indicator values are weak, exit styles are negative.
findings.evidence: out_R2/wf_methods.csv: filter-only search +0.0061 [+0.0013, +0.0109] (monthly/26wk), +0.0067 [+0.0017, +0.0111] (13 wk), half A/B +0.0095/+0.0018 and +0.0075/+0.0055, 25 of 36 cells positive, but only 56% of the trades kept. Stop-only +0.0026 [+0.0014, +0.0038] (half B +0.0004). Indicator-only +0.0031 [+0.0011, +0.0052] (half B +0.0003). Exit-only -0.0006..-0.0031 (CI includes 0). Static levels (out_R2/levels_summary.csv): HTF agreement +0.0048/+0.0086 (A/B), box +0.0024/+0.0075, session -0.0024/-0.0026, stop 1.5 +0.0049/+0.0030, R-ladder -0.0035/-0.0063.
findings.implication: Treat HTF/ADX/box filters and a 1.5 ATR stop as candidate tests worth 0.005 R each, not as a rescue: the cost is 0.08 to 0.17 R per trade.

verification.note: In the pre-registered money metric (net % per notional) the filter-only search is not significant and fades in half B. The indicator-only search is negative, not 'weak positive'. The stop-only gain is partly the k/2 rescale (about 0.001) and is gone in half B. Only the HTF agreement filter is positive in both units and both halves. All effects are at most 0.01 R, against a cost of 0.08-0.17 R.

findings.claim: Nothing found is anywhere near the break-even gap. Default cost is 0.168 R (15m), 0.116 R (30m), 0.081 R (1h) per trade and gross edge is about 0 (-0.002, -0.004, -0.003 R).
findings.evidence: out_R2/cell_desc.csv: default pooled net R/trade -0.170 / -0.120 / -0.084 at 15m / 30m / 1h (691,714 / 368,276 / 198,515 trades); 34 of 36 cells have 0 of 225 combinations with positive 5-year mean R (F5_BOX_30m: 2, F5_BOX_1h: 40 of 225, n=2,199).
findings.implication: Custom values cannot be the source of the edge. The AI must beat the cost by trade selection or exits; budget the cost first.

verification.note: Reproduced. In % per notional the loss is almost the same at every timeframe; it is smaller in R at 1h only because the stop is wider in price.

findings.claim: An adoption gate works only if it is permissive enough to see a real gain and strict enough to ignore noise; the 0.15 R gate is both too strict for +0.10 R and slightly harmful on the actual data; the best tested gate is N_min 100 / delta 0.05 R / z >= 2 / two halves.
findings.evidence: out_R2/wf_methods.csv gates (monthly, 26 wk): 100/0.05/2: +0.0007 [-0.0044, +0.0059], switch share 0.45; 100/0.15/2: -0.0028 [-0.0047, -0.0010]; 100/0.30/2: switch share 0.04. Planted gain (out_R2/planted_summary.csv, 36 cells): +0.20 R captured 86% (gate 100/0.05/2), 76% (100/0.15/2), 1% (100/0.30/2); +0.10 R captured 42%, 2%, 0%; naive no gate 89% / 58% but wrong combination in 16% / 48% of weeks.
findings.implication: Use the 100 / 0.05 R2 / z2 / two-half gate on a 26-week window with an all-signal shadow confirmation; expect to see only effects >= 0.10 R.

verification.note: The recommendation contradicts the PREREG decision rule. The rule says: if no gate passes, keep defaults live and use the strictest gate as the proposal filter. The analyst instead recommends a permissive gate chosen after the fact from the planted test. On the real data that gate switches in 45% of cell-weeks with a 51% noise rate and loses 0.0055 pp per trade in net %. The gate's z test is not adjusted for picking the best of 225 candidates. The planted gains (0.10-0.30 R) are 15-60 times larger than any real effect seen (at most 0.008), so the test says nothing about catching realistic gains.

findings.claim: Confirming a real improvement takes months to years. With the all-signal shadow stream a +0.10 R custom value takes a median 14 weeks per cell (range 3 to 87), +0.20 R a median 3.5 weeks, +0.05 R a median 56 weeks; a one-position trader needs 2 to 11 times longer.
findings.evidence: out_R2/cell_desc.csv (weeks_needed_*, design effect 1.4 to 12) and out/one_position.csv (one-position trades per week 3.8 to 51, mean 23 vs 130 for all signals); one-sided alpha 5%, power 80%, one comparison, no multiplicity.
findings.implication: By 12/31 (about 12 weeks) only gains >= 0.2 R in the high-frequency cells can be confirmed; always track all signals in the shadow account, not the AI's own trades.

verification.recomputed: Own code (verify/vpow.py): one-sample formula reproduces the analyst within 1%. +0.10 median 13.9 weeks (2.8-87.4), +0.20 3.5, +0.05 55.7. Day design effect 1.36-12.1. A two-sample (candidate vs concurrently estimated default, unpaired) test needs x2: +0.10 median 27.9 weeks (3 of 36 cells within 12 weeks), +0.20 median 7.0 (27 of 36). One-position stream: design effect 0.95-1.11, so its weeks / all-signal weeks = 0.73-6.3 (median 1.4), not 2-11; one-position +0.10 median 19.7 weeks (12.4-86.3).
verification.note: The formula is a one-sample test against a known value, not the 'unpaired comparison' the limits describe. An unpaired candidate needs twice as long. A filter judged as a subset of the same trades is close to one-sample; a stop or exit change judged on the same trades (paired) needs fewer weeks. '2 to 11 times longer' is just the trades-per-week ratio. It ignores that the one-position stream is barely clustered, so the true factor is 0.7-6.3, and for F5_BOX the one-position trader needs fewer weeks. '+0.20 R only in high-frequency cells by 12/31' is wrong: 33 of 36 cells one-sample, 27 of 36 two-sample. No allowance is made for the 225-way search.

findings.claim: Pre-registered verdicts: literal rule gives "beats defaults" in R for 6 of 8 schemes and "gate keeps real" for the 0.05 R gates; in money units 0 of 8 and 0 of 144. The post-hoc amendment is disclosed.
findings.evidence: out/wf_methods.csv vs out_R2/wf_methods.csv columns beats_default / gate_keeps_real; AMENDMENTS.md.
findings.implication: Report both; decisions rest on the money-unit result.

verification.recomputed: R2 PREREG verdicts: naive 0 of 8, gates 0 of 144 (correct), but restricted searches pass 14 times: filter-only 7 of 8 schemes, stop-only 4, P-only 3. R: naive 6 of 8; gates pass 76 rows.
verification.note: The CV9 numbers are right but leave out that the per-dimension searches pass the PREREG rule in R2. That 'positive' verdict depends on the post-hoc unit: in the pre-registered secondary money metric (net %), filter-only s4_w26 and s4_w13 do not have CI > 0, and P-only is negative.

strategy_note_problems: Numbers: all 36 notes match the tables (14 fields each, within 1%): cell_desc, wf_cells, persistence, one_position.

Template text '(mostly wide-stop artefact)' is applied where it is wrong: where the R delta is negative (N24_DMI_1h -0.0425, OBV_B_1h, N17_KC_RSI_15m, N16_BBRSI_1h) or smaller than the R2 delta (N17_KC_RSI_1h +0.012 vs +0.032, F5_BOX_30m +0.012 vs +0.064).

N24_DMI_1h: the search significantly HURTS (-0.0826 R2/trade, p_le0 = 1.00, 26 wk; also significant at 13 wk and 1 wk), but the note only says 'BH10 fail'. Same for N17_KC_RSI_15m and N16_BBRSI_30m at 13 wk (-0.060, p 0.99 / 0.98) and N16_BBRSI_15m at 1 wk (-0.060, p 0.998). The notes never flag significant harm.

F5_BOX 'D (watch)': based on in-sample counts (40 of 225 combinations positive at 1h with n = 2,199 and a best-of-225 pick; 2 of 225 at 30m), non-significant walk-forward p values 0.20-0.39, and negative top-10 rank persistence at 15m (Spearman -0.29) and 1h (-0.17). 'Positive in all three timeframes' is 3 non-significant draws. It does not justify a watch status beyond any other D.
Notes report only R and R2. None gives net % per notional, the money unit for the bot's fixed-notional sizing, and none says whether the effects survive in it.
verifier_missed: PREREG already had a stop-independent money metric (net % per notional, secondary). In it the naive search loses 0.011-0.025 pp per trade in all 8 schemes (significant for s1_w1), filter-only is not significant, and P-only is negative (verify/vnp.json).
paperbot sizing is margin_frac x leverage (fixed notional), so money = net %, not R2. R2 corresponds to volatility-scaled sizing. The two units disagree on the ADX and box filters.
The k/2 rescale ignores slippage in the stop distance and biases toward the 1.5 ATR stop by about 0.001 R2 (exact unit: net% / default stop%).
No two-sided harm check: several cells are significantly hurt by the search (N24_DMI_1h -0.08 R2). A live search would cause real damage in some strategies, not just noise.

The adoption gate's z threshold is not adjusted for picking the best of 225 candidates (about z 3.5 would be needed). The planted test only uses effects of 0.10-0.30, far above any real effect (at most 0.008), so gate behaviour for realistic gains is untested.

Only the 20x ladder geometry was tested. The owners plan 20-50x, and the ROE ladder locks at smaller price moves at higher leverage (CONTEXT: lock/lev variants), so custom exits interact with leverage. 4h is not tested.
The 5-year sd and cost differ from the current quiet market (15m cost about 0.22R live vs 0.168R), so the weeks-to-confirm figures will not carry over unchanged to the shadow account.

Week-cluster bootstrap (own) gives CIs close to the day-cluster ones (e.g. filter-only R2 [+0.0016, +0.0108] vs [+0.0011, +0.0111]), so the clustering choice is not a problem. Cross-strategy overlap is handled only by resampling days jointly.
limits: Every signal is a trade, no one-position limit, no portfolio, no margin or liquidation model (the 20x house ladder geometry is used for the lock only; a bar gapping through the stop beyond -100% ROE is not clamped: 2 to 5 of 3,000 sample trades). Results are per-notional unit results, not account curves.

The pre-registered metric (R) turned out to depend on the stop; the money-unit metric R2 was added after seeing the R results (amendment A1, disclosed). The R2 design (scale by k/2) is exact only for per-notional comparisons; it ignores that wider stops allow lower leverage at fixed risk.

Search space is modest (225 combinations, one parameter at a time at x0.75 and x1.25, four filters, three stops, three exits). A larger space or smarter search (Bayesian, shrinkage, regime-conditional) is not tested; it would face more selection noise, not less. Only 3 timeframes (15m, 30m, 1h); no 4h.

Day-cluster bootstrap treats days as independent. Week-to-week dependence, regime shifts and cross-strategy overlap (the 36 cells share coins and many signals, and the 12 strategies are not independent) are not modelled, so CIs are somewhat optimistic and the pooled-over-cells CI is narrower than a strategy-level one.

F6_VWAP_CROSS variants (weekly VWAP anchor, volume confirm, ATR buffers) and the filter definitions (HTF EMA50, ADX 20/25, box 48 bars, UTC 07-20 session) are my own and fixed before looking at results; they are not the repo's locked definitions. F6/F5/F9 default signals match lib_c.entries bar for bar.
Stop/take-profit ordering inside a bar is conservative (stop first); taker fills with fixed slippage; no maker fills, no real order book; funding is a constant 0.01%/8h.

Weeks-to-confirm uses the default stream variance and measured design effect for an unpaired one-comparison test; a paired test of a filter that is a subset of the default trades needs fewer trades, a 225-way search needs more. One-position counts use a greedy first-come, first-served thinning on the default stream.

The planted-improvement test plants a constant true gain in one random combination with >= 30% of the default trades; real improvements are likely time-varying and smaller, so the capture shares are optimistic.
The 2021-2026 period contains one market history; "5 years" is not 5 independent samples. The current market (quiet, narrow stops) has higher cost in R than the 5-year mean.
Not tested: AI discretion (skipping, early exit, switching), 4h, intraday-event filters, data after 2026-09-29, entry-quality tiers.

findings.claim: Under rules, every setup and every priority rule loses per trade when pooled, for the 36 and for DeepSeek (in both halves); the per-trade loss is almost exactly the trading cost, because the signals' gross R (before fees, slippage, funding) is about zero in every setup.
findings.evidence: 5-year (2021-08..2026-09, Binance futures bars, 6 coins), house exits, normal leverage chain. Core36 net R/trade: A -0.147, B -0.136, C-proxy (switch only to higher tf) -0.121, D = -0.134 pooled (15m/30m trader -0.147 + 1h/4h trader -0.087); gross R +0.002 / +0.001 / -0.001 / +0.001; cost R 0.148 / 0.137 / 0.120 / 0.088. DeepSeek44 the same shape (A -0.155, C-proxy -0.121, 1h/4h -0.097). Both halves (IS 2021-08..2024-06 / CF 2024-07..2026-09) negative in every setup. Strategies with mean R > 0 in A: core 1/35 (the only positive one is N14_ICHI_RSI with 3 trades in 5 years), DeepSeek 0/44. summ/pooled.csv, per_strategy.csv.
findings.implication: The setup choice cannot make a rule account profitable; it only changes the hurdle the AI must clear (about = cost per trade) and how many decisions it gets. Any AI gain must come from selection/exit skill worth more than about 0.09-0.20R per trade (1h/4h 5-year cost to A cost in the last 91 days).

verification.recomputed: 3y subset, own sim, pooled per setup (core6 / ds2): net R/trade A|FC -0.147 / -0.173, ALL|FC -0.135 / -0.164, ALL|SWH -0.122 / -0.138, HI|FC -0.081 / -0.114; gross R +0.000..+0.010 (core), -0.011..-0.025 (ds); cost 0.154/0.123/0.089 (core A/C/HI). Every strategy x setup negative (0 of 175 cells positive, v_sim_rows.csv).
verification.note: Gross ~0 and net ~ -cost reproduce. The two DeepSeek definitions in the sample have slightly negative gross (-0.01..-0.025), so for them the hurdle is a bit above cost.

findings.claim: Cost hurdle per trade falls with the held timeframe: the C-proxy (one trader on 15m-4h, switching only to a higher timeframe) cuts the hurdle by ~0.03R/trade vs A, and a 1h/4h-only trader by ~0.06R, entirely through lower cost.
findings.evidence: Core36 paired vs A|FC: ALL|SWH +0.026R [95% week-cluster CI +0.022, +0.030], better in 34/35 strategies; ALL|FC +0.011R [95% week-cluster CI +0.009, +0.013], better in 35/35 strategies; HI|FC +0.060R [95% week-cluster CI +0.052, +0.069], better in 35/35 strategies. DeepSeek44: ALL|SWH +0.034R [95% week-cluster CI +0.031, +0.037], better in 44/44 strategies; HI|FC +0.057R [95% week-cluster CI +0.051, +0.064], better in 44/44 strategies. Cost R by single-tf rule account (core): 15m 0.164, 30m 0.119, 1h 0.091, 4h 0.068. Last 91 days of the data (2026-07..09, quieter): A cost 0.197R, ALL|SWH 0.152R, HI 0.107R (net -0.190 / -0.156 / -0.129). paired.csv, recent_cost.csv.
findings.confidence: high (differences are cost arithmetic; CIs exclude 0 and nearly every strategy agrees)
findings.implication: Lowest cost hurdle per decision: 1h/4h trader (D's second trader) < C-proxy < B < A. At today's volatility the A hurdle is ~0.20R/trade.

verification.recomputed: Paired vs A|FC (week-cluster bootstrap, 3y): core ALL|SWH +0.024 [+0.016,+0.033] (6/6), ALL|FC +0.012 [+0.006,+0.018] (6/6), HI|FC +0.066 [+0.050,+0.085] (6/6); ds ALL|SWH +0.034 [+0.019,+0.048], HI +0.059 [+0.032,+0.085]. Decomposition core ALL|SWH-A: dgross -0.007, dcost -0.031 (pure cost). Last 91 days (core6): cost A 0.194, ALL|SWH 0.148, HI 0.107 (study 0.197/0.152/0.107).
verification.note: Per-trade hurdle numbers reproduce. Caveat (see MT6/MT10): the per-trade metric is not the account result. Per day, the C-proxy pays about the same total cost as B (core6 0.683 vs 0.664 R/day with the same tie rule).

findings.claim: Decision counts: A and B/C give ~4-5 rule trades/day per trader out of ~25-29 signals/day; a 1h/4h-only trader gets ~1.2-1.5 trades/day out of ~4 signals/day, too few to confirm an AI effect within a 60-day check.
findings.evidence: Core36 per trader: A 4.24 trades/day from 24.9 signals/day; ALL|SWH 4.47 from 28.5; HI 1.15 from 3.6. Smallest mean-R change detectable in 60 days (80% power, 5% two-sided, i.i.d. trades = optimistic): A 0.15R, ALL|SWH 0.12R, HI 0.23R (R sd 0.85 / 0.72 / 0.68). Live v4 cross-check (1.5 days): core A 4.47 trades/day/trader, HI 1.76. pooled.csv, dd_quarter_summary.csv, live_check_summary.csv.
findings.confidence: medium-high (MDE ignores time clustering, so real MDEs are larger)
findings.implication: C-proxy gives the most decisions at the lowest per-trade hurdle with enough n; D's 1h/4h trader has the lowest hurdle but cannot be judged by 12/31 on its own.

verification.recomputed: core6 3y: A|FC 5.31 trades/day from 29.5 signals/day, ALL|SWH 5.56 from 33.9, HI 1.53 from 4.45 (these 6 are busier than the 35 average). 60-day MDE i.i.d. A 0.133R, C 0.104R, HI 0.197R; week-cluster design effect 1.05 / 1.02 / 0.95, so clustered MDE 0.136 / 0.105 / 0.193.
verification.note: Counts and MDE arithmetic reproduce. Inside one trader, time clustering barely inflates the MDE because only one position is open at a time, so the study's warning that real MDEs are larger is small for one trader. It matters for pooling traders on overlapping strategies. An AI-vs-shadow comparison with two independent arms needs about x1.4 the MDE.

findings.claim: One position at a time blocks most signals: 60%-77% in setups that include 15m/30m, 48%-55% for a 1h/4h trader; and the blocked signals are no better than the taken ones, so blocking per se does not throw away measurable edge.
findings.evidence: Blocked by an open position (ties at the same moment listed separately), core: A 73% (+10%), B 76% (+9%), C-proxy 72% (+12%), HI 55%; blocked signals alone -0.159R vs taken -0.147R (A), -0.154 vs -0.122 (C-proxy). Live v4 (1.5 days, replayed signals): A blocked 82% (core) / 84% (DeepSeek). pooled.csv, live_check_summary.csv.
findings.confidence: high for the shares; the 'no better' statement is about rules, an AI choosing among signals could differ
findings.implication: The AI has about 5.9-6.4 signals per position slot to choose from (A, C-proxy); a skip-heavy AI loses little by passing. Ranking/skip skill is where an AI could add value.

verification.recomputed: Blocked (non-tie) share core6: A|FC 74% (+8% ties), ALL|SWH 74% (+10%), HI 54% (+12%); ds2 69% / 69% / 48%. Blocked alone-R vs taken: core A -0.168 vs -0.147; ds -0.188 vs -0.173. Within the same tf it still holds: core A 15m blocked -0.184 vs taken -0.159, 30m -0.133 vs -0.115.
verification.note: Reproduces. Blocked signals are slightly WORSE than taken ones even within a timeframe, so under rules one-position blocking is mildly helpful. This is about rule signals and says nothing about AI ranking skill.

findings.claim: Long 1h/4h holds do block many 15m/30m signals, but the blocked low-tf signals during 4h holds are the worst ones (quiet-market 15m signals with high cost in R).
findings.evidence: Core ALL|FC: 1h/4h positions are 26% of held time and cause 23% of blocked 15m/30m signals; 37% of 1h/4h trades block >= 5 and 23% >= 10 15m/30m signals (mean 8.0). With switch-only-to-higher (C-proxy) 1h/4h hold 50% of the time, 30% block >= 10. 15m signals blocked while a 4h position is open: -0.233R alone vs -0.168R when blocked by a 15m position. DeepSeek: by_hi 23%, >=10 21%. blocking_long.csv, blocked_matrix.csv.
findings.implication: Letting 1h/4h signals occupy the trader is not costly in R terms; it is the reason C/B beat A (fewer expensive 15m trades).

verification.recomputed: ALL|FC core6: 25.9% of blocked 15m/30m signals were blocked by a 1h/4h position (ds2 24.1%; study 23%). 15m signals blocked during a 4h hold -0.273R (n 4,866) vs -0.177R when blocked by a 15m position (n 50,486); ds -0.254 vs -0.212.
verification.note: Direction and size reproduce.

findings.claim: Switching to any new signal (the 'human' switch) is the worst proxy: 3x the trades, more cost, lower R; switching only to a higher timeframe is the best of the four rules.
findings.evidence: Core: ALL|SW vs ALL|FC -0.023R [95% week-cluster CI -0.028, -0.018], better in 4/35 strategies; A|SW vs A|FC -0.020R [95% week-cluster CI -0.025, -0.015], better in 5/35 strategies; ALL|SWH vs ALL|FC +0.015R [95% week-cluster CI +0.012, +0.018], better in 29/35 strategies; longer-tf-first on ties vs first-come +0.005R [95% week-cluster CI +0.004, +0.006], better in 27/35 strategies. ALL|SW trades/day 14.7, 11.1 switches/day; the early close itself costs ~0 (+0.004R vs holding), the loss is the extra round trips. DeepSeek same sign: ALL|SW vs ALL|FC -0.016R [95% week-cluster CI -0.020, -0.012], better in 10/44 strategies. paired.csv.
findings.implication: If the AI may switch, the default should be 'hold unless a higher-timeframe signal arrives'; frequent switching raises the hurdle.

verification.recomputed: Switch-to-any is worst: core ALL|SW - ALL|FC -0.030 [-0.040,-0.020] (0/6), A|SW - A|FC -0.026 (0/6); per day -3.12 vs -0.69 R/day. Switched-out trades: R at switch -0.152 vs held-alone -0.152, so the early close itself costs ~0 and the extra round trip is the loss (study's costing reproduces: exit taker+slip at the next 15m open, new entry with its own cost). BUT 'switch only to higher tf is best' holds only per trade and is confounded: sim.py runs SWH with longer-tf-first tie order and FC with coin/shorter-tf-first order. With the tie rule held fixed, core ALL|SWH - ALL|LTF = +0.005 [-0.002,+0.012] (4/6) on my subset (study's own 5y res: +0.007/trade, 29/35). Per day (fixed risk per trade = account P&L), switching up LOSES MORE: study's own 5y res files, core ALL|SWH vs ALL|LTF -0.019 R/day (SWH better in only 10/35; ds 10/44); A|SWH vs A|FC -0.037 R/day (better in 4/35). Own subset: ALL|SWH -0.681 vs ALL|LTF -0.629 R/day; A|SWH -0.830 vs A|FC -0.779.
verification.note: SWH adds round trips (about 1.1-1.5 switches/day). Its lower cost per trade comes from moving into 1h/4h holds, but the account pays more total cost per day. It is the better rule only if the AI's per-trade edge is above the hurdle. At zero edge, no-switch with longer-tf-first ties (B/LTF) is the cheaper account. The +0.015R 'SWH vs FC' figure is about one-third tie-rule effect (LTF vs FC +0.005).

findings.claim: Leverage: with the house 2 ATR stop and the 1 ATR liquidation buffer, 20-50x is executable on 15m (and mostly 30m), 20x only on part of 1h, and 4h almost only on BTC (ETH in quiet weeks). Risk-per-stop sizing (2-5%) does not change the 20x limit, because the liquidation buffer binds; it only removes the 15% loss cap that blocks 40-50x.
findings.evidence: Share of bars sizable, mean over 6 coins, 5y / last 30 days: 4h at 20x house 19% / 26%, 30x 0.9% / 0%; 1h 20x 77% / 90%, 30x 26% / 33%; 15m 50x house 7% / 11% vs risk-per-stop 2% 51% / 63%. 4h 20x by coin 5y / last30d: BTC 56%/100%; ETH 25%/54%; SOL 4%/0%; DOGE 7%/0%; LTC 13%/1%; BCH 9%/0%. Live v4: 49% of core and 46% of DeepSeek 4h signals sized (rest REJECTED_SIZING). feas.csv, live_check.py.
findings.confidence: high (mechanical; brackets inferred from live trades)
findings.implication: '4h only where 20x executes' means mostly BTC 4h; in the 5-year simulation it keeps 4h trades rare (core 4h rule account 0.12 trades/day). Admitting sub-20x 4h trades (sensitivity ALLINF vs B) changes R by +0.009 only.

verification.recomputed: Own sizing math (v_feas.py) reproduces the bar shares exactly: 4h 20x 19.2% (5y) / 25.6% (last 30d), 30x 0.9% / 0%; 1h 20x 77.6% / 89.8%, 30x 25.9% / 32.6%; 4h 20x by coin 5y/30d BTC 56/100, ETH 25/53, SOL 4/0, DOGE 7/0, LTC 14/0.5, BCH 9/0. 15m house 50x 7.0% (5y), 40x 34%, 30x 80%; 30m 40x 13%, 50x 2%. 4h signals in the 3y subset: 24.3% sizable at 30x/20x; forced 20x without the buffer gate: liquidation price inside the stop for 38.8%, and 4.4% exit at the initial stop, i.e. would be liquidated first (3y, quieter; verify_costs 8.1% on 5y). 1h: 16.7% of signals not sizable at 20x/30x.
verification.note: The numbers are right, but the headline '20-50x is executable on 15m (and mostly 30m)' is wrong by the study's own feas.csv. Under house rules, 50x sizes on only 7% of 15m bars (11% last 30d) and 40x on 34%. On 30m, 40x sizes on 13% and 50x on 2%. Only 20-30x is broadly executable on 15m/30m. This agrees with verify_costs: both show 4h at 20x needs the per-signal gate (stop + 1 ATR inside liquidation). The study's 19% sizable share is the gated version of verify_costs' 8.1% liquidate-first figure, and the two do not conflict.

findings.claim: Drawdown at fixed risk: with ~4 trades/day, even a zero-net-edge trader at 1% risk per stop breaches the design's 25% drawdown gate in about a quarter of 91-day windows under A, less under the C-proxy, and almost never under a 1h/4h trader.
findings.evidence: Rule R series with each strategy's own mean removed (pure noise), 91-day windows, 1% risk per trade: median DD A 17%, p90 31%, windows > 25%: 23%; C-proxy 14% / 25% / 10%; HI 7% / 13% / 0%. With the actual negative drift at 2% risk the median 91-day DD is 72% (A), 69% (C-proxy), 21% (HI); share of 91-day windows with positive sum R: A 2.0%, HI 11.6%. dd_quarter_summary.csv.
findings.confidence: medium-high (assumes trade-sequence noise like the rules'; an AI that trades less would see less)
findings.implication: The DD gate is easier to pass with fewer, longer trades; at A's frequency the gate partly measures noise. Consider 0.5-1% risk per stop for 15m/30m traders.

verification.recomputed: Demeaned R, 91-day windows, 1% risk (own code): core6 A|FC median DD 20.3%, >25% in 25.6% of windows; ALL|SWH 16.7% / 12.0%; HI 7.5% / 0%; ds2 A 18.9% / 26.9%, ALL|SWH 13.1% / 7.7%, HI 6.7% / 0%. With the actual drift at 1% risk: >25% DD in 92% of A windows, 95% of ALL|SWH windows, 4% of HI windows.
verification.note: Reproduces (my A numbers are a little higher because the sample strategies trade more). Only about 12 windows per strategy in 3 years, so the window shares are coarse. The zero-net-edge assumption is generous: a rule-level trader (gross 0, cost paid) breaches 25% in about 9 of 10 quarters at 1% risk on A/C.

findings.claim: AI call volume is dominated by holding checks and by whether busy-time signals are shown to the AI; per-trader cost is similar for A, B and C, and a 1h/4h trader costs 36%-55% of an A trader.
findings.evidence: Per trader per day (core), entry calls between 'free-time signals only' and 'every signal incl. hold/switch consults', plus a check every 30 min while holding: A 26..47, B/C 30..54, 1h/4h trader 14..17; at $0.03/call (design v2 estimate): $24..$43, $27..$49, $13..$15 per trader-month; 30 traders A: $714..$1279 vs the $500 budget. D needs two traders per strategy (A + 1h/4h): $37..$58 per strategy-month. Checks at each held-timeframe bar close instead of every 30m: A 40/day, C-proxy 28/day, HI 7/day (free-entry calls included). pooled.csv.
findings.confidence: medium (call price is the design doc's estimate; an AI that skips more makes more entry calls and fewer hold calls)
findings.implication: $500/month covers about 12-21 A traders with 30-min hold checks, not 30, unless hold checks are thinned (e.g. bar-close of the held tf on 1h/4h positions) or busy-time signals are filtered by code.

verification.recomputed: Arithmetic from pooled.csv reproduces: A|FC core 4.24 entries + 4.24 x 2.58 h x 2 = 21.9 hold checks = 26/day; all-signal 24.9 + 21.9 = 47; 30 traders x 26..47 x 30 x $0.03 = $714..$1,279/month. Design doc v2 sec. 14-1 gives $0.03 per Sonnet call, or about $0.015 with good caching.
verification.note: With caching at $0.015, the range halves to about $357..$640 for 30 A traders. The lower bound assumes the AI takes every signal it sees while flat; a skip-heavy AI makes more entry calls. The design doc's locked cost rules (one call per bar close per trader, hold wake-ups only on an opposite signal, small model for routine hold checks) are not modelled and would cut hold calls a lot.

findings.claim: Ranking for 'conditions for the AI' (not profitability): C (one trader, 15m/30m/1h + 4h where 20x sizes, default hold, switch only to a higher timeframe) > B (same scope, first-come) > A on hurdle at the same decision count. D = A's 15m/30m seat plus a 1h/4h seat that has the lowest hurdle but the fewest decisions, and it doubles the seats.
findings.evidence: Core: hurdle (cost/trade) C 0.120R, B 0.137R, A 0.148R, D 0.148R (15m/30m seat) + 0.088R (1h/4h seat); trades/day 4.47 / 4.09 / 4.24 / 5.39 (two seats); net R/trade -0.121 / -0.136 / -0.147 / -0.134; zero-edge 91-day DD > 25% at 1% risk 10% / 19% / 23% / 23%+0%. C vs A per strategy: better in 34/35 core and 44/44 DeepSeek. All four remain negative.
findings.confidence: medium (rule proxies, not an AI; the ranking is about the starting hurdle and sample size)
findings.implication: If one AI seat per strategy, give it 15m/30m/1h (+BTC-type 4h when 20x sizes) with a 'switch only upward' default; keep 4h rule accounts as controls. Do not expect the setup alone to change the sign.

verification.recomputed: Per trade: C (ALL|SWH) > B > A reproduces (core6 -0.122 / -0.135 / -0.147). Per day (account P&L at fixed risk), study's own 5y res: core mean R/day A|FC -0.622, A|SWH -0.660, ALL|FC -0.556, ALL|SWH -0.540, ALL|LTF -0.521, HI -0.100; ds A -0.744, ALL|SWH -0.618, ALL|LTF -0.600, HI -0.143. ALL|LTF beats ALL|SWH per day in 25/35 core and 34/44 ds strategies.
verification.note: 'C best' holds only for the per-trade hurdle. For the account at zero or sub-hurdle edge, B with longer-tf-first ties (no switching) loses less per day than C. A tie rule that takes the widest stop first adds a further +0.014R/trade (core) and +0.019R (ds) on my subset, a free code-level gain. The robust ranking is {B-LTF ~ C} > A, with HI far lowest per day. That HI is lowest is a frequency effect (1.1-1.5 trades/day), not evidence of edge.

strategy_note_problems: 'Lowest-hurdle setup with >= 1 trade/day' (build_json.py line ~195) only compares A|FC, ALL|FC and ALL|SWH, never HI|FC. In 16 of the 35 core notes HI|FC has >= 1 trade/day and a less negative net R than the named setup, yet the note names ALL|SWH or ALL|FC. Examples: DOGE HI 1.21/day -0.061 vs ALL|SWH -0.110; N01_ST_EMA 1.50/day -0.092 vs -0.121; N04_ST_KLINGER 2.85/day -0.070 vs -0.102; N20_EMA9_CHOP 1.43/day -0.084 vs -0.122.

Grades A/B/C (sign of gross R in each half) are at noise level. Example: DOGE gross IS +0.003 / CF +0.016 with SE about 0.014 per half (about 3,750 trades, sd 0.85), t about 0.2 and 1.1. The graded distribution (A 15, B 16, C 15) is close to the 25/50/25 expected if every gross were exactly 0, so the grade should not be read as quality.
Sampled numbers (DOGE, N01_ST_EMA, N02_ST_KST, N20_EMA9_CHOP, OBV_S, S2_ST_ROC, F5_BOX, F11_RAID) reproduce exactly on the overlapping window (v_cmp.py), so no numeric errors were found in the notes.
DeepSeek family notes average 'per def' over definitions that are duplicates (F11_RAID = F11_TSOUP = F13_RAID_PD at 15m, F5_BOX = F5_BOX_HTF, etc.), which double-weights some signal streams.
verifier_missed: Per-trade vs per-day metric: every setup ranking uses mean R per trade. At fixed risk per trade the account result is R per day, and by that measure switching (SWH) is worse than not switching (study's own res: ALL|LTF beats ALL|SWH per day in 25/35 core, 34/44 ds). Hurdle per trade and loss per day should both be reported.
Tie-rule confound: SWH and LTF are run with longer-tf-first ties, FC with BTC-first/shorter-tf-first ties, so 'SWH vs FC' mixes the switch effect with the tie effect.

Coin priority on ties (BTC, ETH, SOL, ...) is not neutral. BTC/ETH have the narrowest stops, so they have the highest cost in R. Random ties improve core A|FC by +0.007 [+0.003,+0.012], ALL|FC by +0.010. A widest-stop-first (lowest cost-in-R) tie rule improves A|FC by +0.014 [+0.009,+0.020] core and +0.019 [+0.010,+0.029] ds, and ALL|SWH by +0.007. This is a free code-level rule for any one-position trader, about half the A-to-C gain.

Feasibility filter changes the trade mix: the ALL/A scopes silently drop the 17% of 1h, 5% of 30m and 76% of 4h signals that 30x/20x cannot size. Those dropped signals are the wide-stop, low-cost-in-R ones (ALLINF|FC -0.127 vs ALL|FC -0.136 per trade). Trading them at lower leverage (e.g. 10x) instead of rejecting them is an untested option that lowers the hurdle.

Leverage headline: 40-50x is not broadly executable on 15m/30m under house rules (15m 50x 7%, 40x 34%; 30m 40x 13%). The owners' '20-50x by AI confidence' would mostly fall back to 20-30x unless sizing changes to risk-per-stop.

Hold-call cost: the design doc's own locked call-reduction rules (one call per bar close, hold wake-ups only on opposite signals, small model for routine checks, $0.015 with caching) are not modelled, so the $/month estimates are an upper-middle range, not a floor.

Overlapping strategies: AI traders on duplicate or near-duplicate definitions would hold the same positions (verify_costs), so pooled CIs across strategies are too narrow and 30 seats are fewer independent experiments than they look.
limits: Rule proxies only: the AI's choices (skip, early exit, switch) are replaced by fixed priority rules; an AI that skips more changes trades/day, blocking and call counts.

Sizing uses the 'normal' chain (30x/30% then 20x/20%) for every signal; the live core run gives ~22% of signals 50x/40x ('best'), which changes ladder R slightly (the ROE ladder locks at smaller price moves at higher leverage).

Stops and ladder checked on 15m bars for all timeframes (live engine uses 1m; the 5-year studies used each tf's own bars). 15m parity with research/strategy_profiles/profiles._scan is exact (3,000 of 3,000 sampled LTC 15m signals to 1e-6); 4h mean R on a 3,000-signal BTC sample is -0.0758R vs -0.0783R on own-tf bars (parity_check.py).
A position frees the trader only after the 15m bar of its exit (conservative by up to 15 minutes); same-moment signals: one taken, the rest counted as 'ties'.
Switching closes the held position at the next 15m open (taker fee + slippage); a new signal on the held coin and side is treated as 'hold'.

Bars are Binance USD-M futures 2021-01..2026-09-29 (scratchpad/binance); 'current' volatility = last 30 days of that data (2026-08-30..09-29) plus the 1.5-day live v4 replay; brackets inferred from live trades, equity $5,000.

MDE and confidence intervals: pooled CIs are week-cluster bootstraps over 2021-2026, but strategies inside a group are correlated (same coins, overlapping signals; several DeepSeek definitions duplicate each other), so group pooled CIs are optimistic; MDE assumes i.i.d. trades.
AI cost uses the design doc's ~$0.03 per Sonnet call; actual cost depends on prompt size and caching.
DeepSeek definitions are run under the house exits (as in paper v4), not their PREREG exits; 'main families' = all 17 families, pooled per family.
N21_ST_RSI_ADX produced no 15m-4h signals in the 5-year window and cannot be evaluated; N14_ICHI_RSI has only a handful of trades in 5 years.

Grades in strategy_notes: A = gross R in the A setup > 0 in both halves, B = in one half, C = in neither, D = under 1 trade/day in the A scope; for DeepSeek families gross per half is approximated by net + whole-window mean cost.

findings.claim: The rule bot's 'margin = leverage % of equity' puts notional at L^2/100 x equity, so one stop-out costs L^2/100 x (stop% + about 0.12%) of the account: 5 to 15% at 20-40x in today's market, and 20x is the only level near the owners' 2-5% band. The 15% max-loss check, not the leverage choice, is what caps it.
findings.evidence: s1_feas.py -> out/s1_feasibility.csv (loss at the stop with fees + exit slippage, size_position formula; parity with paperbot.sizing.size_position 7,200/7,200, t_parity.py). Median loss per stop-out, % equity, 20/30/40/50x: 5y every signal of the 36 locked strategies 2021-08..2026-09 (n 1,140,789 at 15m) 15m 4.5/10.1/18.0/28.1, 30m 6.3/14.1/25.1/39.2, 1h 8.9/20.0/35.6/55.6, 4h 18.0/40.6/72.2/112.8; live (v3b+v4 every submitted signal, 15m n 2,255, stop median 0.61%) 15m 2.9/6.6/11.7/18.3, 30m 3.9/8.8/15.6/24.4, 1h 5.3/12.0/21.3/33.2. Realised live SL exits (s5_live.py -> out/s5_live_stopouts.csv): 15m 30x median -6.8% of equity (n 307, worst -14.9%), 15m 40x -12.1% (n 38), 30m 30x -8.7% (n 175), 1h 30x -10.2% (n 81), 4h 20x -9.7% (n 16). Round-trip taker+slippage (0.14% of notional) = 0.56/1.26/2.24/3.5% of equity per trade at 20/30/40/50x; live median fee+slip 0.9% of equity at 30x, 2.0% at 50x.
findings.implication: The current rule-bot sizing and the '2-5% per stop' alternative are not variants of one rule: the rule bot risks 2-5x more per stop at 30x and 4-9x more at 40-50x. Any AI trader built on 'margin = L%' inherits 7-15% per stop-out.

verification.recomputed: Own formula (no import of common.py) on fy36 stop_frac and on every live signal: margin-rule median loss per stop-out % equity 20/30/40/50x, true pooled median: 5y 15m 4.43/9.97/17.73/27.70, 30m 6.19/13.92/24.74/38.66, 1h 8.78/19.76/35.13/54.89, 4h 17.94/40.36/71.75/112.1; live traded 15m 2.93/6.59/11.72/18.31 (n 2,255). Realised live SL exits (trades_enriched, strategy+ds200): 15m 30x median 6.77% (n 301, worst 14.94%), 15m 40x 12.10% (n 36), 15m 50x 9.00% (n 80, 15% cap binds), 30m 30x 8.79% (n 169), 1h 30x 10.07% (n 78), 4h 20x 10.40% (n 13). Code check: paperbot/config.py V3_QUALITY_TIERS margin_frac = L/100, sizing.py notional = margin x L -> L^2/100 x equity; ladder first lock armed at 12% net ROE = 0.38% price at 50x / 0.74% at 20x (0.62R / 1.21R on a 0.61% stop).
verification.note: Reproduces (their pooled 'median' is a signal-weighted mean of per-coin medians, +0.1-0.4 pt; immaterial). Wording: in today's market 20x costs about 3% (15m) to 5% (1h) per stop, so the range at 20-40x is 3-15%, not 5-15%. v3a live: 4/36 = 11% (not 12.5%) of 15m strategy accounts ended below 50%; 5m 42% final / 47% by hourly minimum. lens2/sizing/verify/v1_feas.py, out/v1_feas.csv, out/v1_live_sl.csv

findings.claim: Which leverage is executable is set by the stop distance, not by the AI. At 50x the liquidation is about 1.6% away, so a 2 ATR stop plus the 1 ATR buffer must be under about 1.07%. Over 5 years 50x fits about half of 15m signals, a quarter of 30m, 8% of 1h and almost no 4h; 20x fits only 20% of 4h signals. Under the margin rule the 15% loss check also blocks most 40-50x trades, and LTC/BCH never get 50x.
findings.evidence: out/s1_feasibility.csv, s1_feasibility_by_year.csv (inferred brackets of analyze.py, live settings: buffer max(1 ATR, 0.2%), max loss 15%). Executable share at exactly 20/30/40/50x, risk rule (2% per stop; only liq buffer + bracket + margin <= equity bind): 5y 15m 98/89/72/52%, 30m 93/72/45/25%, 1h 79/43/19/8%, 4h 20/3.5/0.7/0.15%; live now 15m 100/100/99.6/96%, 30m 100/100/95/67%, 1h 100/98/61/36%, 4h 100/43/0/0% (n 79). Margin rule, all checks: 5y 15m 98/81/36/7%, 30m 92/57/14/2%, 1h 77/27/4/0.4%, 4h 19/1/0/0%; at 50x the 15% check passes only 8.9% of 5y 15m signals. A 'best' signal walking 50->40->30->20 gets 50x 7%, 40x 28%, 30x 45%, 20x 17% (5y 15m). By year (15m, risk rule 50x): 2021 25%, 2022 37%, 2023 66%, 2024 50%, 2025 50%, 2026 70%. By coin (5y 15m, risk rule 50x): BTC 84%, ETH 66%, BCH 48%, LTC 50%, DOGE 31%, SOL 31%; at 5% risk LTC/BCH fall to 30%/28% (bigger notional -> higher mmr bracket). Margin rule at 50x: LTC/BCH 0% (bracket allows 40x above $100k/$50k notional; 50x x 50% of $5,000 = $125k). minNotional: irrelevant at $5,000; exchangeInfo could not be fetched (proxy 403).
findings.implication: 'Confidence -> 50x' cannot be honoured on most 30m/1h signals or in any volatile week; the code, not the AI, must choose the leverage from the stop. '4h only where 20x is executable' means about one 4h signal in five over 5 years (all of them in today's quiet market).

verification.recomputed: 5y shares reproduce exactly with my own liquidation/feasibility code: risk 2% 20/30/40/50x 15m 97.8/89.3/72.3/51.5, 30m 92.8/72.0/45.0/25.1, 1h 78.7/42.6/19.2/8.3, 4h 20.2/3.5/0.7/0.15; margin rule 15m 97.6/81.2/35.8/7.4, 4h 19.3/1.1/0/0; repo size_position (fy36 v4n, example brackets) 15m 30x 81.1%, 4h sized 19.7%. By coin/year (15m 50x) identical (BTC 84.1, ETH 66.1, SOL 30.5, DOGE 30.6, LTC 49.7/30.0 at r5, BCH 47.6/27.6; 2021 25.1 ... 2026 70.4); margin 50x LTC/BCH 0%. LIVE 4h is wrong: s1 used only replay rows with stop_frac, i.e. the 79 TRADED 4h signals, dropping 98 REJECTED_SIZING and 30 UNRESOLVED. Recomputing stop_frac from atr/ref_price for all 207 live 4h signals (recompute matches recorded stop_frac to 3e-16): risk 2% 20x 58.0%, 30x 17.4%, 40/50x 0%; margin 20x 52.7%. Live 1h with unresolved included: 20/30/40/50x 100/95.6/57.1/32.7 (claimed 100/98/61/36).
verification.note: Mechanics and 5y numbers confirmed; the live 4h '100% at 20x (n 79)' is a selection artefact and the implication '4h where 20x fits = all 4h signals in today's quiet market' is false: about 4 in 10 live 4h signals cannot take 20x even now (consistent with lens2_multi_tf MT7: 49%/46% of live 4h signals sized). Consistent with verify_costs: 47% of 5y 4h signals have the 2 ATR stop beyond the 20x (risk-rule) liquidation distance, so entering 4h at 20x without the per-signal check would liquidate many of them (verify_costs 8.1% of all 4h signals liquidated first); the per-signal buffer check in Z2 excludes all of them. lens2/sizing/verify/v1_feas.py

findings.claim: At the same stop and the same risk per stop, the leverage changes almost nothing about expected R. It changes the margin posted, the liquidation distance and, through the ROE-based ladder, the shape of the exits: more small wins and smaller losses at 50x, larger wins at 20x. It does not change fees per unit of risk.
findings.evidence: s2_rerun.py (profiles._scan at fixed 10/20/30/40/50x; parity with lens/fiveyear fy36 v4n R at 30x/20x max abs diff 0.0) -> s2b_levR.py -> out/s2b_lev_R.csv, signals executable at 20x, paired, week-cluster bootstrap. 15m (n 1,115,360): mean R 20x -0.172, 30x -0.171, 40x -0.171, 50x -0.169 (50x-20x +0.003 [-0.001, +0.007]); cost 0.174R vs 0.170R; win rate 52% -> 57%, mean win +0.69R -> +0.38R, mean loss -1.12R -> -0.91R. 30m (n 531,987): -0.125 -> -0.118 (+0.007 [+0.003, +0.011]). 1h (n 226,400): -0.092 -> -0.080 (+0.012 [+0.006, +0.017]). 4h (n 14,127): -0.053 -> -0.035 (+0.018 [+0.005, +0.032]). Isolated margin under the risk rule is r/(L x (stop+cost)): 5y 15m median 3.7% of equity at 50x vs 9.2% at 20x (r = 2%), which caps a gap loss. Liquidation distance is about 1/L - mmr (BTC 50x 1.6%, 20x 4.6%). No gap liquidation in any executable 5y trade under the risk rule (s3_sequences.csv liq_gaps 0). The live d3 'lev10 +0.26R' what-if is not reproduced: 5y 10x vs 20x at 15m +0.004R [-0.003, +0.011].
findings.confidence: high for mean R and costs; medium for tail (no mark-price or 1m data)
findings.implication: With risk-per-stop sizing, 20-50x is mostly a margin and liquidation setting. Higher leverage posts less margin, so it slightly lowers the worst-case loss as long as the stop sits inside the liquidation buffer. If the exits are written in R or price terms instead of ROE, leverage stops changing the exits.

verification.recomputed: Independent paired data (lens/fiveyear fy36: same signals at old tier-walk leverage vs v4n 30x, week-cluster bootstrap): 15m 40x-30x +0.0008R [-0.0023,+0.0040] (n 186,345), 50x-30x -0.0038 [-0.0122,+0.0043] (n 220,773); 30m 40x-30x -0.0009, 50x-30x -0.0096 [-0.031,+0.007]; 1h 40x-30x -0.0146 [-0.0275,-0.0022] (n 6,734). Win rate higher at higher leverage (15m 50x 48.0% vs 30x 42.5%). Holding time on the same 15m signals: 50x 10.98 bars vs 30x 13.89; 40x 8.85 vs 10.33. No liquidation exits (reason 2) in the v4n-executable 5y set (15m, 4h).
verification.note: Core claim holds (|dR| <= 0.015R). The small positive 50x-20x effect they report is not robust in sign (my 1h 40x vs 30x is significantly negative). Missed consequence: under the ROE ladder higher leverage shortens holds by ~20%, so a one-position trader takes more trades per day and pays more cost per day (see Z9). lev10 claim not checked (no independent 10x data): unverifiable here. lens2/sizing/verify/v2_levR.py

findings.claim: Under the current margin = L% rule, a one-position 15m+30m trader without proven edge most likely loses half its account by 12/31 at any leverage 20-50x. Even at zero net edge the chance of falling below 50% is 23% at 20x and 55-71% at 30-50x.
findings.evidence: s3_traders.py -> out/s3_paths.csv, s6_summary.py -> out/s6_paths_summary.csv. 34 strategies (35 in the cache, N21 has no signals, one strategy < 30 trades), one position across six coins, every executable signal (median 3.8-4.3 trades/day at 15m+30m), outcomes = 5y house exit at the leverage used, 1,000 paths of circular 7-day blocks of 1,886 days. Mean over strategies of P(equity < 50% at any trade) to 12/31 (76 days), M20/M30/M40/M50: edge = -cost 83/90/91/91% (median end x0.14/0.013/0.004/0.003); edge 0 net 23/55/68/71%; edge +0.1R 1.0/8.3/16.6/19.7%. One month (30 days): -cost 58/81/84/85%, 0 net 9.5/36/48/52%, +0.1R 0.6/6.4/13/16%. P(< 25%) to 12/31 at 0 net: 4/30/46/51%. 1h alone (about 0.9 trades/day) at 0 net: 18/30/32/32%. Live check: v3a (2.6 days, mostly 50x / 40% margin) 12.5% of 15m and 47% of 5m strategy accounts ended below 50% (out_real/account_stats.csv).
findings.confidence: high (direction and size); exact percentages depend on the bootstrap and the imposed edges
findings.implication: Do not give AI traders the rule bot's margin = L% sizing. Even a real +0.1R edge would carry a 1-in-12 (30x) to 1-in-5 (50x) chance of halving the account before 12/31.

verification.recomputed: Own sequences from fy36 (not their lev pickles), random tie-break, stationary day bootstrap (geometric blocks, mean 10 days; trades on entry day; zero-trade days kept; 2,000 paths), 34 strategies, 15m+30m, mean P(equity<50%) to 76 days, margin 20/30/40/50x: edge -cost 83.8/89.8/91.0/91.2%; 0 net 21.6/56.2/69.1/71.5%; +0.1R 0.5/8.5/18.7/21.8%. 30 days: -cost 60.8/80.2/83.4/83.8, 0 net 8.7/36.1/48.7/51.3, +0.1R 0.3/6.4/14.1/16.9. P(<25%) 0 net 3.7/30.6/47.8/51.5. 1h alone 0 net 17.9/30.1/32.1/32.2. Block length: M30 0 net 56.1/56.2/56.6% for mean block 1/10/28 days. Edge scenarios checked in s3 code: net0 = R - mean R, mcost = R - mean gross R (net mean = -own cost), plus01 = net0 + 0.1, applied per strategy sequence; correct.
verification.note: Reproduces within 2 points with a different bootstrap, data path and tie-break; insensitive to block length (the result is drift, not clustering). Trades/day 4.23 median (theirs 4.2-4.3). lens2/sizing/verify/v3_ruin.py, out/v3_paths.csv

findings.claim: With risk-per-stop sizing, ruin depends on edge x frequency, not on leverage. At zero net edge, 1-2% per stop is safe to 12/31 and 5% is not. If the edge is only what the rules show (gross 0, net -cost), 2% per stop loses half the account by 12/31 in about 65% of 15m+30m paths, and even 1% ends near x0.66.
findings.evidence: out/s6_paths_summary.csv, policy K30 (requested 30x, walk down to 20x), 15m+30m, mean over 34 strategies, 76 days: r = 1/2/3/5%: edge -cost P(<50%) 20/65/78/85% (median end x0.66/0.43/0.27/0.10), P(<25%) 0/22/50/75%; edge 0 net 0/2.2/11/33% (P(<25%) 0/0/0.5/8.3%); edge +0.1R 0/0/0.1/1.6% (median end x1.35/1.78/2.31/3.67). One month: -cost 0/12/37/66%, 0 net 0/0.1/1.8/13.5%. Requested 50x instead of 30x changes P(<50%) at r 2%, 0 net from 2.2% to 1.7% (15m+30m), i.e. leverage does not matter. Thinned to about 2 trades/day (same 28 high-frequency strategies, s7_thin.py -> out/s7_thin_vs_full.csv), edge -cost r 2%: 7.5% vs 79% for the full sequence; r 3%: 45% vs 94%. 1h: -cost r2 0.6%, r5 28%; 4h ~0%.
findings.implication: Pick risk from the evidence on edge, not from the leverage wish. Today's evidence (cost lens: 15m/30m gross edge about 0, cost 0.16-0.24R per trade) supports 1% per stop at most. 2% is defensible only with fewer trades (the AI skipping) or a measured positive edge, and 5% is not defensible.

verification.recomputed: Risk rule 15m+30m, 76 days, r 1/2/3/5%: -cost 15.6/63.6/77.5/84.7% (median end x0.66/0.43/0.27/0.10); 0 net 0/2.2/11.1/33.2%; +0.1R 0/0/0.1/2.0%; 30 days -cost 0/9.5/34.4/64.2%. Proper thinning (signals skipped BEFORE the one-position pass, p tuned to 2.0 trades/day, 28 strategies): -cost r2 8.8% (theirs 7.5%), r3 47.6% (45%). 1h -cost r2 0.5%, r5 26.9%; 4h 0%.
