Scaling each trade's cost by that factor: -cost r1 45.6% ruin (median x0.53), r2 78.7% (x0.28).
verification.note: The 5y-based table reproduces, but it uses 5-year costs per R. In the market the AI will trade (10/17-12/31, quiet, 15m stop ~0.6%) cost per trade in R is ~1.5x higher, so with the rules' zero gross edge even 1% per stop halves the account in ~46% of paths, not 16-20%. 1% is still the right ceiling, but 'safe at 1%' needs a real edge >= today's cost (0.23R at 15m). Frequency was kept at the 5y level in this sensitivity. lens2/sizing/verify/v3b_livecost.py

findings.claim: Without an edge, the loss comes from steady cost drag, not from bad luck. Expected loss per day = trades/day x cost (in R) x risk per stop. Sizing chooses how fast a cost-negative trader bleeds; no sizing makes it safe.
findings.evidence: s3_sequences.csv / s6_sequences_summary.csv: 15m+30m K30 median 4.3 trades/day, mean cost 0.15R -> 0.64R per day; at r 1% that is -0.64% per day, x0.62 over 76 days compounded (bootstrap median x0.66). 15m alone 3.6 trades/day x 0.166R; 30m 2.0 x 0.119R; 1h 0.93 x 0.091R; 4h 0.14 x 0.071R. Per-strategy drag in strategy_notes (0.0-0.9R/day).
findings.implication: An AI trader at 15m needs to add more than the cost (0.15-0.17R per trade) before any size above 1% makes sense. The sizing decision should come after a positive R-based track record, and the trader should be scored in R, not in $ or ROE.

verification.recomputed: Own K sequence 15m+30m: 4.25 trades/day, mean cost 0.144R -> 0.61R/day; r 1% -cost bootstrap median end x0.658 (theirs x0.66). Live cost_all_R medians: 15m 0.225-0.233R (v3a/v4), 30m 0.143-0.165R, 1h 0.08-0.12R, 4h 0.055-0.067R.
verification.note: Mechanism and 5y arithmetic confirmed. The implication's hurdle '0.15-0.17R per trade at 15m' is the 5-year figure; at today's stops the 15m hurdle is ~0.23R (30m ~0.16R), consistent with verify_costs ('5y median requirement is 35-40% lower than today').

findings.claim: On the crash days, risk-per-stop sizing loses a few percent, while the margin rule loses tens of percent and a single slipped stop can take the whole 30-40% margin.
findings.evidence: s4_crash.py -> out/s4_crash_summary.csv, s4_crash_traders_agg.csv, s4_crash_market.csv. Every signal of the 36 entered on the day or the 24 h before; nominal = engine fill, pessimistic = worst 5m print after the stop is crossed (upper bound). 2025-10-10 15m (n 1,156 at 20x): worst trade R -1.33 nominal / -3.98 pessimistic; worst single trade % equity: risk 2% at 20x -2.1% / -6.8%, at 50x -2.0% / -4.7%; margin 30x -15% / -30% (whole margin), 40x -15% / -40%. One-position traders over the 48 h (32 strategies, 15m): risk 2% worst -12% / -23%; margin 30x worst -48% / -85%, 35% of traders lose >= 25% (pessimistic). 2022-11-08 15m: risk 2% worst -7% / -12%; margin 30x worst -46% / -69%, 21% lose >= 25%. 2022-06-13 15m margin 20x worst -37% / -50%. 2024-08-05 30m margin 20x worst -49% / -61%. 2021-05-19 (before the 5y window; cache bars from 2021-01): ATR was so large that the margin rule fell to 20x (M30 traded 5 signals). Market: 2025-10-10 DOGE day low -66%, LTC -59% vs the open, largest 15m bar 22-23 ATR; 2021-05-19 ETH/DOGE/BCH -59 to -69%.
findings.confidence: medium (no 1m / mark-price data; pessimistic fills are a bound, nominal fills are optimistic)
findings.implication: Size so that a 3-4R slipped stop is survivable: at 1-2% risk that is a 4-8% hit. Prefer the highest leverage at which the stop still fits, because isolated margin then caps a disaster gap (r/L of notional).

verification.recomputed: Own crash check from fy36 v4n outcomes + own pessimistic fill (first 5m bar crossing the stop, its extreme; binance/signals bars). 2025-10-10 15m (n 1,156): worst R -1.33 nominal / -3.97 pessimistic; worst single trade risk 2% -2.1/-6.8%, margin 30x -15.0/-30.0% (exact match). One-position 48 h traders (32 strategies, random tie-break): risk 2% worst -14.8/-22.4%; margin 30x worst COMPOUNDED -55.3/-75.9%, SUMMED -70.6/-121.7%; share losing >=25% (pess.) 38%. 2022-11-08 15m: margin 30x compounded -37.0/-52.4% (summed -38.7/-61.8) vs claimed -46/-69; risk 2% -8.2/-10.4% vs claimed -7/-12. 2024-08-05 30m margin 30x -34.6/-44.8%. Market: Binance futures 5m bars confirm 2025-10-10 DOGE low -66.2%, LTC -59.0% vs day open, 2021-05-19 ETH -58.5%, DOGE -58.9%, BCH -68.6%.
verification.note: Direction confirmed (risk sizing loses single digits to ~20%, margin rule tens of %). Per-trade numbers reproduce exactly, but the 48 h trader figures in s4 are SUMS of per-trade equity fractions, not compounded equity: they can exceed -100% (my sum -122%) and overstate the margin-rule loss (-85% summed vs -62 to -76% compounded). Worst-trader values also depend on the greedy tie-break (coin order vs random), e.g. 2022-11-08 15m -46% vs -37%. Report compounded ranges. lens2/sizing/verify/v4_crash.py

findings.claim: 'Confidence -> risk %' is the better design, and only if confidence carries information. 'Confidence -> leverage' does nothing at a fixed risk per stop. Under the margin rule it scales risk with L^2 (6.25x from 20x to 50x) and does worse than flat 30x when confidence is uninformative.
findings.evidence: s3_traders.py confidence(): K30 trade sequences, same exits for every design, confidence 1-5 uniform per trade; null = independent of the outcome, info = E[R|c] shifted 0.05R per level (c5 +0.1R, c1 -0.1R, mean unchanged). out/s6_confidence_summary.csv, 15m+30m, 76 days, mean over 34 strategies, P(<50%) / median end: edge 0 net, null: margin 20-50x by confidence 64% / x0.58 vs flat 30x 55% / x0.77; risk 2-5% by confidence 18.6% / x0.94 vs flat 3.5% 16.7% / x0.94 vs flat 2% 2.2% / x0.99. info: risk 2-5% 9.9% / x1.18 vs flat 3.5% 16.9% / x0.94; margin 20-50x 54% / x0.97. edge -cost, null: risk 2-5% 81% vs flat 2% 65%; margin 20-50x 91%. edge +0.1R: risk 2-5% info 0.1% / x3.3, margin 20-50x info 9.6% / x18 (gamble).
findings.confidence: medium (the confidence model is synthetic; there is no AI confidence data yet)
findings.implication: Map confidence to a narrow risk band, never to leverage under margin = L%. Use flat risk until the trader's own confidence-vs-R record shows it is informative (for example Spearman > 0 over 200+ trades in the shadow account). With uninformative confidence a 2-5% band behaves like a flat 3.5%, which is too much at zero edge.

verification.recomputed: Own synthetic test on own K sequences (conf 1-5 uniform per trade; same maps 2/2.75/3.5/4.25/5% and 20/27/35/42/50x with feasibility walk-down), 76 days, mean P(<50%): NULL, 0 net: margin conf 63.8% (median x0.56) vs flat 30x 56.3% (x0.74) vs flat 35x 67.5% (x0.47); risk conf 2-5% 18.2% vs flat 3.5% 16.8% vs flat 2% 2.2%. NULL -cost: risk conf 80.0% vs flat 2% 63.6%; margin conf 90.4%. INFO (+0.05R/level): risk conf 9.9% vs flat 3.5% 16.9%; margin conf 54.5% vs flat 30x 56.4%. Mean L^2 actually used: conf 836, flat 30x 756, flat 35x 947.
verification.note: Numbers reproduce, but 'confidence -> leverage does worse than flat 30x when confidence is uninformative' is confounded: the 20-50x map has a higher average risk (mean L^2 836 vs 756). Against a flat leverage of the same nominal average (35x) the confidence map is better (63.8% vs 67.5%). Under the null, ruin is simply ordered by mean L^2 (margin rule) or mean r (risk rule); the confidence map adds only the small variance penalty (18.2 vs 16.8%). The real reasons not to map confidence to leverage are that it scales risk with L^2 under margin = L% and does nothing at fixed risk; the 'info' benefit is an assumed 0.05R/level, not a measurement. lens2/sizing/verify/v3_ruin.py confidence(), out/v3_conf.csv

findings.claim: Recommended rule: risk per stop decides size, and leverage is chosen by code as the highest of 50/40/30/20x at which the stop sits inside the liquidation buffer. This keeps the owners' 20-50x on every trade where it is safe and makes the leverage harmless.
findings.evidence: Z1-Z8. Under this rule, at 1% per stop the 5y one-position 15m+30m trader has P(<50%) to 12/31 of 0% at 0 net edge and 20% if the edge is only -cost (median x0.66); at 2% it is 2.2% and 65%. Leverage choice (K20 vs K50) moves these by up to about 9 points (-cost, r 2%: 60% vs 69%), only because more signals become executable at 50x (3.8 vs 4.6 trades/day), not because a single trade loses more.
findings.confidence: medium-high (mechanics high; ruin numbers depend on the edge the AI actually adds)
findings.implication: See report_section_md for the concrete rule. Evidence level: arithmetic and executability high (5y + live, exact parity with the repo's sizing); ruin by bootstrap medium; benefit of confidence scaling unknown until measured.

verification.recomputed: Their s3_sequences.csv (15m+30m): K20 3.84, K30 4.28, K40 4.49, K50 4.60 trades/day on the same signal set. Under the risk rule a signal executable at 50x is always executable at 20x (liquidation farther away; margin r x E/(lpn x 20) < E for any r <= 5% and stop > 0.13%), so the extra trades cannot come from 'more signals becoming executable'. On the same 15m signals the ROE ladder exits sooner at higher leverage (held 10.98 bars at 50x vs 13.89 at 30x), which frees the single position slot for more signals. Rule numbers at r 1%: 0 net 0%, -cost 15.6% (5y cost) / 45.6% (today's cost).
verification.note: The recommended rule is sound in mechanics, but (a) the stated reason K20 vs K50 differs is wrong: it is the ROE ladder shortening holds at high leverage (+20% trades/day, so +20% cost drag per day), which is another reason for exits in R; (b) at today's cost the 1% ruin under 'edge = -cost' is ~46%, not 20%; (c) paperbot/policy.py already contains RecommendedPolicy (risk 1% per stop, 2R default TP, guards 3% daily loss / 5 losses -> 24 h cooldown) but it picks the LOWEST whole leverage whose margin fits, caps at 10x and uses a 3 ATR buffer, i.e. the opposite leverage choice; the owners must pick one and the AI-trader code should reuse that class rather than a third sizing path.

findings.claim: Brackets and liquidation used here are the ones analyze.py inferred from the live trades. They fit every live liquidation price exactly, but they only cover the notional sizes actually traded.
findings.evidence: analyze.py INFERRED_BRACKETS, out_real/brackets_check.csv (1,980 trades without funding, max rel err 1.2e-15): BTC/ETH mmr 0.4% flat; SOL 0.5% to $50k then 0.65%; DOGE 0.65% to $80k then 1%; BCH 0.5/1/1.25% at $10k/$100k with 40x above $100k; LTC 0.5/1/1.5% at $10k/$50k with 40x above $50k. Risk-rule notionals (about 2-5x equity) stay in the low tiers; margin-rule notionals at 40-50x ($80-125k on $5,000) hit the 40x caps. Binance exchangeInfo / leverageBracket could not be read here (proxy 403).
findings.confidence: high for the paper accounts; medium for a real account
findings.implication: Before real money, load the account's real leverageBracket and minNotional (paperbot/binance.py already does) and rerun s1_feas.py with them.

verification.recomputed: Own liquidation formula with the inferred table reproduces all 1,980 live liq prices without funding (max rel err 1.2e-15). Own least-squares fit per coin (y = WB - side Q (EP-LP) = mmr Q LP - cum): DOGE 0.649% to $80k then 0.998% cum 279; LTC 0.9985% cum 49 to $50k then 1.4998% cum 300; SOL 0.497% to ~$49k then 0.650% cum 74; BTC/ETH ~0.40% flat. Rejection texts: BCHUSDT 50x 'bracket allows 40x' 81x, LTCUSDT 50x 'allows 40x' 286x and 'allows 25x' 2x.
verification.note: Confirmed for the notionals traded. Not identified by live trades: the 0.5% tier below $10k for BCH/LTC (smallest live notional $13.7k; implied only through cum continuity) and the mmr of BCH/LTC top tiers. LTC has a further 25x cap at a higher notional that is not in the table (matters only for margin-rule notionals above ~$250k, i.e. grown equity). For small real-money accounts the binding constraints will be qty step and minNotional, not brackets.

strategy_note_problems: Hurdle 'needs >= 0.13-0.17R/trade of AI-added edge just to break even' in every 15m+30m note uses the 5-year cost; at today's stops the cost is ~1.5x (live cost_all_R 0.23R at 15m, 0.16R at 30m), so the hurdle is ~0.2R for most cells.

r1 '-cost' ruin for the 7-9 trades/day strategies is threshold-sensitive and not reproduced closely: N17_KC_RSI 0.61 vs 0.37 (mine), N18_VWMA_MACD 0.62 vs 0.43, N10_HA_PSAR 0.54 vs 0.38, N04_ST_KLINGER 0.78 vs 0.64, S2_ST_ROC 0.66 vs 0.54. r2, 0-net and margin-30x columns reproduce within 0.06 for all 34 (trades/day within 0.5, mean R within 0.02; N04 trades/day 8.74 vs 8.23).

'cost-drag low' for N15_KC_AO (0.06 trades/day), S1_EMA_RSI_CHOP (0.09), N11_BREAKAWAY (0.40), N03_ADX_GC (0.72) reflects inactivity (about 5-55 trades by 12/31), not quality; the grade reads as favourable and should say 'too few trades to judge'.
Notes give no per-strategy share of signals that can take >= 20x at 1h/4h, although that is what the owners' 4h rule needs (5y 4h at 20x: BTC 55%, ETH 25%, LTC 17%, BCH 11%, DOGE 8%, SOL 4%).

Notes repeat 'bootstrap (7-day blocks)' as the only uncertainty; the bigger uncertainty is the cost level (5y vs today) and the imposed edge, not the block length (mean block 1/10/28 days changes ruin by < 1 point).
verifier_missed: Live 4h executability excluded the 98 REJECTED_SIZING (and 30 unresolved) 4h signals; with all 207 live 4h signals only 58% fit 20x under the risk rule (53% margin rule), 17% fit 30x.
Today's cost per trade in R is ~1.5x the 5-year level (narrow stops); the -cost ruin at r 1% rises from ~16-20% to ~46%, r 2% to ~79%.

Under the house ROE ladder leverage changes holding time (50x exits ~20% sooner), hence trades/day and cost drag per day for a one-position trader; this, not executability, drives the K20/K50 difference.

paperbot/policy.py RecommendedPolicy already implements risk-per-stop sizing (1%, max 10x, lowest leverage that fits, 3 ATR buffer, R take-profit, daily-loss / losing-streak guards). The study's rule (highest 50/40/30/20x, 1 ATR buffer) contradicts it on leverage and buffer; neither was reconciled.
Crash-day 48 h trader losses are sums, not compounded equity (can exceed -100%).
Confidence -> leverage null comparison is confounded by a higher mean leverage; compare at equal mean risk.

Portfolio level: ruin is computed per trader. Duplicate / overlapping strategies (e.g. F11_RAID = F11_TSOUP = F13_RAID_PD, N-strategy overlaps) would make several AI traders hold the same position, so 1% each can be 3-5% on one event for the owners' total book; a cross-trader exposure cap per coin/direction is not discussed.

Mark-price liquidation and the liquidation clearance fee are not modelled; with stops 1 ATR inside liquidation at 50x a fast wick can fill the stop-market near the liquidation price (pessimistic crash fills reached -3 to -4R).
Small real-money accounts: qty steps (BTC 0.001 ~ $86-120) and minNotional will bind before brackets at r 1% on a few hundred dollars; the rule needs a 'skip if rounding changes risk by > x%' check.
Kill switch / daily loss cap was not simulated although the repo's RecommendedSettings already define 3% daily loss and 5-loss cooldown values.
limits: Trade outcomes are the house exit (2 ATR stop + ROE ladder) on every executable signal, taken one position at a time. The AI will skip, exit early and switch timeframes, so its frequency and outcome shape will differ. The thin2 variant (about 2 trades/day) brackets the frequency effect.

Edge scenarios shift every trade's R by a constant (net0: R - mean; -cost: gross R demeaned minus the trade's own cost; +0.1R). This keeps the 5-year shape and does not model an edge that changes win rate or tails.

The bootstrap uses circular 7-day blocks of 1,886 calendar days (2021-08-01..2026-09-30). Regimes longer than a week are only partly kept, and the 34 strategies' ruin probabilities are not independent (same coins, same days). Ruin is checked at every trade. Drawdown peaks are taken at day starts, so intraday peaks are missed (max drawdown is slightly understated).

The 5-year engine fills stops at the stop price unless a bar opens through it (optimistic in wicks) and uses trade price, not mark price, for liquidation. The crash-day pessimistic fill (worst 5m print) is an upper bound. No 1m data and no order-book depth for 2021-2025 crashes, and no exchange outages or API failures are modelled.
2021-05-19 is before the 5-year window and is replayed from the cache's earlier bars (signals warm up from 2021-01). 2022-11-08/09 are treated as two UTC days.

Brackets are inferred from the live trades (exact there). minNotional and lot steps for real money could not be fetched (exchangeInfo proxy 403); qty steps were inferred from the live trades (BTC 0.001 = about $86).
The confidence experiment is synthetic. There is no AI confidence data yet. 'info' assumes a linear 0.05R per level, which is an assumption and not a measurement.
Fixed-fraction compounding with no daily loss cap or drawdown kill switch was simulated. A kill switch would cap ruin by construction but not change the expected drift.
Funding is 0.01% per 8 h paid by both sides, as in the research. The live quiet market (15m stop median 0.61%) is narrower than the 5-year median (0.99%), so live executability is the optimistic end.

findings.claim: Signal rates are high and stable: the 36 strategies on the 6 tradable coins submit about 570 (15m), 290 (30m), 190 (1h) and 40 (4h) signals a day live, the same as the 5-year rebuild; DeepSeek 44 adds about 780 / 410 / 245 / 84.
findings.implication: Raw signal counts are not the cost driver once a trader holds one position at a time; per-trader call counts are.

verification.recomputed: Raw signal_log, SUBMITTED, 6 tradable coins (v_rates.py -> rates_mine.csv): core v3b (0.698 d) 15m 560.5 / 30m 288.1 / 1h 167.7 / 4h 24.4 per day; v4 (1.503 d) 572.7 / 291.3 / 192.2 / 42.6; DeepSeek v4 779.5 / 412.4 / 244.8 / 83.8; per-strategy bar-close bundles v4 core 398 / 197 / 126 / 28. 5-year per-strategy rates from the multi_tf outcome masks match the analyst's y5 notes cell by cell (134 cells, median ratio 1.000).
verification.note: Exact reproduction. 'Same as the 5-year rebuild' holds for 15m/30m; live 1h runs +26% (v4) and 4h ranges -35% (v3b) to +16% (v4) against 5y. That spread doesn't matter for cost, because one position at a time caps calls.

findings.claim: One position at a time caps entry calls at about 4-5 per trader-day (5y median), but a trader is in a position 43-54% of the time (5y) or 53-73% (live, quiet market), so most calls are holding checks and switch decisions.
findings.evidence: live_vs_5y.csv: 5y median entry calls A 4.6, trades 4.6, occupancy A 0.43 / B 0.54; live v4 ours occupancy A 0.6 / B 0.72, ds200 A 0.64
findings.implication: Budget by holding-check policy first, not by signal counts.

verification.recomputed: Own one-position simulations. 5y (v_5y.py: house exits checked on 15m bars, 20x/30x sizing feasibility, 2021-08..2026-09, core, 32 non-rare strategies, medians): entry calls 4.51/trader-day (A) and 4.52 (B); occupancy A 0.47, B 0.55 (0.59 without the sizing filter). Live replay (v_live.py; validated replay exits, 1m bars): occupancy core v3b A 0.52 / B 0.57, v4 A 0.58 / B 0.73, DeepSeek v4 A 0.65 / B 0.68; entry calls 4.0-7.2.
verification.note: Within 0.04 of the analyst on every cell. Means across strategies are lower than medians (v4 core A mean occupancy 0.51).

findings.claim: Per-trader calls/day (median strategy, setup A, AI enters every signal): switch mode 24-39 (5y) / 28-60 (live, ours and DeepSeek) depending on the holding policy; ignore mode 20-38 (5y) / 19-58 (live). P4 (30-minute checks + events, the PLAN_ATTACH draft) is the most expensive: about 39 (5y) and 49-60 (live) calls per trader-day.
findings.implication: Live (quiet market) runs ~15-50% above the 5-year emulation because positions last longer when ATR is small (the ROE ladder needs a larger move in ATR terms). Plan with the live numbers as the upper case.

verification.note: Levels agree within about 10% (my P3 is 10-16% lower because I reset the move reference to the trigger bar's close). P4 is the most expensive policy in both. Correction to the implication: live runs above 5y by +16% (P4) to +29% (P2), but P3 runs about the same live as 5y (17.3 vs 17.6; the analyst's own figures are 18.8 vs 19.8). So '15-50% above' does not hold for event-only checks.

findings.claim: A '>= 0.5R move' trigger is not rare: on 15m positions it fires about 1.8 times per hour held (1m bars), almost as often as a 15m bar-close check; 1.0R fires 0.46 per hour (-74%).
findings.evidence: move_threshold.csv (live replay, 2255 15m trades): per hour 0.5R 1.78, 0.75R 0.81, 1.0R 0.46; 30m 0.5R 0.88, 1h 0.43, 4h 0.13
findings.implication: Use 1.0R (or 1 ATR of the held tf with a 15-minute cooldown) for event wakes, or route move wakes to Haiku.

verification.recomputed: Same 2,255 15m replay trades / 5,037.6 h held (v_move.py, 1m bars): 0.5R 1.53/h (reference reset to the bar close) or 1.58/h (reference stepped by k*R); 0.75R 0.71/h; 1.0R 0.40-0.41/h (-74%); 0.5R with a 15-minute cooldown 1.16/h. 30m 0.74-0.79/h, 1h 0.36-0.38/h, 4h 0.11-0.12/h.
verification.note: Same conclusion. Absolute rates are 10-15% below the analyst's 1.78/h, which depends on how the reference price resets. A 15-minute cooldown alone cuts 0.5R wakes by about 25%.

findings.claim: A realistic screen is about 13.5-14.5k characters: about 6.2-6.6k tokens with Korean labels (range 5.1-7.3k) and 5.1-5.4k with English keys (4.5-6.2k). The cacheable prefix (instructions + market bundle) is about 5.0k of 6.3k Korean tokens (~80%); the variable part (card + journal + wake) is about 1.1-1.4k.
findings.evidence: outscreens/screens_measure.json: S1 KO total mid 6359 (low 5187, high 6991; instr 1407, market 3651, card 797, journal 240, wake 259); S1 EN 5226; S2 (5-signal bundle) KO 6640; S3 hold KO 6201, EN 5112; market bundle EN JSON 3456 vs EN rows 3136
findings.implication: Token counts are estimates (ASCII/3.2 + Hangul x0.95; no tokenizer offline). Measure with usage fields in the pilot. English keys save ~15% input but input is only ~30% of the bill.

verification.recomputed: I rebuilt the market bundle from real Binance 15m bars (last bar 2026-09-29 23:45 UTC; 6 coins x 15m/30m/1h/4h with 8-bar rows, ATR/EMA/RSI/ADX/box/volume profile, plus a real daily line; funding/OI/analyst lines are placeholders of realistic format) and added a 20-line journal (design 6-4 asks for 20, not 10). I estimated tokens with my own heuristic: digit runs ceil(len/3), letter runs 1 per 6 chars, each ASCII symbol 1, newline 1, Hangul 0.7/1.0/1.3 per syllable, other symbols 1.5. Result: total 9,216 tokens mid (range 7,474-11,244); instructions 1,614, market 5,622, card 1,080, journal 586, wake 314. The cacheable share is 78.5%. The same heuristic on the analyst's own KO screen gives 8,870 mid (7,192-10,822) against their 6,359 (5,187-6,991). EN versions come out 17% below KO.
verification.note: The ~80% cacheable share and the ~15% English saving reproduce. The absolute size probably does not: the analyst's ASCII/3.2 chars-per-token rule is optimistic for number-dense rows like '+0.18 -0.08' (realistically 1.5-2.5 chars/token). My heuristic puts the screen about 40% higher. Neither figure is tokenizer-measured. The count_tokens endpoint is free, so the owners can measure the real screens exactly before the pilot without paying for calls.

findings.claim: Output (thinking + answer) dominates the per-call price: a Sonnet entry decision costs about $0.0129 at ~900 output tokens (low $0.0079, high $0.0249); a holding check $0.0067 (low $0.0047, high $0.0117); Opus about 1.9x; Haiku hold $0.0019.
findings.evidence: per_call_costs.json; cached input 5,058 tokens at $0.20/M, uncached ~1.1-1.4k at $2/M, output at $10/M (Sonnet).
findings.implication: Thinking length is the largest unknown (3x range in the total). Fix effort per call type and cap max_tokens; measure output_tokens in the pilot before locking the budget.

verification.recomputed: With the stated inputs (5,058 cached at $0.20/M, 1,435 or 1,137 uncached at $2/M, 900 or 345 output at $10/M) the arithmetic reproduces exactly: Sonnet entry $0.01288, hold $0.00673; Opus $0.02475 / $0.01246; Haiku hold $0.00187; output share 70% / 51%. Prices match the claude-api reference (Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10 with $0.20 cache reads; Opus 5.5 $4/$20 with $0.20 cache reads, i.e. 0.05x; Haiku 4.5 $1/$5; 5-minute cache writes 1.25x). With my token basis: Sonnet entry $0.0144, hold $0.0085; Opus $0.0274 / $0.0157.
verification.note: The per-call prices leave out cache writes. Caches are model-scoped, so Opus twins (and Haiku) need their own market-bundle writes. From live v4 timestamps (v_cache.py), about 34% of Opus twin calls fall on a cold 15-minute version even with pre-warming (89% if same-minute calls fire together). Each write adds 3,651 x ($5.00-$0.20)/M = $0.0175, so the effective Opus entry cost is about $0.031 (2.4x Sonnet, not 1.9x). Thinking length remains the largest unknown.

findings.claim: Reference plan (30 Sonnet traders, setup B, P4 holding checks, switch calls, + 5 Opus twins, Korean, mid thinking) costs about $574/month on 5-year rates and $607/month on live (quiet-market) rates; busy days (p90) about +15%.
findings.evidence: scenarios.csv / scenarios_live_basis.csv: 5y mean 574, p90-day x30 661, p90 30-day window 622, max 30-day window 661; live mean 607, live p90-day x30 699
findings.implication: The draft plan does not fit $500 reliably; it needs one or two cuts.

verification.recomputed: 30 Sonnet + 5 Opus, B, P4, switch, KO, mid thinking (v_scen.py, 100 random 30-sets from 32 non-rare strategies, median): with the analyst's token basis and no Opus writes (their method) on my call counts, 5y $513/month (p90-day x30 $606), live v4 $582. Adding Opus cache writes (pre-warmed): 5y $560, p90-day $653, live $629. With my token basis plus Opus writes: 5y $692, p90-day $801, live $774. Low thinking (300/100): $523; high (2,000/800): $1,103.
verification.note: The direction holds: the draft exceeds $500. The level is $510-$630 on the analyst's token basis and roughly $690-$775 on mine, and unmodelled items add more (see missed). Two framing problems. (1) Neither PLAN_ATTACH 1-3 nor design v2 6-2 wakes the AI for every new signal while holding. The plan wakes on other-timeframe signals of the own strategy; v2 wakes only on held-coin signals. The draft therefore sits between 'ignore' and 'switch', and switch is its upper case. On the analyst's basis with Opus writes, B/P4/ignore is 5y $454, p90-day $517, live $504; on my token basis it is $585, $665, $649. (2) The 'draft = setup B with 4 timeframes' label is wrong. PLAN_ATTACH 1-2 has the AI enter only on 15m/30m (setup A); the owners' 10/7 update says 15m/30m/1h plus 4h where 20x is executable (setup C). With the 20x/30x sizing filter, B and C are identical in my 5y simulation. A costs about 5-7% less than B.

findings.claim: Market activity moves the bill only a little: with one position per trader, calls are bounded by clock time, so the 90th-percentile day is about 1.15x the mean day and the worst 30-day window in five years about 1.14x the mean month (30 traders).
findings.evidence: scenarios.csv: p90_day_x30 / mean_month 1.08-1.21 (median 1.16); max_30d_window / mean_month 1.06-1.21
findings.implication: Set the daily cap at ~1.25x the planned mean; budget risk is in thinking tokens and policy choice, not in volatile markets. A shock day can still exceed the cap for a few hours.

verification.recomputed: Across all 240 scenario rows: p90-day x30 / mean month median 1.166 (range 1.12-1.23); worst 30-day window / mean 1.141 (1.06-1.22).
verification.note: Reproduces. The daily cap at about 1.25x the mean is reasonable.

findings.claim: Combinations that fit $500 including 5 Opus twins under both 5-year and live rates at the p90 day (Korean screen, mid thinking): 10 traders: every setup x policy x mode; 20 traders: every combination in ignore mode, and in switch mode P2 or P3 (P1 only for B/C; P4 fits only on an average month); 30 traders: only ignore mode with P2 (30-minute checks) or P3 (event checks), any setup (P1-ignore and P2/P3-switch fit only on an average month; P4 never).
findings.evidence: fit_500.csv (KO screen, mid thinking, Sonnet holding checks; values = mean / p90-day x30)
findings.implication: With 30 traders, 'ignore new signals while holding' plus either 30-minute checks or event-only checks is the main way to stay under $500; with switch calls, only 10-20 traders fit. If the analyst, coach and re-asks (~$55/month) come out of the same $500, plan the traders at <= ~$445.

verification.recomputed: Requiring p90-day x30 <= $500 and live mean <= $500, with Opus writes. Analyst token basis: 10 traders: all fit. 20: everything except B/P4/switch. 30: A or B with P2/P3 ignore, A/P2-P3 switch, B/P3 switch, B/P1 ignore. My token basis: 10: all fit. 20: only P2/P3 (both modes) and B/P1-ignore; P4-ignore and A/P1-ignore fit only an average month. 30: only P2- or P3-ignore (A or B).
verification.note: The 30-trader conclusion (ignore new signals plus 30-minute or event-only checks) is robust. The 20-trader claim 'every combination in ignore mode fits' fails on the larger token basis (P4-ignore p90 is over $500). And if the analyst, coach and re-asks (~$55) and the server come out of the same $500 cap (PLAN_ATTACH 2-6 says monthly cap 500 for the AI side), 30 traders fit only with event-only checks (P3-ignore: $282-361 p90-day).

findings.claim: What to cut first, by saving per dollar of lost information: (1) the 0.5R move trigger -> 1.0R or Haiku; (2) switch calls while holding (ignore new signals except opposite signals on the held coin); (3) the 30-minute schedule when events are on; (4) Opus twins to 3 or to entry calls only; then thinking caps, then trader count.
findings.evidence: levers.csv: reference: 30 Sonnet + 5 Opus, setup B, P4 (30m + events), switch calls: 574 (saves 0); signals while holding ignored (no switch calls): 465 (saves 108); holding checks only every 30 min (P2): 451 (saves 123); holding checks only on events (P3): 446 (saves 128); P4 with move trigger 1.0R instead of 0.5R (approx.): 483 (saves 91); drop the 5 Opus twins: 453 (saves 120); Haiku first for holding checks (20% escalated): 477 (saves 97); English keys instead of Korean labels: 508 (saves 65); thinking low (entry ~300, hold ~100 tokens): 390 (saves 183); thinking high (entry ~2000, hold ~800 tokens) [cost increase]: 1021 (saves -448); screen 1.5x larger instructions/card/journal [cost increase]: 641 (saves -67); setup A (15m/30m entries only): 542 (saves 31); 20 traders instead of 30: 447 (saves 126); AI skips half the signals (pe 0.5): 510 (saves 63)
findings.implication: Keep 30 traders and the 15m/30m(+1h) entries; cut the holding-check frequency, which the owners' own data says is noise (most move wakes are ordinary 1-ATR wiggles).

verification.recomputed: Savings from the reference (analyst token basis, Opus writes included, 5y mean): ignore switch calls -$106; P2 instead of P4 -$128; P3 -$146; drop the 5 Opus twins -$157 (their share including writes; analyst says $120); 1.0R move trigger instead of 0.5R about -$67 (my 15m-bar counts: B P4-switch 41.6 -> 33.1 calls/trader-day; analyst $91); Haiku 4.5 for holding checks with 20% escalation about -$90 once Haiku's own cache writes (~$14/month) are counted (analyst $97).
verification.note: The individual savings reproduce roughly, but the ranking is a judgment, and the Opus-twin cut is worth more than stated once its cache writes are included. The Haiku lever routes all holding checks to the small model, which contradicts design 6-7: the small model is locked to the 1 ATR move and 70%-point wakes only, and 30-minute checks, opposite signals, releases and funding wakes go to the large model. It also uses Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5). Claude Haiku 5.5 is listed at $0.10/$0.50, 10x cheaper, but its fit for this task is untested.

findings.claim: Letting the AI skip half the signals (pe 0.5) lowers the bill a little (fewer positions to check) rather than raising it.
findings.evidence: scenarios.csv (30 traders, Opus 5): pe 0.5 vs 1.0 mean month e.g. B/P4/switch 510 vs 574
findings.implication: Skip rates within the pilot band (15-85%) do not threaten the budget.

verification.recomputed: 5y, 8 mid-rate strategies, B/P4/switch, AI skips 50% at random (v_pe.py): cost per trader-day ratio pe0.5/pe1 median 0.81 (entry calls go up, trades and holding time go down). Analyst: 510/574 = 0.89.
verification.note: Same direction; my effect is somewhat larger.

strategy_note_problems: Rate notes: the 5-year values match my recount exactly (134 cells). In the live values, 26 of 280 differ by about 0.15%, from day-length rounding (0.7 vs 0.698 days). Negligible.

Setup notes (y5 calls per trader-day): my counts are about 9% lower (switch P4 median ratio 0.91, p10 0.86, p90 0.93) with the same rank order (Spearman 1.00) and occupancy within 0.01. The cause is exits checked on 15m bars plus the sizing filter, against own-timeframe bars and no filter.

Setup B notes include 4h trades the house sizing would reject: 4h 20x is executable on only ~19-26% of bars, mostly BTC (multi_tf MT7). With that filter B equals C, and B occupancy drops from 0.59 to 0.55.

The grade 'heavy' covers 15 of 35 strategies (43%), so it does not single out the expensive ones. My top six by switch-P4 calls are N04_ST_KLINGER, N23_HA_ST, S2_ST_ROC, N22_VORTEX_PSAR, N18_VWMA_MACD, N17_KC_RSI, the same busy list the analyst names.

The 44 DeepSeek notes rest on 1.5 live days only. Their live per-trader calls (switch P4 ~57) run 10-25% above core (45-52), so treating them as drawn from the core distribution understates DeepSeek traders.

The analyst's daily, market-data and analyst lines in the screens are identical placeholders across coins (e.g. ETH shows BTC's daily line). Token size is similar, but the screens are not 'from real data' for those parts.
verifier_missed: Opus twins need their own cache writes (caches are model-scoped). About $46/month with a pre-warm per 15-minute version, about $120/month if same-minute calls fire together (v_cache.py, live v4 timestamps).

Burst cache misses: at each bar close all traders fire at once. Without a max_tokens=0 pre-warm or a stagger, nearly every Sonnet call writes the 3.7k-token market block: about 1,227 writes/day instead of ~125 for 30 traders P4, roughly +$280/month. The PLAN's 20-second answer deadline leaves little room to stagger.

20-second deadline (PLAN_ATTACH 1-2 #5): ~900 output tokens of thinking plus answer, after time-to-first-token on a ~7-9k-token input and 30 simultaneous requests, may often miss 20 s. Late answers are billed and then discarded. The SDK default (timeout plus max_retries=2) can bill a call up to 3 times. max_retries must be set and late answers counted in the budget.

Re-asks, format failures and refusals (design ~$20/month), the hourly market analyst (~$20), coach/night journal (~$15), funding-settlement wakes (~1.6-2.2 calls/trader-day, about +$13/month with twins), 70%-of-stop/target wakes, shock wakes, and 4-hour near-signal scans for flat traders (up to ~2.7 calls/trader-day, about +$30/month if enabled). These are listed by the analyst but left out of the headline, while the PLAN's $500 cap covers all AI cost.

Opus twin definition: design v2 6-2 pairs each twin with a Sonnet trader and wakes it only at that trader's moments, and budgets about $45/month for all five (14-3). The model's five median-rate twins cost about $99-157/month (analyst basis) to about $200 (my basis). If the twins go to busy strategies (up to ~2.4x the median), double that.
Journal length: design 6-4 shows the last 20 decisions; the model used 10 (about +300 uncached tokens per call, roughly +$20/month at 30 traders).

Tokenizer differences: Opus 5.5 may use the newer Opus tokenizer (1-1.35x the tokens of older ones), so Opus input and output token counts may not equal Sonnet's for the same screen. Korean tokenization is unmeasured. All of this can be measured for free with count_tokens before any paid call.

Effort defaults: Sonnet 5.5 defaults to effort high and Opus 5.5 to medium, and thinking cannot be disabled on either (Sonnet only via between_tools). If effort is not pinned per call type, the thinking-token assumption (800/300) is likely too low, and the cost scales roughly linearly with it (low $523, mid $692, high $1,103 on my token basis).

Long-context surcharge: not applicable. Screens are under 12k tokens, and Sonnet/Opus 5.5 bill their 1M context at standard rates. The Batch API 50% discount does not apply to real-time decisions; it applies only to the coach/night journal.
Calendar-month console limits: October will also carry pre-launch replay tests ($45-90 by design 14-3, up to about $210 worst case), and PLAN step 5 pilot calls.

Inconsistency with multi_tf MT9: it prices calls at $0.03 each (design v2 14-1), which gives 30 A traders $714-1,279/month and '$500 covers 12-21 A traders'. The call counts agree (MT9 A 26-47 vs cost model A 24-39 per trader-day), but the per-call price differs about 2-4x, so MT9's dollar figures should be superseded by measured per-call prices.
limits: No tokenizer was available offline and no API was called: token counts are character-based estimates (low/mid/high) using the repo's own conservative rule as the high end. Korean text in particular may tokenize differently on Sonnet 5.5; measure usage.input_tokens / cache_read_input_tokens / output_tokens in the pilot.
Thinking tokens are assumed (entry 300/800/2000, holding 100/300/800 for low/mid/high). They are the largest driver of the bill and are unknown until measured.

Holding times use rule exits (5-year: a house-exit emulation on the trade's own bars at 30x / 20x; live: the validated replay). AI early exits would shorten holds (fewer checks) but add entries; not modelled.

The 5-year emulation gives shorter holds than live (5y median 52-82 min vs live 15m median 92 min) because the ROE ladder triggers sooner when ATR is large; live (quiet market, 2.2 days, holds truncated at run end) is the upper case. Truth for the coming month is likely between.

Live rates rest on 0.7 (v3b) and 1.5 (v4) days; per-strategy live numbers are noisy. DeepSeek traders have live rates only (no 5-year call simulation); they were treated as drawn from the same per-trader distribution (their live per-trader calls are similar to ours).

Scenario trader sets are random draws of 10/20/30 from the 32 non-rare core strategies; the final AI-trader list is not chosen yet. A list of busy strategies (S2_ST_ROC, N04, N23, N22, N18, N17) costs up to ~2.4x the median trader.

Market-bundle caching assumes one shared 15-minute version written about twice per window; the card sits after the market bundle (design 6-4 order), so it is never cached. A per-trader second breakpoint or a different order could change input cost by a few percent only.

Prices are from the owners' design doc (AIBOT_DESIGN_KO_v2 14-3) and the claude-api reference cached 2026-09-25: Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, cache read $0.20; Opus 5.5 $4/$20, cache read $0.20; Haiku 4.5 $1/$5, cache read assumed $0.10, minimum cacheable prefix 4,096 tokens on Haiku. Re-check before launch.

Not included: market analyst (design ~$20/month), coach/night journal (~$15), re-asks and format failures (~$20), the separate server (~$40), pre-launch tests. Macro releases add only ~0.25 calls per trader-day (4 releases / 30 days).
Funding-settlement wakes (design v2: 10 minutes before each 8h settlement while holding) are not in P1-P4; they would add about 3 x occupancy calls per trader-day (~1.5-2).
